# ah-engine reference

This reference is generated from the engine's registries and shipped defaults by `ah-engine docs --format md`; do not edit it by hand. A test fails when it differs from the generated text.

## Commands

Every command accepts `--json`. Read-only commands never change state.

| Command | Arguments | Read-only | Status | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_tick` | `` | no | implemented | The scheduled agent tracker tick (the `agent_tick` job): one tracker tick, the same as `agents tick`; prints its counts with --json. |
| `agents` | `<status\|tick\|wake-watch\|send> [<id>] [--json]` | no | implemented | The agent tracker (feature 21): `status` lists every tracked agent (main sessions, subagents and background tasks, DevSwarm workspaces) with tokens, progress, last output, state and flags, plus today's reminder and recovery totals; `tick` runs one tracker tick now (the scheduled job `agent_tick` does the same every minute); `wake-watch [--auto]` is the Monitor armed at session start that wakes an idle session when the tracker queues a wake row for it. `send <id> [--progress-request\|--ping\|--stop-request\|--text <message>]` puts a reminder in one agent's queue (and wakes it when a watcher is armed) or reads its heartbeat; it is audited. It never stops or kills an agent. |
| `audit` | `entry-paths [--json] [--root <dir>] [--home <dir>] [--no-live]` | yes | implemented | The entry-path audit: `audit entry-paths` inventories every js/sh/wrong-entry leftover in four sections (files of the plugin tree, command strings of hooks.json / defaults / skills / docs, files the engine itself generates into launcher directories, and a read-only look at the running machine: processes, LaunchAgents, crontab, installed hooks.json) against the allowlist in entry_audit.toml. Exit 0 = clean, 1 = findings. `--no-live` skips the machine section (the deploy gate), `--root` names the repository or plugin root, `--home` the home directory. |
| `auto-handover-config` | `<get [--json]\|set <1-99>\|off\|on\|nag on\|off\|nag-step <n>\|nag-quiet <n>\|max-tokens <n>>` | no | implemented | Get or change the auto-handover trigger's settings: `get [--json]` (the resolved values and where the threshold came from), `set <1-99>`, `off`, `on`, `nag on\|off`, `nag-step <n>`, `nag-quiet <n>`, `max-tokens <n>` (0 turns the token ceiling off). It writes through the settings store, one key at a time, like `settings set`. |
| `backup` | `[--to <dir>]` | no | implemented | Make a consistent online snapshot of hot.db and archive.db with SQLite's backup API, scrubbed of secrets, in backups/<ms> or the given directory; prints its manifest. |
| `briefing` | `[--root <plugin dir>]` | yes | implemented | A derived inventory of a plugin tree: every registered hook by event with the purpose from its own header comment, the skills, the DevSwarm substrate and the docs map. |
| `capability-scan` | `[--root <plugin dir>]` | yes | implemented | A read-only gap report: for each opt-in capability of a plugin tree, whether it is shipped and whether it is active on this machine, and how to enable it; prints the JSON report, then one line per capability. |
| `check` | `<name>` | yes | implemented | Run one built-in check in-process on a hook payload from stdin (used by the parity harness). |
| `config` | `[validate <file>\|heal\|set <key> <value> [--check] [--confirmed]\|reset <key> [--confirmed]\|undo <id> [--confirmed]\|apply\|history [--limit <n>] [--key <k>] [--verb <v>]]` | no | implemented | Show the effective config and where each value comes from, validate a config file, or `heal` the plugin's edited defaults (add the settings they lack from the pristine copy, also in a version-controlled checkout); `set` / `reset` write one validated key into the settings.json layer (a registry setting through the settings store, any other shipped key checked against its default's type and bounds; locked keys refused; `set --check` validates only), `undo <id>` restores the value before a history row, `apply` makes a running daemon reload now, and `history` lists the config-history log (every write: ts, who, key, old, new, verb, result); the shipped defaults and the pristine copy are never written. Versions and export are planned (D18, they need the config database). |
| `coordinator-work-baseline` | `<transcript.jsonl> [--from-line <n>] [--cwd <dir>] [--json]` | yes | implemented | Replay a session transcript's main-thread Bash calls through the coordinator-work classifier and window and print what the guard would have done: calls, work, share as recorded, attempted share with enforcement, would-nudge and would-block counts. |
| `ctl` | `<ping\|reload\|stop\|status\|profile on [sample\|full] [--for <dur>]\|profile off\|profile status>` | no | implemented | Send a control verb (with its arguments) to the daemon: ping, reload, stop, status, or profile (switch per-check CPU and allocation profiling on for a limited time, off, or report it). |
| `defect` | `<report\|list\|show\|rule\|archive\|backfill\|recurring\|similar> [flags] [--json]` | no | implemented | File, list, show and rule anti-hall defect reports and query the bug history: `report`, `list [--mine\|--open\|--unfinished]`, `show <fp>`, `rule <fp> --status ...`, `archive`, and the history verbs `backfill`, `recurring` and `similar`; the store is ~/.anti-hall/defects/. |
| `describe` | `[--part <a,b,...>] [--coverage]` | yes | implemented | The engine's generated self-description for the dashboard and agents: the generated reference (commands, flags, env, metrics, impact kinds) plus the registry settings, config files and keys, checks (bindings, reads, switch, rebindable), event bindings, scripts, Jev integrations, switches, jobs, control verbs and query sources; `--part a,b` limits it, `--coverage` reports the features no screen selector (`web.coverage`) covers, the ones a screen shows but cannot edit, and the selectors that match nothing. Nothing in it is hand-kept. |
| `devswarm` | `<status\|line\|supervisor\|ingest\|ledger [--since <window>]\|recover --id <ws> --request <id>\|advisory --session <id>\|archive --id <ws> --request <id>\|plan-prune --older-than <days>\|prune --confirm-ids <ids> --plan <nonce>\|help [<verb>]\|skip <guard> [--ttl <min>]\|archive-ignore <id>\|archive-unignore <id>\|gate-intent --reason <text>\|notice --list\|plan set\|show <id>\|scope add <id> --glob <g> --note <t>\|gate <id> --set <csv> --clear <csv>\|workspaces list\|logs [--limit <n>]\|wake-directive <id>\|ready-check <sha> [--base <ref>]\|app-state [--json]\|app-sync [--dry-run]\|done [--summary <text>]\|primary [status\|takeover] [--session <id>]\|relay <seq> --to <id> [--note-file <path>]\|archive-request <childId> [--reason <text>]\|nudge <id>\|supervision-report [--days <n>] [--json]\|sync-ui --titles-json <file> [--yes]\|retention status\|run [--dry-run] [--store <key>]\|unarchive <id>\|migrate-owner-keys\|ensure <id> [--worktree <p> --session <s>]\|register <id> --worktree <p> --session <s> [--nudge <word>]\|correct <id> [--dry-run]\|reap-orphans [--apply --max <n>]\|wake-watch [--auto]\|register-primary [--worktree <p> --session <s> --force]\|diagnose [--json]\|healthcheck [--json]\|merge [<hivecontrol merge-into-source args>]\|spawn <branch> [-s <src> -a <agent> -p <brief> -t <title>]\|respawn <id> [--dry-run]\|reconcile-registry\|reap-stale [--yes]\|reconcile-active --active <ids> [--yes]\|auto-archive>` | no | implemented | The DevSwarm realtime state and owner actions (lane dswire). `status` and `line` print the live workspace state and its statusline segment; `advisory --session <id>` prints the changes that session has not seen; `archive --id <ws> --request <id>`, `plan-prune --older-than <days>` and `prune --confirm-ids <a,b> --plan <nonce>` run the hivecontrol actions at the owner's request, with Node's preconditions, ledger and confirmations. `ingest` prints who drains the native queue (devswarm_ingest.mode), the projects and each project's lock and heartbeat (read-only). Roles (devswarm_wire.role_matrix): reads are open; the acting verbs are for the main session only. `create` and `merge` are `ah-engine mesh` verbs. The ah-engine mesh verbs `help`, `skip`, `archive-ignore`, `archive-unignore`, `gate-intent`, `notice --list`, `plan set\|show`, `scope add`, `gate`, `workspaces list`, `logs`, `wake-directive` (a child workspace), `ready-check`, `app-state`, `app-sync`, `done`, `primary`, `relay`, `archive-request`, `nudge`, `supervision-report`, `sync-ui`, `retention`, `unarchive`, `migrate-owner-keys`, `ensure`, `register`, `correct`, `reap-orphans`, `register-primary`, `diagnose`, `healthcheck`, `merge`, `spawn`, `respawn`, `reconcile-registry`, `reap-stale`, `reconcile-active` and `auto-archive` are native too (the guarded fronts: `spawn` answers its refusals, `respawn` its usage and not-primary refusals, `reap-stale` and `reconcile-active` their dry runs and an empty confirmed run, `auto-archive` the plan without the app database; Node answers the rest): `devswarm <verb> <the ah-engine mesh arguments>` prints what `ah-engine mesh <verb> ...` prints (Node answers what the engine defers). `supervisor` prints who owns the supervisor duties (devswarm_sup.mode), whether the Node supervisor is still running and each duty's gate; `recover --id <ws> --request <id>` kills and resumes ONE session on demand (never from a sweep): the engine refuses an automated caller, an unsafe id, a repeated request, a workspace without a worktree and session and one already recovered the most times allowed, then Node's devswarm-recover.js `run` does the kill with its exactly-one-target, identity and working-directory confirmations. Roles (devswarm_wire.role_matrix): reads are open; the acting verbs are for the main session only. `create` and `merge` are `ah-engine mesh` verbs. Inert (exit 64) where DevSwarm is absent. `wake-watch [--auto]` is the idle-wake Monitor the plugin runs for the whole session: it prints one line per event (armed, new mail, a persistent read error, a newer build) and runs until the session ends, on the realtime watch layer (OS events, polling where there are none) and the Node watcher's own tick; it reads plain files only and consumes nothing; roles: main session and workspace child. It answers exit 75 (nothing printed or written) for what only Node can decide, and the launcher then runs the Node watcher. |
| `diag` | `<cpu\|mem\|threads\|hooks\|mesh\|jev\|fs\|locks\|trace>` | yes | implemented | Read-only diagnostic reports over state the engine already keeps: cpu, mem, threads, hooks, mesh, jev, fs, locks and the trace ring. Needs no feature flag and changes nothing. |
| `dispatch-report` | `[--json]` | yes | implemented | Read-only effectiveness metrics: the parallel-dispatch demand shown, followed and ignored with its compliance rate, the idle-neglect blocks, the Jev dispatch-tier verdicts and follow rate, and the coordinator-work window's nudges, blocks and work share per plugin version. |
| `docs` | `[--format md\|skill\|skill-list] [--host <host>] [--name <path>] [--out <file>]` | yes | implemented | Print the generated reference: every command, setting, metric, impact kind, check and error code. `--out <file>` writes it atomically and only when something was generated (a failed run never leaves an empty file); with no text it exits 70 and prints why. |
| `doctor` | `[--check] [--repair\|--fix] [--dry-run] [--migrations-only] [--quiet] [--home <dir>] [--cwd <dir>] [--plugin-root <dir>] [--repair-ingest-orphans] [--repair-test-stores] [--repair-resurrected] [--apply]` | no | implemented | The health check and repair of anti-hall (D81), with the Node doctor's report layout and finding texts: the platform and versions, the hook scripts the registry names, the live behaviour of the guards (each built-in check run in-process on a crafted payload; a payload the engine defers to its Node hook is reported as a deferral, never a pass), the statusline configuration and the saved Workflow templates. Read-only by default; `--repair` (or `--fix`) runs the repair pass of `migrate` after the diagnostics, `--dry-run` previews it, and `--migrations-only` with either prints only the migration report as JSON. |
| `fallback` | `<node\|off\|status>` | no | implemented | The manual fallback switch of the Node backup (stage 2): `node` makes the launcher run the original Node hooks directly instead of the engine (it writes the marker file files.fallback_switch), `off` makes the engine answer again, `status` shows the switch. It never flips by itself; while it is on the Node hooks' verdicts are written to the shadow ledger with source node. |
| `finding-dedup` | `[--file <findings.json>]` | yes | implemented | Advisory duplicate-finding detector for the deadly-loop reviewers: reads a JSON array of findings (stdin or `--file`), asks Jev whether candidate pairs describe the same root cause, and prints `{groups}` on stdout and one `possible duplicates` line per confirmed pair on stderr. It never collapses anything; with Jev off or unkeyed it prints no groups. |
| `gen-hooks` | `--host claude\|codex [--kind hooks\|registry\|list\|map]` | yes | implemented | Print a file generated from the dispatch table (D87): the thin hooks.json (one trigger per event), the per-hook registry, the wrapper's fallback list or its fallback map, for one host. |
| `gh` | `<status\|segment\|poll> [--cwd <dir>] [--force]` | no | implemented | GitHub realtime (feature #20, independent of DevSwarm): `status` prints, from the state file with no network, what is followed (the repos of the working directories of live sessions, their pull request, review, CI and mergeability), the rate-limit budget, the hold in force (backoff, budget, gh missing, logged out or offline) and the measured rate-limit cost of 200 and 304 answers; `segment [--cwd <dir>]` prints the statusline piece for the repo that holds the directory (empty when there is nothing to say); `poll [--force]` runs one tick now. |
| `gh_poll` | `` | no | implemented | The scheduled GitHub realtime tick (the `gh_poll` job): notices pushes, polls the followed repos that are due inside the rate budget and records the edges; prints its counts with --json; exits nonzero when recent sessions exist and the tick leaves gh missing/logged-out/offline so the scheduler backs off. |
| `handovers` | `<index\|check\|search> [query] [--project <dir>] [--registered] [--force] [--limit <n>]` | no | implemented | The handover brief tree: `index` rebuilds the root brief and the per-day briefs (BRIEF.md plus a typed BRIEF.json) of the changed days under .anti-hall/handovers (`--registered` walks every project the SessionStart check has seen, `--force` rebuilds all days), `check` reports unindexed or stale handovers, missing briefs, malformed handovers and broken references without writing (exit 3 when there are any), `search <words> [date:..] [session:..] [decision:..] [file:..]` ranks entries from the sidecars. Never edits a handover file and never deletes. The logic is the plugin script handover-hygiene.js; the scheduled job `handovers` runs `index --registered`. |
| `harvest` | `[--dir <path>] [--stale-days <n>]` | yes | implemented | Scan a code tree for deliberate-debt markers, `anti-hall: <ceiling>, <when>` in any comment syntax, and flag the ones with no payback trigger or in files untouched for the stale window. |
| `hook` | `[--fallback <hook.js>] \| --event <Event> [--tool <Tool>] [--host claude\|codex] [--fallback-map <file>]` | no | implemented | The hook client: read one hook payload from stdin, ask the daemon, print the answer; falls back to the Node hook given by --fallback. With --event it is the per-event dispatcher: it runs every hook entry hooks.json registers for that event and tool, built-in checks in the engine and the rest as their Node hooks (--fallback-map overrides their commands), and combines the results the way the host would. |
| `impact` | `[--kind <kind>] [--project <hash>] [--window <7d>]` | yes | implemented | Show everything the engine affected: blocks by reason, warnings, context injected, fallbacks, and labelled savings estimates, including the NET of model-routing savings minus what injection and Jev cost (D77). |
| `install-codex` | `[--global] [--dry-run] [--root <plugin dir>]` | no | implemented | Install the anti-hall hooks for Codex (D81, lane L9b): merge the generated hook registration into .codex/hooks.json (project, or --global for the home directory), replacing only anti-hall's own groups, and enable the hooks feature in config.toml. A changed file is copied to <file>.bak-<time> first; --dry-run writes nothing. |
| `install-statusline` | `` | no | implemented | Retired no-op kept for old invocations: prints that anti-hall no longer writes a command-backed statusLine and exits 0. Use uninstall-statusline to clean up older installs. |
| `jev` | `<ask\|status\|scrub\|evidence>` | no | implemented | The optional Jev lane (D34-D38): `ask` reads JSON requests, one per stdin line, and prints each decision (a real call when Jev is enabled and keyed), `status` prints the resolved settings and each integration's mode without any key, `scrub` redacts secrets from JSON strings read one per stdin line. |
| `jev-report` | `[--json] [--days N] [--window 24h\|7d] [--by project\|session] [--project <name>] [--weekly] \| label <hash> [tp\|fp] \| prune-audit --days N` | no | implemented | The Jev report of the /anti-hall:jev skill: per-integration calls, agreement, changed decisions, precision, cost and the KEEP / REVIEW / REMOVE verdict from the decision log, with `--json`, `--days`, `--window 24h\|7d`, `--by project\|session`, `--project`, `--weekly`, `--since`, `--until`, `--exclude-window`, `--exclude-project`; `label <hash> [tp\|fp]` reads or records a human precision label and `prune-audit --days N` trims the audit snippets (the only two forms that write). |
| `jev-setup` | `<status\|enable\|disable\|set-key\|bind-generic-key\|test\|mode\|review-due\|reviewed\|snooze> [--days <n>] [--transport vercel\|typesafe] [--fallback vercel\|typesafe\|none] [--role fallback] [--vendor vercel\|typesafe]` | no | implemented | Activate, configure and inspect the opt-in Jev classifier: `status` (resolved settings, key presence yes or no, every integration's mode, calls in the last 24 hours, the Vercel credit balance), `enable` and `disable`, `set-key` (the key is read from stdin only and written 0600), `bind-generic-key`, `mode <integration> on\|shadow\|off`, `test` (one real gateway call per configured transport, each on its own) and the shadow-review verbs `review-due [--json]`, `reviewed <integration>` and `snooze <integration> --days N`. |
| `jev_sweep` | `` | no | implemented | The scheduled Jev evidence sweep (the `jev_sweep` job): gathers the WaitKind, Loop and StepMap facts of the supervisor's questions (plan, transcript, git, CI, mesh) and runs them through the evidence gate, writing its telemetry; takes no arguments and reads the home directory from the environment. |
| `maintain` | `` | no | implemented | Size control (D26): move consumed messages, expired key values and old impact events from hot.db to archive.db, prune derived bookkeeping, checkpoint both WALs and VACUUM both databases; prints a report. |
| `mesh` | `<unread\|dump\|read <id>> [--db <devswarm.db>] [--since <n>] [--last <n>] \| roster --db <devswarm.db> \| <mesh verb argv>` | no | implemented | DevSwarm mesh store (D45). With `--db <file>`: the read-only S0 reader (stage S0): `roster` lists the registered workspaces, `unread` the per-workspace counts, `read --id <ws>` its messages (`--since <n>` skips the first n, `--last <n>` the newest n, capped by mesh.read_byte_cap), `dump` the full canonical dump the parity harness compares with Node; the store is opened read-only and never created, and a journal-backed store is refused. Without `--db`, `unread`, `read <id>` and `dump` read the store of the project the working directory is in (`read <id>` finds the one other project store that holds an id this project does not); every other word after `mesh` starts a mesh verb argv that the engine runs itself (`help --short` lists the verbs, `help <verb>` shows one verb's forms), per the `mesh.engine_writes` switch: on (default) the engine answers, and says so on stderr and exits with mesh_write.exit_unable when it cannot; off does nothing, counted and said. A verb form that moved is refused with the command to use instead (mesh_write.retired_verbs, exit mesh_write.exit_unsupported); `inbox <sub>` without an id reads the calling workspace session's own. The ah-engine mesh verb `archive <id>` (the local archive and the DevSwarm app leg, `hivecontrol workspace archive` with Node's retry) is answered here too, and only here: the owner action of the same name under the realtime command takes `--id` and `--request`. |
| `metrics` | `[--check <name>] [--rollup <resolution> [--since <s>]]` | yes | implemented | Show the engine's metrics: counters, gauges and latency percentiles, optionally for one check; with --rollup, the stored rollups of one resolution (minute, hour), optionally for the last --since seconds. |
| `migrate` | `[--dry-run] [--home <dir>] [--cwd <dir>] [--plugin-root <dir>]` | no | implemented | The persisted-state migrations and sweeps of the Node doctor's repair pass (D81): the legacy progress and history copy, the reply-state, gate-intent and auto-archive state forward-migrations, the settings.json migration from the legacy jev.json and the stored plugin options, the Jev triage cache repair, the lock scratch sweep and the retention sweeps, with Node's report; `--dry-run` previews and writes nothing. Steps that need the DevSwarm stores are left to the Node doctor while DevSwarm state is present. |
| `phase` | `<set\|advance\|step\|agents\|update\|clear> [args]` | no | implemented | Write or update the phase state the status line's phase bar shows: `set <code> <desc> <done> <total>`, `advance [n]`, `step <text>`, `agents <n>`, `update key=value ...`, `clear`; the state is ~/.anti-hall/phase-state.json. Fails open. |
| `proc` | `<list\|status\|stop\|restart> [<pid>] [--confirmed] [--json]` | no | implemented | Dashboard process actions by pid, audited: `list` shows the engine family's records (the wake watchers and the web server), `status <pid>` reads one, `stop <pid> --confirmed` sends SIGTERM and `restart <pid> --confirmed` stops it and starts it again from its recorded command. Only a pid with a record of an engine-family process is accepted, it must still have the recorded start stamp and executable, an agent session is refused, and nothing is found by name or killed with SIGKILL. |
| `proj` | `<cwd> <put\|take\|len\|set\|setex\|get> [args]` | no | implemented | Per-project state in hot.db: a mailbox (put, take, len) and key-value pairs (set, setex with a TTL in seconds, get); the partition is derived from the cwd. |
| `query` | `[<source>] [--limit <n>] [--offset <n>] [--where <field=value,...>] [--since <7d>] [--window <7d>] [--schema]` | yes | implemented | Read-only, paginated query over the existing stores: `query <source> [--limit N] [--offset N] [--where field=value,...] [--since 7d] [--schema]`; `query sources` lists the sources (per-check stats, outcomes, kinds, events, counters, agents, health, config history) with their filters, and `--schema` shows one source's row fields. |
| `reset` | `` | no | implemented | Clear the client breaker, the crash-loop stop and the failure record. |
| `restore` | `<snapshot-dir>` | no | implemented | Restore a snapshot directory: first keep the current state as an unscrubbed pre-restore snapshot (never deleted), stop the daemon, then swap the databases. |
| `schedule` | `<list\|run <job>\|history> [--job <name>] [--limit <n>]` | no | implemented | The scheduler (D33): `list` the jobs with their next run and last result, `run <job>` now (waits briefly for the result), or show the run `history` from hot.db; adding and removing jobs from the command line is planned (D33), today they come from schedules.toml and schedules.json. |
| `serve` | `` | no | implemented | Run the resident daemon in the foreground (the client starts it detached when needed). |
| `settings` | `<show\|get\|set\|reset\|judge\|tunables\|trust-command-allow\|trust-edit-allow> [args] [--section <key>] [--all] [--confirmed] [--json]` | no | implemented | Show or change any anti-hall setting: `show [--section <key>] [--all]`, `get <section.key>`, `set <section.key> <value> [--confirmed]`, `reset <section.key> [--confirmed]`, `judge on\|off\|status`, `tunables [<category\|key prefix>] [--all]` (every key of the plugin's engine/defaults/*.toml with its default, env variable and description, grouped by file; read-only, edit the file to change one), and `trust-command-allow` / `trust-edit-allow [<repo>] [--confirmed]`; the settings.json file and the registry are the plugin's own. |
| `shadow-compare` | `[--days N] [--check ID] [--event NAME] [--daily]` | yes | implemented | Report how the engine and the original Node hooks agree (the Node backup, stage 1): pairs the shadow ledger's engine rows and node rows and prints, per check, the compared pairs, agreement, engine-weaker, engine-stricter and the errors of each side, plus what the shadow skipped (CPU, load, payload size, busy slots). `--days N` sets the window (default nodeback.report_days), `--check ID` and `--event NAME` narrow it, `--daily` adds a line per UTC day, `--json` prints everything. Works without the daemon; a daily job (shadow_report) also writes the JSON report to nodeback.report_file. |
| `shadow-run` | `<job file>` | no | implemented | Internal: the detached half of the Node shadow. Runs the Node hooks of one followed hook event on their own, in a scratch home, and writes the engine rows and the node rows to the shadow ledger; started by the engine, not by people. |
| `status` | `[--memory] [--threads] [--migration]` | yes | implemented | Show the daemon's state: version, uptime, memory, counters, breaker and crash-loop state, rules, and a headline summary of what it did. |
| `statusline` | `(session JSON on stdin)` | no | implemented | The two-line status line the host runs after each turn (L9a): reads the session JSON on stdin; line 1 is the configured base command or the rich line, line 2 the phase bar, swarm activity or context gauge. Fails open. |
| `stop` | `` | no | implemented | Ask the daemon to drain and exit. |
| `telemetry` | `[summary\|events\|rollup\|actions [feature]] [--window <7d>] [--kind <k>] [--limit <n>] [--mistake <feature> <action> <target> <kind>]` | no | implemented | Telemetry (D78): `summary` (invocations, outcomes, latency and injected bytes per hook and check), `events` (routing, spawn, Jev and spill events), `rollup` (move complete days into archive.db and apply the retention), `actions [feature]` (what the acting features did and got wrong: action counts, success rate, mistake signals and mistake rate; `--mistake <feature> <action> <target> <kind>` records one the engine cannot see, such as a dismissed escalation). Local only. |
| `uninstall-statusline` | `[--user\|--project] [--purge-base]` | no | implemented | Take an older anti-hall status line out of the host's settings: restores the saved original statusLine, else the settings backup, else removes the key; `--project` for ./.claude/settings.local.json, `--purge-base` to also remove the shared base configuration. |
| `update` | `[--check] [--post-pull-only] \| --from-local <dir> [--engine-bin F] [--hook-bin F] [--tree D] [--source release\|local\|manual] [--check] [--yes] [--force] \| --rollback [--deploy-dir D] [--yes]` | no | implemented | Update anti-hall (D81, lane L9b, the native update): `git pull --ff-only` of the marketplace clone (a dirty tree or a diverged history is a hard STOP, offline fails open), a copy of the plugin into a new version-pinned cache directory, the harness's own `claude plugin update` when its registry is behind (bounded, never answering a confirmation; installed_plugins.json is only read), the changelog delta, then one JSON status line and a human summary. `--check` only compares versions (with --json it adds an `engine` object: the running build version, its sha, where it came from - release, local build or manual - and the latest GitHub release). `--from-local <dir>` and `--rollback` run the ONE install routine (pre-check, rollback copy, install, settle, validate, automatic rollback on failure, cleanup, install record); a downgrade needs --force. The DevSwarm store sweeps and the settings migration still run by the plugin's own update.js --post-pull-only and are merged into the status. |
| `version` | `` | yes | implemented | Print the version this build reports. |
| `web` | `[open\|status] [--no-open] [--json]` | no | implemented | The Command Center web dashboard (GH #266): `open` (default) starts the local server when it is not running and prints its address, opening it in the browser unless --no-open; `status` says whether it runs. The server (binary ah-web) binds to the loopback address on a random port behind a per-session token, serves the live agent tree and exits when idle (web.idle_exit_s). Reads the agent list through `agents status`; changes nothing. Switch: web.enabled. |
| `mcp-reaper` | `run [--dry-run]` | no | implemented | The standalone MCP orphan reaper as an engine command: `run` makes one sweep (the scheduled job `mcp_reaper` runs it every mcp_reaper.job_every_ms), `--dry-run` logs what it would reap and signals nothing. It does nothing while maintenance.mcpReaperJob is off, on auto until the Node reaper's opt-in was carried over (`ah-engine units heal`), and while a Node reaper unit is still installed, so the reaper never runs twice. Prints one JSON line. |
| `refresh` | `[--force] [--home <dir>]` | no | implemented | Handle the pending session-cache refresh requests the SessionStart checks wrote (L06): the remote-latest release tag (version-alert), the Claude Code and DevSwarm CLI versions (the drift probes) and the reload repair (repair-on-reload), each as a bounded subprocess; `--force` runs every probe whether requested or not (never the repair unless requested). Prints one result per probe. The scheduler runs it every refresh.every_ms. |
| `engine-update` | `--from <file> [--sha256 <x>] [--yes] \| --channel <stable\|dev> \| --rollback \| --auto [--dry-run] [--no-restart]` | no | implemented | Update the engine binary: runs the thin client's updater (ah-engine update) with the given arguments (--from FILE [--sha256 X] [--yes] \| --channel stable\|dev \| --rollback \| --auto \| --dry-run). The engine itself does no network access. |
| `post-update-check` | `[--dry-run] [--expect-sha <sha256>]` | no | implemented | The step every update ends with: verify exactly one live engine runs the installed binary (sha, path, answers status and a ping inside its budget), stop stale and scratch daemons and duplicate watchers by verified pid (never pkill), let watchers on a replaced binary re-execute themselves, report servers on an old binary, and clean old binary copies, dead pid files, a dead socket and dead temp files. --dry-run reports and changes nothing. Exit 0 verified, 1 not. |
| `units` | `<status\|install\|heal\|uninstall> [--dry-run] [--bin <path>]` | no | implemented | The engine's service units: `status` lists the engine unit and the units the Node installers wrote, with whether the engine runs their duty; `install` writes (or refreshes) the one unit that keeps `ah-engine serve` running (launchd on macOS, a systemd user service and timer on Linux) and loads it; `heal` installs and then retires each Node unit whose duty the engine runs (the MCP reaper when its job is on, the DevSwarm supervisor and ingest when devswarm_sup.mode / devswarm_ingest.mode is engine); `uninstall` unloads the engine unit. `--dry-run` reports and changes nothing; `--bin <path>` names the engine binary the unit runs. A removed unit file is moved into the state directory, never deleted. A retired unit that comes back is recorded as a mistake and left alone. |
| `codex-activate` | `` | no | implemented | Write the advisory Codex activation marker ~/.anti-hall/codex-activated.json ({activatedAt, scope = the working directory}) that the anti-hall-activate skill leaves after installing the hooks; it changes no real configuration and deleting it is harmless. |
| `codex-limit-status` | `` | yes | implemented | Print whether limit conservation is active, as JSON (active, reason, weekly, fiveHour, sonnetWeekly, source, stale, resetsAt): the Codex skill anti-hall-context-conserve runs it. Same decision as the limit-conserve-inject hook: the limitConserve.mode setting (on, off, auto), else the OMC usage cache with the threshold, the reset-aware and snapshot-age rules and the account-switch guard. Read-only apart from the account-switch state file the hook keeps current. Fail-open: an unreadable cache is inactive. |

## Flags

Every flag in a command's arguments, with the commands that take it. A flag shared by several commands is described once; the command's own entry says how it uses it.

| Flag | Commands | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--active` | `devswarm` | Comma-separated workspace ids that are currently active in the app (`devswarm reconcile-active`). |
| `--all` | `settings` | Include every item, also the advanced ones (`settings show`, `settings tunables`). |
| `--allow` |  | Comma-separated globs a change may touch; files outside them are reported (`devswarm ready-check`). |
| `--apply` | `devswarm`, `doctor` | Carry out the previewed change instead of only reporting it (`devswarm reap-orphans`, `doctor --repair-*`). |
| `--auto` | `devswarm`, `engine-update` | Run in the automatic mode the plugin starts (`devswarm wake-watch`). |
| `--base` | `devswarm` | The base ref to compare against (`devswarm ready-check`). |
| `--bin` | `units` | Path of the engine binary the installed service unit runs (`units`). |
| `--by` | `jev-report` | Group the report by `project` or `session` (`jev-report`). |
| `--channel` | `engine-update` | Update channel to install from: `stable` or `dev` (`engine-update`). |
| `--check` | `config`, `doctor`, `metrics`, `shadow-compare`, `update` | Name of one check to limit the output to (`metrics`), a read-only check without repairs (`doctor`, `update`), or validation only without writing (`config set`). |
| `--clear` | `devswarm` | Comma-separated gates to clear (`devswarm gate`). |
| `--confirm-ids` | `devswarm` | Comma-separated workspace ids the owner confirmed for pruning (`devswarm prune`). |
| `--confirmed` | `config`, `proc`, `settings` | Confirm a change to a safety-relevant setting, after the one-line warning (`settings set`, `settings reset`). |
| `--coverage` | `describe` | Report which features a dashboard screen covers, which it cannot edit and which selectors are stale (`describe`). |
| `--cwd` | `coordinator-work-baseline`, `doctor`, `gh`, `migrate` | Directory to treat as the working directory instead of the current one. |
| `--daily` | `shadow-compare` | Add a line per UTC day (`shadow-compare`). |
| `--days` | `devswarm`, `jev-report`, `jev-setup`, `shadow-compare` | Look-back window in days, or the snooze length for `jev-setup snooze`. |
| `--db` | `mesh` | Path of a DevSwarm database to read instead of the live one (`mesh`; makes the verb read-only). |
| `--debug` |  | Turns debug mode (diagnostics.debug_mode) on for one `serve` or `hook` process. |
| `--deploy-dir` | `update` | Install or update into this directory. |
| `--dir` | `harvest` | Directory to scan (`harvest`). |
| `--dry-run` | `devswarm`, `doctor`, `install-codex`, `migrate`, `mcp-reaper`, `engine-update`, `post-update-check`, `units` | Show what would change and write nothing. |
| `--engine-bin` | `update` | Use this ah-engine binary for an operator routine. |
| `--event` | `hook`, `shadow-compare` | The hook event name to dispatch (`hook --event`). |
| `--expect-sha` | `post-update-check` | Require the installed engine to have this SHA-256. |
| `--fallback` | `hook`, `jev-setup` | The fallback transport of the Jev classifier (`jev-setup enable`). Older versions of `hook` took a Node script here; it is ignored now. |
| `--fallback-map` | `hook` | File that maps hook entries to their Node fallback commands (`hook --event`). |
| `--fetch` |  | Run `git fetch --quiet` before the checks (`devswarm ready-check`). |
| `--file` | `finding-dedup` | Read the input from this file instead of stdin. |
| `--fix` | `doctor` | Same as `--repair` (`doctor`). |
| `--for` | `ctl` | How long a runtime switch stays on (`ctl profile on --for 10m`: a number with an optional ms, s, m or h suffix; a bare number is seconds). |
| `--force` | `devswarm`, `gh`, `handovers`, `update`, `refresh` | Go past the usual skip: `gh poll` polls now, `handovers index` rebuilds every day, `devswarm register-primary` overrides the existing registration. |
| `--format` | `docs` | Output format; `md` prints the Markdown reference (`docs`). |
| `--from` | `engine-update` | Install from this local file, a release .tar.gz or a bare engine binary (`engine-update`). |
| `--from-line` | `coordinator-work-baseline` | First transcript line to replay (`coordinator-work-baseline`). |
| `--from-local` | `update` | Use the local checkout or branch as the source. |
| `--glob` | `devswarm` | Path glob a workspace is allowed to touch (`devswarm scope add`). |
| `--global` | `install-codex` | Install into the home directory instead of the current project (`install-codex`). |
| `--home` | `audit`, `doctor`, `migrate`, `refresh` | Home directory to use instead of the real one (scratch-HOME runs). |
| `--hook-bin` | `update` | Use this ah-hook binary for an operator routine. |
| `--host` | `docs`, `gen-hooks`, `hook` | The host the output is for: `claude` or `codex`. |
| `--id` | `devswarm` | Workspace id (`devswarm`, `mesh`). |
| `--into` |  | Target branch for a mesh merge. |
| `--job` | `schedule` | Name of one scheduled job (`schedule`). |
| `--json` | `agents`, `audit`, `auto-handover-config`, `coordinator-work-baseline`, `defect`, `devswarm`, `dispatch-report`, `jev-report`, `proc`, `settings`, `web` | Print machine-readable JSON instead of text. Accepted by every command. |
| `--key` | `config` | Limit the history to one setting key (`config history`). |
| `--kind` | `gen-hooks`, `impact`, `telemetry` | Limit the output to one kind (an impact kind, a telemetry kind, or the generated file kind for `gen-hooks`). |
| `--last` | `mesh` | Only the last N entries (`mesh`). |
| `--limit` | `config`, `devswarm`, `handovers`, `query`, `schedule`, `telemetry` | Maximum number of rows to print. |
| `--list` | `devswarm` | List instead of acting (`devswarm notice --list`). |
| `--max` | `devswarm` | Upper bound on how many items one run may act on (`devswarm reap-orphans`). |
| `--memory` | `status` | Add the per-subsystem memory breakdown to the output (`status`). |
| `--message` |  | The body of a mesh message (`mesh send`). |
| `--migration` | `status` | Print the migration report: every hook check, supervisor duty, post-update stage, command and Node switch as native, partial or node (`status`; add `--json` for the machine form). |
| `--migrations-only` | `doctor` | With `--repair` or `--fix`, run only the migration pass and print its report as JSON (`doctor`). |
| `--mistake` | `telemetry` | Record a mistake signal the engine cannot see itself: `--mistake <feature> <action> <target> <kind> [detail]` (`telemetry actions`). |
| `--name` | `docs` | Name the generated skill document (`docs --format skill`). |
| `--no-live` | `audit` | Skip the live-machine section of the entry-path audit. |
| `--no-open` | `web` | Print the dashboard address without opening a browser. |
| `--no-restart` | `engine-update` | Install without restarting the daemon; the next hook call starts the new one (`engine-update`). |
| `--note` | `devswarm` | Free-text note stored with the entry (`devswarm scope add`). |
| `--note-file` | `devswarm` | File whose contents are sent as the note (`devswarm relay`). |
| `--nudge` | `devswarm` | The nudge word a registered workspace answers to (`devswarm register`). |
| `--offset` | `query` | Rows to skip before the page starts (`query`). |
| `--older-than` | `devswarm` | Only items older than this many days (`devswarm plan-prune`). |
| `--out` | `docs` | Write generated documentation to the named output file. |
| `--part` | `describe` | Comma-separated parts of the self-description to return (`describe`). |
| `--plan` | `devswarm` | The nonce printed by `plan-prune`, proving the prune was planned first (`devswarm prune`). |
| `--plugin-root` | `doctor`, `migrate` | Plugin directory whose files are read, before anything is loaded. |
| `--post-pull-only` | `update` | Run only the steps that follow a plugin update pull (`update`). |
| `--project` | `handovers`, `impact`, `jev-report`, `uninstall-statusline` | Limit the output to one project (a hash, name or directory, per command), or the project-level settings file (`uninstall-statusline`). |
| `--purge-base` | `uninstall-statusline` | Also remove the saved base statusline (`uninstall-statusline`). |
| `--quiet` | `doctor` | Print only problems (`doctor`). |
| `--reason` | `devswarm` | Why the action is taken; recorded with it (`devswarm`). |
| `--receipt` |  | Delivery receipt identifier for inbox acknowledgement. |
| `--registered` | `handovers` | Walk every project the SessionStart check has seen (`handovers index`). |

## Environment variables

Every `AH_ENGINE_*` variable the engine or its wrappers read. A variable that overrides a setting names that setting.

| Variable | Setting | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AH_ENGINE_ACK_TIMEOUT_MS` | `storage.ack_timeout_ms` | How long a request waits for its write to commit before it is answered with an error (the client then retries or spools; the write id makes a late commit harmless); kept below client.ctl_timeout_ms so the client hears the error. |
| `AH_ENGINE_AGENT_TICK_MS` | `schedule.agent_tick_ms` | Interval of the agent_tick job; 0 turns the tracker's ticks off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_ALLOCATOR` |  | Selects the daemon's allocator: jemalloc (default) or system. The client sets it from `diagnostics.allocator` on the daemon it spawns, unless it is already set; the daemon reads it before its first allocation. Environment variable the client sets on the daemon it spawns to select the allocator (the daemon reads it before its first allocation). An existing value in the client's own environment wins. |
| `AH_ENGINE_AUTO_UPDATE` |  | Read by `ah-hook update --auto`: off, stable or dev overrides the `engine.autoUpdate` setting for one run. |
| `AH_ENGINE_BACKUP_MS` | `schedule.backup_ms` | Interval of the backup job (D27); 0 (the default) turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_BIN` |  | Test-only: the engine binary the thin client runs instead of the installed one. The thin client ignores it unless AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1 is also set, so a stray value can never turn the safety net into a silent allow. Test-only: environment variable that replaces the engine binary (honoured only when the test flag is set). |
| `AH_ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP` |  | Set to 0 or 1 to turn the automatic download of the sha256-pinned engine binary off or on (default off: the explicit install is `sh hooks/install.sh --download`); overrides the `engine.bootstrap` setting. Read by `ah-hook install --auto` and hooks/install.sh. |
| `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S` | `client.breaker_cooldown_s` | How long the breaker stays open once tripped. |
| `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_N` | `client.breaker_n` | Engine failures within the window that open the breaker (the client then skips the engine). |
| `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_WINDOW_S` | `client.breaker_window_s` | Window in which breaker failures are counted. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CLAUDE_BIN` |  | Overrides the Claude Code program the agent tracker asks for its session listing (tests point it at a stand-in). |
| `AH_ENGINE_COMMIT_MARK` | `mesh_write.env_commit_mark` | The environment variable by which the stable launcher names a marker file; the engine creates it at its commit point, so a launcher that has to stop the engine (time limit) can tell that the verb already acted and must not be run again in Node. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CONFIG` |  | Overrides the path of the engine's own user config file (default: config.toml in the state directory). |
| `AH_ENGINE_CONFIG_DEBOUNCE_MS` | `config.debounce_ms` | A change must stay unchanged this long before it is loaded, so a half-written or rapidly edited file is read once. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CONFIG_WATCH_MS` | `config.watch_ms` | How often the daemon checks the config files for a change. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_COOLDOWN_S` | `client.crash_cooldown_s` | How long respawning stays stopped after a crash loop. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_N` | `client.crash_n` | Daemon deaths within the window that stop respawning. |
| `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_WINDOW_S` | `client.crash_window_s` | Window in which daemon deaths are counted. |
| `AH_ENGINE_DEADLINE_MS` | `client.deadline_ms` | Overall hook-client deadline for one engine exchange (connect, write, read); a hard watchdog thread enforces it so a hung daemon fails open quickly. |
| `AH_ENGINE_DEBUG` |  | When set to anything but 0 or empty, turns debug mode (diagnostics.debug_mode) on for that process. |
| `AH_ENGINE_DIR` |  | Overrides the state directory (default: base_dir/state_dir under the home directory). |
| `AH_ENGINE_DISPATCH_IN_PROCESS` | `dispatch.in_process` | Run the built-in checks inside the hook client (1) instead of asking the daemon (0, the default). |
| `AH_ENGINE_DISPATCH_MAX_TIMEOUT_S` | `dispatch.max_timeout_s` | An upper bound on any Node hook's timeout, whatever its hooks.json entry says (the default is above every real timeout, so it changes nothing; tests lower it to exercise a hook that never exits). |
| `AH_ENGINE_DONE_FILE` |  | A file the dispatcher creates once it has dispatched an event and decided its exit code (D87). The thin client sets it, so that an engine exit code of a hook's own (1, say) is told from an engine failure and is not answered by running every hook a second time. |
| `AH_ENGINE_DOWN_MARKER_TTL_MS` | `client.down_marker_ttl_ms` | How long other clients skip connecting after one client finds the daemon absent or failed, or hung (client.heartbeat_stale_ms) and not replaced, or after client.slow_down_n consecutive slow replies; this prevents hook pile-ups while a restart is attempted. |
| `AH_ENGINE_EVAL_BUDGET_US` | `daemon.eval_budget_us` | HARD thread CPU budget of ONE check: a check that used more than this alone loses its own answer (counted answers_dropped reason `cpu_budget`) and takes its failure policy; the checks after it still run and answer, and the request as a whole is bounded by daemon.request_hard_ms. The SOFT budget (a warning only) is daemon.eval_soft_us. 0 turns the hard budget off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_FAIL_OPEN_FILE` |  | A file the client appends one line to (`<reason> <check>`) for every engine-level fail-open the daemon reported in a reply (GitHub #201). The launcher sets it inside its per-call run directory and counts the lines after the engine exits, so its own stats and log know the call failed open. |
| `AH_ENGINE_FULLFSYNC` | `storage.fullfsync` | 1 makes SQLite use F_FULLFSYNC on macOS, which also survives power loss at a large cost in commit rate (D73: 479 against 43k commits per second measured); 0 keeps the plain fsync. Off until metrics decide. |
| `AH_ENGINE_GH_POLL_MS` | `schedule.gh_poll_ms` | Interval of the gh_poll job, the tick that decides which repos are due (the cadences below decide how often a repo is really polled); 0 turns GitHub realtime off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_GITIGNORE_PROBE_MS` | `session.gitignore_probe_ms` | The longest the engine waits for the gitignore probe before it hands the hook to Node. Node waits 3000 ms, but the client gives up on the engine after client.deadline_ms, so a longer wait here could answer after the client has already left; a test keeps the shipped value below that deadline. |
| `AH_ENGINE_GROUP_COMMIT_MS` | `storage.group_commit_ms` | Group-commit window: after taking a write, the writer waits up to this long for more before committing them together (D23); 0 commits at once with whatever is already queued, which still groups writes that arrive during a commit. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HANDOVERS_MS` | `schedule.handovers_ms` | Interval of the handovers job; 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HEALTHY_AFTER_S` | `daemon.healthy_after_s` | How long the daemon must stay up before its binary is recorded as having run healthy (files.healthy_binary). A binary that dies earlier never earns the record, so a roll-back may replace it. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HEALTH_SNAPSHOT_MS` | `telemetry.health_snapshot_ms` | How often the daemon records a `daemon` health snapshot event (resident set, its cap, restarts, degraded flag, queue and worker load, saturation). Events are kept for retention_days and capped by max_event_rows. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HEARTBEAT_CONFIRM_MS` | `client.heartbeat_confirm_ms` | How long a stale daemon heartbeat (client.heartbeat_stale_ms) must stay unchanged, by the monotonic clock, before a client ends that daemon. The first stale sample only records a suspicion and fails open; any beat, a new daemon, or a wall-clock jump that only made a moving heartbeat read old resets it. Keep it at most client.down_marker_ttl_ms, so a stopped daemon is replaced by the first call after the down marker expires. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS` | `client.heartbeat_stale_ms` | A hook call past client.deadline_ms keeps waiting for a late reply (client.slow_fallback_max_ms) only while the daemon's heartbeat (files.heartbeat) is younger than this. Older means the daemon may be stopped or wedged, not slow: the call fails open at once and marks it down (client.down_marker_ttl_ms). One stale sample only raises a suspicion (files.heartbeat_suspect); the client ends that daemon only once the same heartbeat stayed unchanged for client.heartbeat_confirm_ms, and only when it is the pid holding the singleton lock, verified as this engine's daemon, of this state dir, and still the process generation the heartbeat recorded (start time and executable from the operating system, re-read immediately before the signal); single-flight and under the crash-loop rule. Then it starts a new one. A heartbeat that names another pid or is missing counts as alive. Keep it well above daemon.watchdog_tick_ms and below client.slow_fallback_max_ms less client.slow_wait_margin_ms, so a stop is detected within the first slow call. 0 disables the check. |
| `AH_ENGINE_HOOK_ENGINE_MIN` |  | Set by the hook launcher (ah-hook) on the engine client it runs, to the lowest engine version that launcher supports. It travels with each request (`request_env.allow`) and the daemon checks it against its own version (`compat` in status). |
| `AH_ENGINE_HOOK_VERSION` |  | Set by the hook launcher (ah-hook) on the engine client it runs, to the launcher's own build version. It travels with each request (`request_env.allow`) and the daemon reports the last one it saw as `hook_version` in status and pulse. |
| `AH_ENGINE_IDLE_EXIT_S` | `daemon.idle_exit_s` | Seconds without any request after which the daemon exits cleanly (the next hook call starts a fresh one, and the scheduler catches up its missed jobs); 0 keeps it resident. Default is 1800 (about 30 minutes), so a daemon with no sessions does not linger forever. A daemon whose state dir, lock file or executable is gone still exits on its own (daemon.orphan_check_ms). |
| `AH_ENGINE_INSTALL_LOCK_HOOK_WAIT_S` | `rollback.lock_hook_wait_s` | How long the integrity check started by the thin client waits for the install lock before skipping (the next run checks). A held lock never holds a session. |
| `AH_ENGINE_INSTALL_LOCK_STALE_S` | `rollback.lock_stale_s` | An install lock held longer than this is broken (one whose holder process is gone is broken at once). Longer than the slowest install: updater.go_live_timeout_s. |
| `AH_ENGINE_INSTALL_LOCK_TOKEN` |  | Set by an installer (`ah-hook update`) for the integrity check: the token of the install lock it already holds, so recording the expected sha256 runs under the caller's hold instead of waiting on it. |
| `AH_ENGINE_INSTALL_LOCK_WAIT_S` | `rollback.lock_wait_s` | How long an install, a roll-back by the updater, or the recording of the expected sha256 waits for the install lock before giving up (the installer then fails and keeps the old binary). |
| `AH_ENGINE_JEV_ARRIVAL_MS` | `schedule.jev_arrival_ms` | Interval of the jev_arrival job (how soon a queued arrival is labelled); the job does nothing while the queue is empty. 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_JEV_SWEEP_MS` | `schedule.jev_sweep_ms` | Interval of the jev_sweep job; 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_MAINTAIN_MS` | `schedule.maintain_ms` | Interval of the maintain job (D26); 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_MAX_EVENTS` | `telemetry.max_events` | Most impact events kept in memory (oldest dropped first); counts per kind are kept exactly in separate counters. |
| `AH_ENGINE_MAX_REQUEST` | `daemon.max_request` | Largest request the daemon reads; the client sends nothing larger (it falls back instead). |
| `AH_ENGINE_MCP_REAPER_MS` | `mcp_reaper.job_every_ms` | Interval of the mcp_reaper job (the Node unit's StartInterval was 60 s); 0 turns the job off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_MEM_MB` | `daemon.mem_mb` | Data-segment limit applied with setrlimit; 0 = none. It is a ceiling against runaway allocation, not a budget (the RSS cap is the budget), and Linux enforces it on thread stacks, so it must exceed daemon.workers times git.stack_mb plus headroom or a check thread cannot start. macOS does not support RLIMIT_DATA here, so the daemon reports unsupported and relies on the RSS/footprint cap. |
| `AH_ENGINE_MESH_NOW_MS` |  | Pins `Date.now()` of an `ah-engine mesh` verb, in epoch milliseconds (the parity tests pin Node's `ctx.now` the same way). Never set in production. |
| `AH_ENGINE_NICE` | `daemon.nice` | `nice` increment applied to the daemon process. |
| `AH_ENGINE_NOSPAWN` |  | When set, the client never starts a daemon (tests, and hosts that manage the daemon themselves). |
| `AH_ENGINE_PLUGIN_ROOT` |  | Plugin install directory, used by built-in checks that build override commands (a rule's `options.plugin_root` wins). |
| `AH_ENGINE_PROCWATCH_MS` | `schedule.procwatch_ms` | Interval of the process watch job (resource sampling; orphan scans run every procwatch.scan_every_s); 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_PROJECT_BURST` | `daemon.project_burst` | Token-bucket burst per project. |
| `AH_ENGINE_PROJECT_RPS` | `daemon.project_rps` | Sustained requests per second allowed per project; 0 = unlimited. |
| `AH_ENGINE_QUEUE` | `daemon.queue` | Connections that may wait for a worker; beyond this the daemon answers BUSY and the client falls back. |
| `AH_ENGINE_READ_MS` | `daemon.read_ms` | Total time a client has to deliver its request. |
| `AH_ENGINE_REFRESH_MS` | `refresh.every_ms` | How often the refresh job looks for requests; a request waits at most this long (plus jitter). Cheap when there is none: it reads a few small files. 0 turns the job off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RELEASE_BASE` |  | Test-only: download base URL for the engine binary (http allowed). Honored by `ah-hook install` and hooks/install.sh only with AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1. |
| `AH_ENGINE_REQUEST_PEER_PID` | `request_env.peer_pid_key` | The name under which a daemon request's sender pid (its socket peer; 0 when the socket did not say) reaches the checks. Not on the allowlist, so no client can set it; host functions that walk the process ancestry (the DevSwarm reader nonce) start there. Absent in a one-shot `ah-engine check`, which starts at itself. |
| `AH_ENGINE_ROLLBACK_FAIL_N` | `rollback.fail_n` | Engine failures seen by the thin client (timeout, signal death, no answer) within rollback.fail_window_s that roll a never-healthy binary back. The thin client counts them because a hung binary cannot count its own. |
| `AH_ENGINE_ROLLBACK_FAIL_WINDOW_S` | `rollback.fail_window_s` | Window in which the wrapper's engine failures are counted for rollback.fail_n. |
| `AH_ENGINE_ROLLBACK_ON_MISMATCH` | `rollback.on_mismatch` | 1 = a binary whose sha256 differs from the one the installer recorded (swapped by hand) and that has never run healthy is rolled back to the known-good binary at the next check. 0 = never roll back on a mismatch alone (a local build you are developing). `accept` records the installed binary as the expected one. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RSS_CAP_KB` | `daemon.rss_cap_kb` | Owner decision 2026-10-23: the restart cap sits at the hard memory limit (mem.global_hard_bytes, 200 MB; 204800 KB = 209715200 bytes), never below it. Memory cap, compared with the figure `daemon.mem_metric` selects (default: the footprint, not the resident set); above it the daemon drains and exits cleanly and the next call starts a fresh one; 0 = none. The measurement below is of the resident set. Set from measurement, not guessed (DECISIONS.md 1.111, 2026-10-09): on the real-payload replay (2,113 recorded hook calls, unpaced, isolated home) the engine with 16 scripted checks sits at 69 MB after one pass and 78 MB after three (jemalloc, aarch64-apple-darwin), and at 102 MB after one pass with the system allocator (the x86_64-apple-darwin and musl builds, measured as a system-allocator build on this Mac); the live heap is 45-52 MB. The engine before the scripted checks (live4) measured 62 and 68 MB on the same replay, so the previous 64 MB cap (set from a synthetic soak with a 16-18 MB live heap) sat inside the steady state of both: the daemon restarted 4 times in 600 s and the crash-loop breaker sent every hook to Node. The cap sits above the larger figure with room for the slow growth both builds show on repeated passes (about 1.5 MB per 1,000 calls), so only real growth trips it. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RSS_CHECK_MS` | `daemon.rss_check_ms` | How often the watchdog samples resident memory. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RT_DEBOUNCE_MS` | `realtime.debounce_ms` | A changed file is reported once it has been quiet this long, so a burst of writes becomes one report. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RT_MAX_DELAY_MS` | `realtime.max_delay_ms` | A file that keeps changing is still reported at least this often (the ceiling on debounce_ms), so a busy source is never starved. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RT_POLL_MS` | `realtime.poll_ms` | How often a polled directory is listed and its watched files stat'ed, in milliseconds. Only directories that cannot use OS events are polled (9p, drvfs, NFS, SMB, FUSE, a directory that does not exist yet, backend = poll), so this is the detection latency of those: at most this plus debounce_ms. Polling costs CPU in proportion to the files watched divided by this interval. |
| `AH_ENGINE_RULES` |  | Overrides the rules file path. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SCRIPT` | `script.enabled` | 1: a check whose script exists runs the script instead of its compiled port; 0: the compiled port always runs (the parity baseline). |
| `AH_ENGINE_SCRIPT_CUT_AT_DEADLINE` | `script.cut_at_request_deadline` | 1 = a scripted check still running when its request's client stops waiting (client.deadline_ms minus daemon.reply_slack_ms) is interrupted there, and a check not yet started by then is not started: each such entry takes its check's failure policy while the entries answered in time keep the engine's answer, so a loaded machine costs single checks instead of the whole event (before, the reply came after the client had given up). Not counted as a script error. A check whose failure mode is closed (script.failure_mode_by_check) keeps only its own limit on a guard event. 0 = the checks run to their own limits whatever the client's deadline (the Node parity harness sets AH_ENGINE_SCRIPT_CUT_AT_DEADLINE=0 so its daemon answers every case, however loaded the machine). |
| `AH_ENGINE_SCRIPT_EXEC_SCALE` | `script.exec_timeout_scale` | Multiplier on the time every `ah.exec` run and every process listing a script asks for may take (the limit a script asks for, and the longest one, are both multiplied). 1 in production; a test build on a loaded machine raises it so a slow child process is not read as a failure. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SCRIPT_TIME_MS` | `script.time_limit_ms` | SOFT CPU-time limit of one script call (the interpreter thread's own CPU time): a call that used more is logged (script_soft) and counted, and keeps running. The HARD limit that interrupts it is this value times script.time_hard_factor (the call then defers to Node, never a silent allow); script.wall_limit_factor sets the wall-clock backstop from the hard limit. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SESSION` |  | Session id a `proj` write is spooled under; spooled writes keep their order per session (D24). |
| `AH_ENGINE_SESSION_BURST` | `daemon.session_burst` | Token-bucket burst per session. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SESSION_RPS` | `daemon.session_rps` | Sustained requests per second allowed per session; 0 = unlimited. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SETTINGS` |  | Overrides the path of anti-hall's settings.json (default: settings.json in the base directory under the home directory). |
| `AH_ENGINE_SHADOW_REPORT_MS` | `schedule.shadow_report_ms` | Interval of the daily Node-shadow agreement report job; 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_DOWN_N` | `client.slow_down_n` | Consecutive slow (late) daemon replies within client.slow_window_ms after which the daemon is treated as wedged and marked down. A single call that gets no reply in the window never marks it down: it fails open and the next client asks the daemon again. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_FALLBACK_MAX_MS` | `client.slow_fallback_max_ms` | How long, measured from the engine start, a hook call keeps waiting for the daemon's own reply once client.deadline_ms has passed (a daemon that is alive answers late rather than never). The wrapper's watchdog waits the same bound (never past the hook's own timeout), so a delayed block still blocks. A reply that arrives in the window is used as is: the daemon's decision. Nothing by then fails the call open and counts toward client.slow_down_n. A normal or unavailable daemon keeps the short fail-fast budget (client.deadline_ms + client.deadline_slack_ms + client.wrapper_extra_ms). 0 disables the extension. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_WINDOW_MS` | `client.slow_window_ms` | Window in which consecutive slow daemon replies are counted toward client.slow_down_n; a streak older than this starts over. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SNAPSHOT_MS` | `telemetry.snapshot_ms` | Interval of the scheduled metrics snapshot job, which keeps the counters in hot.db and their rollups in archive.db (D51); the daemon also keeps one when it exits. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS` | `client.spawn_lock_ttl_ms` | How old the single-flight daemon spawn lock may get before another client treats it as stale and may try one restart. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_N` | `client.spawn_n` | Daemon starts within the spawn window that count as a crash loop even when the daemon reported no crash (a binary that exits at once reports nothing). Respawning then stops for client.crash_cooldown_s. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_WINDOW_S` | `client.spawn_window_s` | Window in which daemon starts are counted for client.spawn_n. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPILL_OVER_CAP` | `dispatch.spill_over_cap` | 1 = a SessionStart (or any event that cannot block) whose joined additionalContext is over dispatch.context_cap is delivered natively: the hooks' contexts that fit stay inline whole and in hook order, the rest is written to a file under dispatch.spill_dir and a pointer line (dispatch.msg_spill_pointer) names it, so nothing is cut and no Node hook runs. The host would spill an over-cap value itself but keeps only about 2000 characters of it inline. 0 = deliver the join and let the host spill it. Used only when the join is exactly the hooks' contexts joined by dispatch.context_joiner and the file can be written; otherwise the previous answer stands. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPOOL_BACKOFF_MS` | `spool.backoff_ms` | First retry delay; each retry doubles it, up to backoff_max_ms, with random jitter of up to half the delay. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPOOL_DRAIN_MS` | `spool.drain_ms` | Interval of the scheduled spool drain job (it also drains on start and before each project write). |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPOOL_MAX_BYTES` | `spool.max_bytes` | Largest spool; a write that would grow it past this is refused instead of spooled, so the client learns it was not kept. |
| `AH_ENGINE_SPOOL_RETRIES` | `spool.retries` | Retries of a project write before it is spooled (the first attempt is not counted). |
| `AH_ENGINE_STALL_MS` | `daemon.stall_ms` | An accept loop silent for longer than this trips a drain and exit. |
| `AH_ENGINE_START_STALL_MS` | `daemon.start_stall_ms` | How long a starting daemon may take from its start to the accept loop's first round (database open, spool drain, scheduler and wiring start) before the watchdog calls it stalled and restarts it. Longer than daemon.stall_ms because start-up work is not the accept loop and a loaded machine slows it; once the loop has run, daemon.stall_ms applies, and a loop that has returned (a clean drain) is never judged. |
| `AH_ENGINE_STATUSLINE_DEADLINE_MS` | `statusline.total_deadline_ms` | Longest the whole status line run may take, input wait included, in milliseconds. Past it the first line already rendered is printed and the run ends, and every step's own limit (git, base command) is cut to what is left, so a loaded machine costs a late second line, never a status line the host has stopped waiting for. Set it just under the host's own wait. |
| `AH_ENGINE_STUCK_MS` | `daemon.stuck_ms` | A worker that makes no progress on its request for longer than this trips a drain and exit (a hung worker). Progress is a check starting or finishing and the script interpreter running, so a worker a loaded machine only slows down is not stuck; the time without progress is what a blocked host call (a lock, a child process, a disk sync) adds. |
| `AH_ENGINE_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_MS` | `telemetry.flush_ms` | How often the recorder's counters and events are stored in hot.db, and at shutdown. A kill -9 loses at most this much (the data recorded since the last flush). |
| `AH_ENGINE_TELEMETRY_ROLLUP_MS` | `schedule.telemetry_rollup_ms` | Interval of the telemetry rollup job (D78); 0 turns it off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_TEST_HOOKS` |  | When set, the daemon accepts the test-only control verbs (sleep, stall, panic). Never set in production. |
| `AH_ENGINE_THREADS_WINDOW_MS` | `diagnostics.threads_window_ms` | The window of `status --threads`: per-thread CPU % and counters per second are measured over this long. |
| `AH_ENGINE_TICK_MS` | `schedule.tick_ms` | Longest the ticker sleeps between checks; it wakes earlier when a job is due sooner or `schedule run` asks. |
| `AH_ENGINE_TIER_BUDGET_KB` | `tier.budget_kb` | Memory budget of the active key-value items; past it the least recently used item is dropped from memory (SQLite keeps it). |
| `AH_ENGINE_UPDATE_MS` | `engine_update.every_ms` | How often the job starts the updater's automatic check; the script's own daily limit decides whether it does any work. 0 turns the job off. |
| `AH_ENGINE_VERSION` |  | Overrides the version this build reports and compares for handoff (the plugin version in production, arbitrary in tests). |
| `AH_ENGINE_WAIT_FILE` |  | A file the client creates while it waits on the daemon and keeps when the daemon answered BUSY/ERR, so the call is handed to its Node hooks; it removes it when the daemon answered with nothing left for Node to decide (an OK reply whose entries defer to Node hooks keeps it until the call's final result is ready), gave no reply in the wait window, or none was there. The thin client sets it, so that its watchdog can tell a call that is still deciding (give it up to client.slow_fallback_max_ms) from a hung engine (kill at the normal budget). |
| `AH_ENGINE_WATCHDOG_TICK_MS` | `daemon.watchdog_tick_ms` | How often the watchdog thread wakes to look at heartbeats. |
| `AH_ENGINE_WIRE_ACK` | `wire.ack` | 1 = the client asks the daemon for ACK(req)/ACK(res) (retry-safe requests, undelivered verdicts counted, per-phase latency); 0 = the original request/reply exchange, no acks. The client only opts in when the daemon has announced the protocol (wire.caps_file), so an older daemon is never sent an ack-mode request. |
| `AH_ENGINE_WORKERS` | `daemon.workers` | Worker threads evaluating requests. |
| `AH_ENGINE_WRAPPER_DIAG` |  | Test-only: absolute path of a file the thin client appends its diagnostic lines to. Honored only with AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1. Test-only: environment variable naming a file the launcher appends its diagnostic lines to (an absolute path). |
| `AH_ENGINE_WRITE_MS` | `daemon.write_ms` | Time allowed to write a reply. |
| `AH_ENGINE_WRITE_QUEUE` | `storage.write_queue` | Writes that may wait for the writer thread; beyond this a write is refused as busy (the client retries, then spools). |


## Socket protocol

| Name | Request | Reply | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hook` | `V <client-version> E <request env JSON> <hook payload JSON>` | `OK <hook output JSON or empty> \| BUSY \| ERR <reason>` | A hook payload evaluated against the rules and built-in checks. The client half-closes after writing; the reply is always a framed OK, BUSY or ERR, and anything else makes the client run the Node hook. |
| `impact` | `CTL impact [kind=<kind>] [project=<hash>] [recent=<n>] [window=<7d>]` | `OK <impact JSON>` | The impact ledger report as JSON. |
| `metrics` | `CTL metrics [check=<name>] [rollup=<resolution> since=<s>]` | `OK <metrics JSON>` | All metric series as JSON, optionally for one check; with rollup, the stored rollups of one resolution instead. |
| `ping` | `CTL ping` | `OK pong <version> <pid>` | Liveness probe; also how a starting daemon checks that a live one already owns the socket. |
| `project` | `P <cwd> [W <write-id> ]<put\|take\|len\|set\|setex\|get> [args]` | `OK <value> \| ERR <reason> \| BUSY` | A per-project operation on hot.db; the daemon derives the partition from the cwd, so a request cannot name another project's key. A write is answered only after it commits; the optional write id makes it idempotent. |
| `reload` | `CTL reload` | `OK ok` | Re-read the rules file now (it is also re-read on SIGHUP and on change). |
| `schedule` | `CTL schedule list \| run job=<name> \| history [job=<name>] [limit=<n>]` | `OK <schedule JSON>` | The scheduler: the jobs and their schedules, run one now, or the run history. |
| `status` | `CTL status` | `OK <status JSON>` | The daemon's state as JSON, including a headline summary. |
| `stop` | `CTL stop` | `OK ok` | Drain and exit. |
| `telemetry` | `CTL telemetry [summary\|events] [window=<7d>] [kind=<k>] [limit=<n>]` | `OK <telemetry JSON>` | The telemetry summary or its events as JSON, including what the daemon has recorded but not yet flushed (D78). |
| `dispatch` | `D <client-version> <meta JSON: host, event, tool, root> <hook payload JSON>` | `OK <JSON array of [id, verdict, text]> \| BUSY \| ERR <reason>` | The built-in checks of one event's dispatch table, evaluated by the daemon; the client runs the other entries and every deferral as their Node hooks. |

## Checks

A rule selects a built-in check with `"check": "<name>"`; the check's tables, limits and messages are in its defaults file.

Rule fields (JSON): `id`, `events`, `tools`, `field`, `pattern` (regex), `check`, `options`, `action` (deny, warn or context), `message`, `paths`.

| Check | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git` | Port of the git-guard hook: blocks force pushes, remote ref deletion, AI self-credit in commits, handover commits, launcher-directory writes and the same through aliases, runners and heredocs |
| `merge-side-pick` | Advisory: a push after a conflict was resolved by taking one side wholesale, with no test run since. |
| `ship-it-guard` | Opt-in plan gate: blocks edits to hard-risk files with no PLAN.md and advises on files a plan's phases do not declare. |
| `scan-throttle` | Advisory: recommends the background-throttled form of a user-configured heavy scan command. |
| `coordinator-work-guard` | Main-thread work window. PreToolUse: allows subagent Bash calls in the engine and defers the rest (the classification and the block stay with Node). PostToolUse: records the call in the window, nudges once per crossing and folds stale session files, when the call's classification is already known (the Node pre-verdict of the same tool call) or provably not work; otherwise defers. |
| `compact-declaration-guard` | Allows new work unless the current turn may hold a SAFE TO COMPACT declaration; a possible declaration defers to the Node guard, which decides and blocks. |
| `command` | command-guard (PreToolUse on Bash): heavy-command and Bash-write delegation gate; the engine answers the commands allowed in every context and every command of a payload-proven subagent, and defers the rest to the Node hook. |
| `model-routing` | Anti-waste Agent/Task model routing: blocks execution-shaped flagship or inherited generic spawns and advises on routing mismatches. |
| `failure-root-cause-nudge` | Advisory after a failed Bash call: trace the cause before patching; silent for expected exit-1 predicates, interrupts, harness refusals and repeats within a turn. |
| `git-audit` | Advisory after a commit-creating git command: a commit made in the last 15 minutes carries an AI self-credit trailer. |
| `verify-first-subagent` | SubagentStart context: injects the verify-first protocol (compact, or full when context.protocolLevel is full) into every spawned subagent. |
| `verify-first-full` | SessionStart context: injects the verify-first protocol and discipline index for the session, Claude or Codex text. |
| `fable-availability` | SessionStart: records whether a Fable model is available (from the host's model cache) in ~/.anti-hall/fable-availability.json and tells the session when it is. |
| `inbox-read-guard` | Blocks a Read of the raw DevSwarm inbox; a Read of the raw store defers to Node, which probes the wrapper; dormant unless DevSwarm is active. |
| `phase-tracker` | Records each Agent or Task spawn in ~/.anti-hall (the statusline's live swarm bar and the running-agents heartbeat); never blocks. |
| `orch-on-spawn` | Silent unless a spawn-time delivery is pending: answers every case where Node would print nothing; a pending marker takes the claim (a file created only when absent) and sends the full rules; only the retry slot after the claim lease, which needs the transcript scan, defers to Node. |
| `verify-first-orch` | SessionStart orchestration text for the Claude entry: composes the full or compact text (with the workspace-tier rule for a DevSwarm Primary) and keeps the delivery marker (port of verify-first-orch.js --host=claude). |
| `verify-first-orch-codex` | SessionStart orchestration text for the Codex entry (the same hook without --host=claude, so never Claude-confident): composes the full or compact text (with the workspace-tier rule for a DevSwarm Primary) and keeps the delivery marker. |
| `verify-first` | UserPromptSubmit: the short rotating verify-first reminder, deduplicated per session; DevSwarm Primary sessions stay on Node. |
| `idle-agent-sweep` | UserPromptSubmit: lists agents that finished but were never stopped or closed, and the call that ends each. |
| `emit-dedupe-reset` | SessionStart: marks a context loss in the session's emit-dedupe state so the next UserPromptSubmit blocks are re-emitted. |
| `limit-conserve-inject` | UserPromptSubmit: injects the limit-conservation directive while conservation is on or a usage bucket is at the threshold (account-switch guard and emit-dedupe as in Node), else an empty context; defers only what JavaScript could read differently. |
| `auto-handover` | UserPromptSubmit: the threshold fire, the soft advisory, the milestone nag, the latch re-arm and the post-handover gate with its backstop, latch and inferred-window writes as in Node; defers the gate on a prompt with text (Node logs a Jev decision row there) and what JavaScript could read differently. |
| `auto-handover-pause-nag` | Stop: the Stop-side fire with the decisive good-point line, the pause nag (step, quiet window, open tasks, recent spawns, handover freshness) and the re-arm, latch writes as in Node; defers only what JavaScript could read differently. |
| `compact-advice-guard` | Stop: blocks, once per declaration, a final reply that recommends compacting at low context or just after a compact (phrase analysis, latch exception and record as in Node); defers a text with a line terminator other than LF and what JavaScript could read differently. |
| `version-alert` | SessionStart advisory: a newer anti-hall release is available or already mirrored locally; a stale remote cache defers to Node, which starts the refresh. |
| `devswarm-version` | SessionStart advisory: the DevSwarm CLI differs from the verified version (including patch releases); a stale cache requests the native refresh and read-only dependency probe. |
| `claude-cli-version` | SessionStart advisory: the Claude Code CLI drifted by major or minor from the audited version; a stale cache defers to Node, which starts the probe. |
| `repo-self-drift` | SessionStart advisory: docs/KB.md's claimed hook and skill counts differ from disk, or the model KBs were audited too long ago. |
| `defect-nudge` | SessionStart advisory, at most daily: unfinished defect reports (in the anti-hall repository) or rulings on defects this project reported; counts and ages only. |
| `progress-prune` | SessionStart maintenance: archives stale per-session progress files into the history ledger before removing them, and reminds weekly to git-ignore .anti-hall/. |
| `speculation-guard` | Stop gate: blocks once per reply that states something with a hedge word and no evidence or uncertainty flag, asks Jev (speculation, add-block; speculationFramed, relax-block) and records the outcome of the previous block; defers the causal-claim scan, a payload without the reply text and a reply window that would cut a surrogate pair. |
| `speculation-judge` | Stop: the opt-in semantic judge; answers every path without a model call, and asks the Claude CLI judge itself (jev.judgeBackend cli) in the dispatcher process or a one-shot process (the daemon hands the check to the dispatcher, which cannot be made to wait); an Anthropic API call is never made by the engine (counted, the reply is allowed). |
| `claim-ledger` | Stop, never blocks: records the checkable claims of the last reply that no evidence in the session backs; asks the Jev shadow question (claimLedger) for each flag on the shared Jev lane without waiting. |
| `output-verify-guard` | PostToolUse advisory: flags a test-runner output with both a passing and a failing signal; asks the Jev shadow question (outputVerifyGuard) without waiting. |
| `ask-guard` | Advises on or blocks a question put to the user, and notes background agents still in flight. |
| `silent-agent-nudge` | Stop: nudges once per silent background agent (the block text, the nudge state, the stale-build downgrade and the per-session ack of the Node hook) and answers every Stop that would not nudge. |
| `stale-agent-stop-note` | Advisory: a TaskStop on an agent that was sent a message or resumed after its last report. |
| `merge-gate` | Opt-in false-done backstop: answers every Bash call natively, including the block of an auto-merge after an unresolved self-hedge and the Jev shadow ask that goes with a hedge; defers only a relative transcript path, a transcript line the engine cannot parse and a text window that would cut a surrogate pair. |
