| `api-guard` | Fabricated-API guard: answers every call the Node api-guard would allow without probing an interpreter (guard off or skipped, a target that is not Python or JavaScript, code that names no verifiable module or global, a Bash command that names no code file, or whose text cannot hold a verifiable reference or cannot write a file) and defers the rest, so every interpreter probe stays with the Node hook. |
| `edit-guard` | Coordinator delegation gate for Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and Codex apply_patch: blocks a write into the launcher directory for every agent, lets a subagent pass, and decides every main-thread target as the Node edit-guard does (the coordinator allowlist with its symlink and hard-link honesty checks, the trusted per-project allowlist, the harness plan file, the session scratchpad, handover documents, plan mode, DevSwarm child workers and the DevSwarm wording); a call that needs the hook process's own working directory or home defers to the Node hook. |
| `engine-role-guard` | PreToolUse on Bash: refuses an ah-engine command the caller's role may not run, per the roles.matrix (subagent from the payload, workspace child from the environment). |
| `broad-kill-guard` | PreToolUse on Bash, every agent: blocks pkill, killall, `kill -9 -1`, a kill of process group 0 and a kill fed by a name, pattern or port lookup (xargs kill, kill $(pgrep ...)); kill <pid> of an explicit PID is allowed. |
| `queued-wait-guard` | PreToolUse on Bash, subagents only: blocks a build or test command started with run_in_background (run it in the foreground under the lock, where waiting costs nothing) and a sleep or until/while sleep poll loop above the configured seconds. |
| `lane-test-guard` | PreToolUse on Bash, subagents only: blocks suite-scale test commands (cargo test or nextest without a narrowing filter, --workspace, node --test without a file, test.sh, replay and soak runners) unless guards.allowTestSuites is on; cargo check and a filtered single-module test stay allowed. With guards.testPolicy = none it blocks EVERY test-runner command from a subagent (and the main session when guards.testPolicyMainThread is on). |
| `wide-search-guard` | PreToolUse on Bash, every agent (subagents and the main thread): blocks a whole-disk search (find, bfs, fd, rg, ag, ack, grep -r, mdfind without -onlyin) rooted at a forbidden root (/, ~, $HOME, /Users, /Volumes, /home), named or implied by a cd or the working directory, unless guards.allowWideSearch is on or the root is in the allow list; a search under a project directory stays allowed. |
| `switch-notice` | Run by the dispatcher on UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse (an engine-only dispatch row): tells the agent one short line when the session-wide switches change (spawn-usage stop, limit conserve, a guard skip set or expired in skip.json), once per state. Switch guards.upfrontNotice. |
| `engine-role-note` | SessionStart and SubagentStart context: tells the session its role, the engine verbs it may use and where the full guide is (the anti-hall:engine skill). |
| `gh-rt-advisory` | Advisory (UserPromptSubmit, engine-only): tells a session about GitHub edges in its repo, once each: CI went red or green, the pull request was merged, changes were requested (plugin script gh-rt-advisory.js). |
| `devswarm-comms-guard` | Blocks SendMessage to a peer session whose cwd is a DevSwarm workspace while DevSwarm is active, and labels other known targets. |
| `swarm-guard` | Blocks an agent spawn past the spawn-rate cap or under critical memory pressure, and adds the shared-tree advisory to an allowed write-capable spawn that shares a working tree with a running write-capable agent. |
| `jev-weekly-scorecard` | Stays silent when the weekly Jev scorecard notice cannot be due (Jev off, notice off, child workspace, checked within a week); when it is due it builds the 7-day verdicts (the jev-report scorecard), names the first integration whose mode does not yet match its KEEP or REMOVE verdict and stamps the weekly latch; a week whose scorecard could not be built is not consumed. |
| `jev-review-reminder` | SessionStart notices of Jev: the one-time legacy-key notice, the recommend-Jev notice (Jev off) and the review-due line (Jev on), with their state files kept by the engine; answers every case itself. |
| `repair-on-reload` | Stays silent when no repair can start (switch off, subagent turn, skipped, nothing pending at the running version, cooldown); otherwise defers to the Node hook, which takes the lock and starts the detached repair (port of the gates of repair-on-reload.js). |
| `codex-availability` | SessionStart: probes PATH for a real codex executable, records it, folds a Codex job-log usage-limit error into the quota record and tells the session. |
| `codex-quota-detect` | Advisory: records a Codex quota or rate-limit exhaustion reported by a codex:codex-rescue Agent result, once, in the shared availability file. |
| `codex-nudge` | Stop: one soft nudge to get a Codex second opinion after several substantial code edits with no Codex review; defers when Jev is enabled for it. |
| `precompact-snapshot` | PreCompact: writes a mechanical continuation snapshot (git state, task list, last user messages) before compaction and never blocks it. |
| `handover-resume` | SessionStart: points a fresh or compacted session at the newest handover with git facts measured now. |
| `task-lifecycle-log` | Appends one line per TaskCreated/TaskCompleted event to the per-session history ledger and its index. |
| `dispatch-tier` | Asks Jev (dispatchTier, detached) how a new or changed task should be dispatched, once per task text, and keeps the request marker in dispatch-tier-state.json; does nothing while the integration is off. |
| `task-guard` | Stop gate: blocks a Stop while tasks are open (the idle-neglect block when dispatchable work has no running agent, else the generic block), with the loop state, the per-prompt budget and the OMC and live-agent steps aside of the Node hook; hands a Stop whose answer needs the DevSwarm app database to Node. |
| `tasklist-guard` | Stop gate: blocks a Stop after untracked work, tasks stalled in progress or a missing or stale progress file, with the Node hook's loop state, dedupe, cap, handover advisories, stop-policy budget and acknowledgement; answers the quiet Stops, plan mode and the resume-verification nudge with the same file effects. |
| `devswarm-parent-inbox` | DevSwarm Primary prompt hook: answers the silent cases (not a Primary, DevSwarm inactive, switch off, judge child) and every active Primary turn, in a git checkout or not, in the engine: the communication-override reminder through emit-dedupe, the ingest-daemon banners and summary refresh, the mailbox-wake line, the session-drift and maintainer-notice feeds, the live workspace table of the project's summary with its nudges, archive recommendation and not-draining / stale-build labels, the orphaned-mesh, stale-registry and broadcast segments, the Primary's own inbox with the questions it was asked, the screenshot-sync ask and the parked supervisor escalations. A seat conflict still owed its repeat, a setting of the hook set anywhere, an unseen maintainer notice, a row the supervisor's auto-archive owns and the other rare states defer to the Node hook, each cause logged as parent-inbox-defer. |
| `devswarm-child-turn` | DevSwarm child prompt hook: answers the silent cases (not a child workspace, DevSwarm inactive, switch off, judge child) and every active child turn in the engine: the heartbeat (with the git push state in a checkout), the descriptor and registry row under the workspace lock, the fixed reminder block through emit-dedupe, the step plan, unread parent mail and the archive request. An archived workspace, an ingest daemon that is not healthy, mesh-direct unread mail, a store Node would first create and the other rare states defer to the Node hook. |
| `devswarm-child-role` | SessionStart: injects the DevSwarm mesh-only messaging directive and native engine commands for a child workspace or Primary; direct ah-hook events use the active plugin defaults root when the request supplies none. |
| `devswarm-parent-gate` | Stop: the DevSwarm Primary gate (decided in the plugin's engine/logic/devswarm-parent-gate logic file): the early exits, the inert and clean passes (loop state removed), the busy and grace advisories, and the neglect block with its loop state, cap, escalation, waiting-on-human lines and wake line; own unread, pending questions, stale verdicts, a parked escalation and every case it cannot reproduce byte for byte defer to the Node gate before anything is written. |
| `devswarm-child-gate` | DevSwarm child Stop gate: makes a child workspace report to its parent (a heartbeat summary) and drain its parent mail before it stops, within a per-kind block budget; an archived workspace and the shapes it cannot read exactly defer to the Node gate. |
| `devswarm-parent-reply-tracker` | DevSwarm Primary reply tracker: records a direct `devswarm send` (or a send receipt of this turn) as the Primary's reply to that child, so the Stop gate stops counting the child's question as unanswered; silent for every other Bash call. |
| `devswarm-child-drain` | DevSwarm child mailbox drain nudge: after a Bash call of a child workspace's main thread, tells the child how many parent messages it has not read (its durable inbox plus the mesh store) and how to drain them, throttled while the count is unchanged. |
| `sibling-sweep` | Stop and SubagentStop reminder: when the reply states the cause of a bug in a fix context and the turn shows no search for other occurrences of the same pattern, asks once per cause to search, fix or list every occurrence and state the search run; counts reminders and follow-through (engine-only, no Node twin). |
| `handover-hygiene` | SessionStart advisory (engine-only, no Node twin): reports handovers that are unindexed, stale, missing a brief or malformed (no front matter, no Situation or Next action, a broken reference) once per distinct problem set; the same script builds the handover brief tree (`ah-engine handovers index\|check\|search`) and runs as the `handovers` scheduled job. |
| `agent-reminders` | Delivers the agent tracker's queued reminders and advisories to the session or subagent that owns them, at its next UserPromptSubmit or PostToolUse (engine-only, advisory). |
| `devswarm-rt-advisory` | Tells the main session which DevSwarm workspace changes (stuck, CI, PR, lifecycle) it has not seen yet; engine-only. |
| `session-end-mcp-reaper` | SessionEnd sweep of orphaned MCP server processes (parent PID 1, MCP command signature, old enough, not service-managed, never test runners), with Node's selection rules and audit log; a user pattern or start time it cannot read exactly defers to Node. |
| `procwatch-advisory` | SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse advisory: leftover processes of ended Claude sessions, agents silent past a threshold, processes of this session using too much CPU or memory, and low free disk; warns only (a kill is a per-class opt-in of the scheduled sweep, a block at critical disk an opt-in setting). |
| `task-tracker` | UserPromptSubmit task-list discipline: the full directive or the short reminder (window, transcript growth, keepalive and burst dedupe as Node keeps them), the open-tasks line, the per-turn DISPATCH NOW line with its Jev tier annotations (the running-agent cover and count proof, the cached verdict, the request for a task with none, the recorded recommendations and their outcomes), the newRequest Jev label of each prompt and the previous turn's demand score; a payload, state file or transcript timestamp in a shape only V8 reads exactly defers to Node. |
| `burn-breaker` | PreToolUse on every tool, subagents only: while the agent tracker holds the hard burn flag (tokens spent since the last commit, finished step, passing check or new file past burn.hard_tokens_no_outcome) blocks every call except commit, push, status commands and SendMessage (the report). |
| `uncommitted-guard` | PreToolUse on Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and apply_patch, subagents only: warns past git.soft_uncommitted_lines and blocks past git.max_uncommitted_lines uncommitted lines in the subagent's worktree (commit first). |

## Settings

Defaults ship with the plugin in `engine/defaults/*.toml` and are read at run time; a numeric setting with an environment variable can be overridden for one process.


### engine.toml / atomic

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `atomic.tmp_suffix` | `.tmp` |  |  | Suffix of the temporary file every atomic state write goes through before the rename (a `.json` target keeps a `.json` ending after it). |

### engine.toml / cli

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cli.help_flags` | `--help, -h` |  |  | The arguments that make an `ah-engine` or `ah-hook` command print its usage and stop before anything runs (checked once, before dispatch; an argument after a bare `--` is never one). |

### engine.toml / client

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `client.breaker_cooldown_s` | `60` | `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S` | s | How long the breaker stays open once tripped. |
| `client.breaker_n` | `5` | `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_N` |  | Engine failures within the window that open the breaker (the client then skips the engine). |
| `client.breaker_window_s` | `60` | `AH_ENGINE_BREAKER_WINDOW_S` | s | Window in which breaker failures are counted. |
| `client.cold_guard_kick_event` | `ColdStartKick` |  |  | Event name of the empty request the wrapper sends to start a cold daemon before a guard event waits for it; it names no hook, so it decides nothing. |
| `client.cold_guard_poll_ms` | `50` |  | ms | Poll interval of the cold-start wait for a guard event (the daemon socket appearing). |
| `client.cold_guard_wait_ms` | `2000` |  | ms | How long a guard event (PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop, SubagentStop) waits for a cold-starting daemon before it is let through with one notice per session; 0 turns the wait off. The engine client keeps the same bound: a guard-event call that still finds no daemon (it starts one, or finds another call starting it) waits for it within this budget and then sends its request once, so it is never answered with nothing while a daemon starts. Prompts and advisories never wait. The wait never exceeds what the hook's own timeout leaves after the engine attempt. It is one absolute deadline: the kick, its kill grace and the socket poll all end within it, so a cold guard call takes at most this plus the normal engine attempt. |
| `client.cold_start_poll_ms` | `1` |  | ms | Poll interval while waiting for a cold-started daemon. |
| `client.cold_start_wait_ms` | `40` |  | ms | How long a client with no fallback waits for a cold-started daemon before giving up (prints nothing). |
| `client.crash_cooldown_s` | `1800` | `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_COOLDOWN_S` | s | How long respawning stays stopped after a crash loop. |
| `client.crash_n` | `4` | `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_N` |  | Daemon deaths within the window that stop respawning. |
| `client.crash_window_s` | `600` | `AH_ENGINE_CRASH_WINDOW_S` | s | Window in which daemon deaths are counted. |
| `client.ctl_timeout_ms` | `1500` |  | ms | Deadline for a control exchange (ping, status, reload, stop, project ops). |
| `client.deadline_ms` | `300` | `AH_ENGINE_DEADLINE_MS` | ms | Overall hook-client deadline for one engine exchange (connect, write, read); a hard watchdog thread enforces it so a hung daemon fails open quickly. |
| `client.deadline_slack_ms` | `10` |  | ms | Extra wait for the exchange thread to report after the deadline before the client declares a timeout. |
| `client.down_marker_ttl_ms` | `3000` | `AH_ENGINE_DOWN_MARKER_TTL_MS` | ms | How long other clients skip connecting after one client finds the daemon absent or failed, or hung (client.heartbeat_stale_ms) and not replaced, or after client.slow_down_n consecutive slow replies; this prevents hook pile-ups while a restart is attempted. |
| `client.fallback_poll_ms` | `2` |  | ms | Poll interval of short waits on a child process or a reply (the GitHub runtime, the Jev sweep and the scheduler use it). |
| `client.heartbeat_confirm_ms` | `1000` | `AH_ENGINE_HEARTBEAT_CONFIRM_MS` | ms | How long a stale daemon heartbeat (client.heartbeat_stale_ms) must stay unchanged, by the monotonic clock, before a client ends that daemon. The first stale sample only records a suspicion and fails open; any beat, a new daemon, or a wall-clock jump that only made a moving heartbeat read old resets it. Keep it at most client.down_marker_ttl_ms, so a stopped daemon is replaced by the first call after the down marker expires. |
| `client.heartbeat_poll_ms` | `100` |  | ms | While a hook call waits past its deadline for a late reply, how often it re-reads the daemon's heartbeat (client.heartbeat_stale_ms). |
| `client.heartbeat_stale_ms` | `1500` | `AH_ENGINE_HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS` | ms | A hook call past client.deadline_ms keeps waiting for a late reply (client.slow_fallback_max_ms) only while the daemon's heartbeat (files.heartbeat) is younger than this. Older means the daemon may be stopped or wedged, not slow: the call fails open at once and marks it down (client.down_marker_ttl_ms). One stale sample only raises a suspicion (files.heartbeat_suspect); the client ends that daemon only once the same heartbeat stayed unchanged for client.heartbeat_confirm_ms, and only when it is the pid holding the singleton lock, verified as this engine's daemon, of this state dir, and still the process generation the heartbeat recorded (start time and executable from the operating system, re-read immediately before the signal); single-flight and under the crash-loop rule. Then it starts a new one. A heartbeat that names another pid or is missing counts as alive. Keep it well above daemon.watchdog_tick_ms and below client.slow_fallback_max_ms less client.slow_wait_margin_ms, so a stop is detected within the first slow call. 0 disables the check. |
| `client.max_reply` | `2097152` |  | bytes | Largest reply the client reads. |
| `client.max_stdin` | `8388608` |  | bytes | Largest hook payload the client reads from stdin. |
| `client.slow_down_n` | `5` | `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_DOWN_N` |  | Consecutive slow (late) daemon replies within client.slow_window_ms after which the daemon is treated as wedged and marked down. A single call that gets no reply in the window never marks it down: it fails open and the next client asks the daemon again. |
| `client.slow_fallback_max_ms` | `3000` | `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_FALLBACK_MAX_MS` | ms | How long, measured from the engine start, a hook call keeps waiting for the daemon's own reply once client.deadline_ms has passed (a daemon that is alive answers late rather than never). The wrapper's watchdog waits the same bound (never past the hook's own timeout), so a delayed block still blocks. A reply that arrives in the window is used as is: the daemon's decision. Nothing by then fails the call open and counts toward client.slow_down_n. A normal or unavailable daemon keeps the short fail-fast budget (client.deadline_ms + client.deadline_slack_ms + client.wrapper_extra_ms). 0 disables the extension. |
| `client.slow_wait_margin_ms` | `400` |  | ms | How much earlier than the wrapper's watchdog (client.slow_fallback_max_ms from the engine start) the client stops waiting for a late daemon reply, so the client fails open and counts the slow call itself instead of being killed by the watchdog first. Covers the client's own start-up before it begins to wait. |
| `client.slow_window_ms` | `10000` | `AH_ENGINE_SLOW_WINDOW_MS` | ms | Window in which consecutive slow daemon replies are counted toward client.slow_down_n; a streak older than this starts over. |
| `client.spawn_lock_ttl_ms` | `3000` | `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_LOCK_TTL_MS` | ms | How old the single-flight daemon spawn lock may get before another client treats it as stale and may try one restart. |
| `client.spawn_n` | `6` | `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_N` |  | Daemon starts within the spawn window that count as a crash loop even when the daemon reported no crash (a binary that exits at once reports nothing). Respawning then stops for client.crash_cooldown_s. |
| `client.spawn_window_s` | `60` | `AH_ENGINE_SPAWN_WINDOW_S` | s | Window in which daemon starts are counted for client.spawn_n. |
| `client.wrapper_default_timeout_s` | `10` |  | s | Last-resort hook budget for the hook launcher (ah-hook) when the fallback list has no row for the event: the event's hook timeout it assumes, which also caps the slow-daemon window and the cold-start wait. |
| `client.wrapper_extra_ms` | `250` |  | ms | Extra shell watchdog budget beyond the client deadline and client slack; this lets the client write the daemon-down marker and release the single-flight spawn lock before the wrapper kills it. |
| `client.wrapper_kill_grace_ms` | `200` |  | ms | How long the hook launcher (ah-hook) waits after SIGTERM to a timed-out engine's process group before it sends SIGKILL. The soft stop lets the client write its markers; the hard stop bounds the call. |
| `client.wrapper_watchdog_poll_ms` | `2` |  | ms | Poll interval for the thin client's millisecond watchdog. |

### engine.toml / compat

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compat.engine_min` | `0.2.0` |  |  | The lowest engine version this plugin supports. An engine older than this is reported by status and doctor; it never blocks a session. |
| `compat.hook_min` | `0.2.0` |  |  | The lowest hook client (ah-hook) version this plugin supports. |
| `compat.log_join` | `; ` |  |  | What joins several mismatch lines in the engine log line. |
| `compat.msg_logged` | `version mismatch (sessions are not blocked): {detail}` |  |  | The one engine log line written when a mismatch is first seen. Placeholder: {detail} (the mismatch lines joined). |
| `compat.msg_mismatch` | `{needer} {needer_version} needs {needs} >= {required}, installed {actual} -> ...` |  |  | One pair that does not hold, as doctor, the engine log and the dashboard show it. Placeholders: {needer}, {needer_version}, {needs}, {required}, {actual}. |
| `compat.msg_ok` | `component versions are compatible ({count} pairs checked)` |  |  | The doctor line when every pair that can be checked holds. Placeholder: {count} (pairs checked). |
| `compat.part_engine` | `engine` |  |  | The name of the engine in compatibility reports. |
| `compat.part_hook` | `hook` |  |  | The name of the hook client in compatibility reports. |
| `compat.part_plugin` | `plugin` |  |  | The name of the plugin in compatibility reports (`status --json` compat.pairs[].needer / needs). |
| `compat.part_web` | `web` |  |  | The name of the dashboard in compatibility reports. |
| `compat.state_mismatch` | `mismatch` |  |  | The state of a compatibility pair whose installed version is below the requirement. |
| `compat.state_ok` | `ok` |  |  | The state of a compatibility pair whose installed version meets the requirement. |
| `compat.state_unknown` | `unknown` |  |  | The state of a compatibility pair where one of the two versions is not known (never a mismatch). |
| `compat.web_min` | `0.2.0` |  |  | The lowest dashboard (ah-web) version this plugin supports. |

### engine.toml / crash

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `crash.closed_pipe_marker` | `Broken pipe` |  |  | Text of the I/O error that marks the closed-pipe panic (see `crash.closed_pipe_prefix`). |
| `crash.closed_pipe_prefix` | `failed printing to std` |  |  | Start of the panic message Rust prints when a write to stdout or stderr fails; with `crash.closed_pipe_marker` it recognises a closed pipe (`ah-engine docs \| head`), which is the reader leaving and not an engine crash. |

### engine.toml / daemon

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `daemon.accept_error_backoff_ms` | `50` |  | ms | Sleep after an accept that failed for a reason other than nothing pending (a full descriptor table, EMFILE): the pending connection would make poll fire again at once, so without it the accept loop spins at full CPU. Kept well under daemon.stall_ms. |
| `daemon.accept_poll_ms` | `200` |  | ms | Accept-loop poll interval while serving. |
| `daemon.bucket_cap` | `4096` |  |  | Most distinct keys one token-bucket map tracks; idle full buckets are dropped first and unknown keys are refused under a key flood. |
| `daemon.close_max_ms` | `30000` |  | ms | Longest a drain's exit timer waits for the database close (the commit of everything queued) once it has started, so a timer that fires during the close cannot lose queued commits. A close wedged longer than this is cut off. |
| `daemon.cpu_check_ms` | `30000` |  | ms | How often the watchdog compares process CPU time to wall time for the sustained-CPU self-check; 0 disables the check. |
| `daemon.cpu_warn_pct` | `80` |  | % | Warn and back off scheduled jobs when daemon CPU over daemon.cpu_check_ms exceeds this percent of one core; 0 disables the warning. |
| `daemon.drain_grace_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | After a drain starts, a worker or loop that has not finished in this long is cut off. |
| `daemon.drain_max_ms` | `10000` |  | ms | Longest a clean drain (handoff, stop, idle exit, SIGTERM) may take before the daemon exits anyway, so a worker stuck while draining can never keep the process (and the singleton lock) alive with its socket already gone. Above daemon.stuck_ms, so the stuck-worker check normally ends such a drain first. |
| `daemon.drain_poll_ms` | `20` |  | ms | Accept-loop poll interval while draining. |
| `daemon.eval_budget_us` | `1000000` | `AH_ENGINE_EVAL_BUDGET_US` | us | HARD thread CPU budget of ONE check: a check that used more than this alone loses its own answer (counted answers_dropped reason `cpu_budget`) and takes its failure policy; the checks after it still run and answer, and the request as a whole is bounded by daemon.request_hard_ms. The SOFT budget (a warning only) is daemon.eval_soft_us. 0 turns the hard budget off. |
| `daemon.eval_soft_us` | `200000` |  | us | SOFT per-request thread CPU budget for rule evaluation: a request that used more is logged (budget_soft) and counted, and every check keeps its answer. The HARD budget is daemon.eval_budget_us. 0 turns the warning off. |
| `daemon.forced_exit_code` | `75` |  |  | Exit status of a forced drain exit (sysexits EX_TEMPFAIL, 75); the next client call starts a fresh daemon. |
| `daemon.healthy_after_s` | `30` | `AH_ENGINE_HEALTHY_AFTER_S` | s | How long the daemon must stay up before its binary is recorded as having run healthy (files.healthy_binary). A binary that dies earlier never earns the record, so a roll-back may replace it. |
| `daemon.idle_check_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | How often the watchdog compares the last request time with idle_exit_s. |
| `daemon.idle_exit_s` | `1800` | `AH_ENGINE_IDLE_EXIT_S` | s | Seconds without any request after which the daemon exits cleanly (the next hook call starts a fresh one, and the scheduler catches up its missed jobs); 0 keeps it resident. Default is 1800 (about 30 minutes), so a daemon with no sessions does not linger forever. A daemon whose state dir, lock file or executable is gone still exits on its own (daemon.orphan_check_ms). |
| `daemon.lock_poll_ms` | `10` |  | ms | Poll interval while waiting for the singleton lock. |
| `daemon.lock_wait_ms` | `1500` |  | ms | How long a starting daemon waits for an outgoing (version-handoff) daemon to release the singleton lock. |
| `daemon.malloc_conf` | `narenas:1,dirty_decay_ms:0,muzzy_decay_ms:0,tcache_max:1024` |  |  | Allocator purge tuning handed to the daemon at start (jemalloc `malloc_conf` syntax): one arena for the four worker threads (less fragmentation) and decay 0 (freed pages go back to the OS at once; the system allocators keep them, which left RSS at 2.5x the live heap). Measured on 1000 mixed calls, this Mac: system allocator 45-48 MB RSS, jemalloc with only decay 0 37 MB, with narenas:1 as well 32 MB (live heap 16 MB), adding tcache:false 27 MB but p50 call latency 10 ms against 6.5-7 ms, so tcache stays on. tcache_max:1024 caches only blocks up to 1 KiB per thread: after the same 220-hook run on the shipped checks and a 300 MB transcript, footprint was 84.3-85.0 MB without it and 75.8-76.0 MB with it (tcache_max 2048: 73.2 against 79.3 on a shorter run, 512: 72.8 but p50 +1.5 ms), hook p50 11.2-13.5 ms without and 11.5-12.0 ms with it, daemon CPU 3.25-3.83 s without and 3.07-3.47 s with it. empty = the allocator's own defaults. A variable the caller already set is not overridden. |
| `daemon.malloc_conf_vars` | `_RJEM_MALLOC_CONF, MALLOC_CONF` |  |  | Environment variables the allocator reads its tuning from (the crate's prefixed name and the plain one). |
| `daemon.malloc_decay_keys` | `dirty_decay_ms, muzzy_decay_ms` |  |  | The decay settings of `daemon.malloc_conf` that a daemon started without the tuning in its environment (a launchd or systemd unit, a replay or test driver) applies to the running allocator; each is also the name of the allocator control under `arenas.` and `arena.<all>.`. `narenas` is not among them: it cannot change once the allocator runs. |
| `daemon.malloc_decay_kind` | `malloc_decay` |  |  | Event-log kind of the line written when the daemon applies (or cannot apply) the allocator decay settings at start. |
| `daemon.malloc_decay_why_error` | `the allocator refused {key} (error {rc})` |  |  | Reason logged when the allocator refused a decay setting. Placeholders: {key}, {rc} (the allocator's error number). |
| `daemon.malloc_decay_why_none` | `daemon.malloc_conf holds no decay setting` |  |  | Reason logged when `daemon.malloc_conf` holds none of `daemon.malloc_decay_keys`. |
| `daemon.malloc_decay_why_system` | `the system allocator is active` |  |  | Reason logged when the decay settings are not applied because the system allocator is active. |
| `daemon.max_request` | `1048576` | `AH_ENGINE_MAX_REQUEST` | bytes | Largest request the daemon reads; the client sends nothing larger (it falls back instead). |
| `daemon.mem_mb` | `512` | `AH_ENGINE_MEM_MB` | MB | Data-segment limit applied with setrlimit; 0 = none. It is a ceiling against runaway allocation, not a budget (the RSS cap is the budget), and Linux enforces it on thread stacks, so it must exceed daemon.workers times git.stack_mb plus headroom or a check thread cannot start. macOS does not support RLIMIT_DATA here, so the daemon reports unsupported and relies on the RSS/footprint cap. |
| `daemon.mem_metric` | `footprint` |  |  | Which figure `daemon.rss_cap_kb` is compared with: `footprint` (the process's own memory: macOS physical footprint, Linux RssAnon + RssShmem; shared and reclaimable file pages are not counted) or `rss` (the kernel's resident set, which also counts shared code pages touched over time and made the daemon restart without a real leak). Falls back to the resident set where the platform has no footprint. |
| `daemon.mem_metric_rss` | `rss` |  |  | The word that selects the resident set for `daemon.mem_metric`. |
| `daemon.nice` | `5` | `AH_ENGINE_NICE` |  | `nice` increment applied to the daemon process. |
| `daemon.orphan_check_ms` | `2000` |  | ms | How often a daemon checks that its state directory, its lock file (same inode) and its executable still exist; non-live daemons also check that their parent process and socket file still exist. Once one is gone it drains and exits, so a daemon whose files were removed under it (a test's temporary dir, an uninstall) never runs on unreachable. |
| `daemon.project_burst` | `400` | `AH_ENGINE_PROJECT_BURST` |  | Token-bucket burst per project. |
| `daemon.project_rps` | `100` | `AH_ENGINE_PROJECT_RPS` |  | Sustained requests per second allowed per project; 0 = unlimited. |
| `daemon.queue` | `16` | `AH_ENGINE_QUEUE` |  | Connections that may wait for a worker; beyond this the daemon answers BUSY and the client falls back. |
| `daemon.read_ms` | `1000` | `AH_ENGINE_READ_MS` | ms | Total time a client has to deliver its request. |
| `daemon.reply_slack_ms` | `50` |  | ms | Time kept back from a request's client deadline (client.deadline_ms, or what a dispatch request says) to write the reply: the inner budgets that could outlast the client's wait (a git call, a Jev consult) are clamped to the deadline minus this, so a slow dependency costs a fallback, not a lost answer. |
| `daemon.request_hard_ms` | `2000` |  | ms | HARD deadline of a request, measured from its arrival (less daemon.reply_slack_ms): the point where a scripted check still running is cut and a check not yet started gets no answer: both take the check's failure policy (script.failure_mode_by_check). The SOFT deadline is client.deadline_ms (past it the request is logged as deadline_soft and counted, nothing is cut). A client whose daemon is alive waits for a late reply up to client.slow_fallback_max_ms less client.slow_wait_margin_ms and uses it, so this must stay below that window. |
| `daemon.rss_cap_kb` | `204800` | `AH_ENGINE_RSS_CAP_KB` | KB | Owner decision 2026-10-23: the restart cap sits at the hard memory limit (mem.global_hard_bytes, 200 MB; 204800 KB = 209715200 bytes), never below it. Memory cap, compared with the figure `daemon.mem_metric` selects (default: the footprint, not the resident set); above it the daemon drains and exits cleanly and the next call starts a fresh one; 0 = none. The measurement below is of the resident set. Set from measurement, not guessed (DECISIONS.md 1.111, 2026-10-09): on the real-payload replay (2,113 recorded hook calls, unpaced, isolated home) the engine with 16 scripted checks sits at 69 MB after one pass and 78 MB after three (jemalloc, aarch64-apple-darwin), and at 102 MB after one pass with the system allocator (the x86_64-apple-darwin and musl builds, measured as a system-allocator build on this Mac); the live heap is 45-52 MB. The engine before the scripted checks (live4) measured 62 and 68 MB on the same replay, so the previous 64 MB cap (set from a synthetic soak with a 16-18 MB live heap) sat inside the steady state of both: the daemon restarted 4 times in 600 s and the crash-loop breaker sent every hook to Node. The cap sits above the larger figure with room for the slow growth both builds show on repeated passes (about 1.5 MB per 1,000 calls), so only real growth trips it. |
| `daemon.rss_check_ms` | `10000` | `AH_ENGINE_RSS_CHECK_MS` | ms | How often the watchdog samples resident memory. |
| `daemon.rules_check_ms` | `200` |  | ms | How often the daemon checks the rules file (and SIGHUP) for a change. |
| `daemon.session_burst` | `200` | `AH_ENGINE_SESSION_BURST` |  | Token-bucket burst per session. |
| `daemon.session_rps` | `50` | `AH_ENGINE_SESSION_RPS` |  | Sustained requests per second allowed per session; 0 = unlimited. |
| `daemon.skip_when_client_gone` | `true` |  |  | Stop running the remaining checks of a request once its client has closed the connection (an ack-mode client keeps it open until it has the verdict, so an end-of-stream means it gave up and nobody reads the reply). Off runs them all. |
| `daemon.spawn_cwd_fallback` | `/` |  |  | The working directory of a daemon whose starter has no usable home directory. Otherwise it starts in the home directory: the directory of the hook that spawned it can be a workspace's worktree that is archived and removed while the daemon, and every job it starts, keeps running. |
| `daemon.spawn_env_allow` | `38 items` |  |  | The only environment variables the daemon (`ah-engine serve`) is started with; everything else of the hook that happened to start it is dropped. A daemon outlives the session that spawned it and serves every later one, so a per-session value left in its environment (the session id, the DevSwarm workspace and role variables, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, the git object-store variables of the hook's repository) would be read for all of them: the first session to spawn it would own it. Per-session values reach the checks only with each request (`request_env.allow`). What is kept is what the daemon and the jobs and tools it starts need as the user: the account and search path (HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL, PATH, the temp directory, locale, TZ, XDG_*), the user's git and GitHub credentials (SSH_AUTH_SOCK, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_HOST, GH_CONFIG_DIR), the engine's own tunables (AH_ENGINE_*, the allocator tuning variables), the plugin root the daemon loads its files from, the user's Jev settings and keys (ANTIHALL_JEV*, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_JEV_*, the gateway keys), and the user-level DevSwarm and maintenance tunables. A trailing `*` matches a prefix. |
| `daemon.spawn_env_deny` | `ANTIHALL_ROLE, ANTIHALL_SESSION_ID, ANTIHALL_CALLER, ANTIHALL_DEVSWARM_SOURCE...` |  |  | Variables the daemon never inherits even when `daemon.spawn_env_allow` matches them by prefix: the ones that name the session, the role or the DevSwarm workspace of whoever started it. Deny wins. |
| `daemon.stall_ms` | `5000` | `AH_ENGINE_STALL_MS` | ms | An accept loop silent for longer than this trips a drain and exit. |
| `daemon.start_fail_exit_code` | `78` |  |  | Exit status when the daemon cannot start (sysexits EX_CONFIG, 78). |
| `daemon.start_stall_ms` | `60000` | `AH_ENGINE_START_STALL_MS` | ms | How long a starting daemon may take from its start to the accept loop's first round (database open, spool drain, scheduler and wiring start) before the watchdog calls it stalled and restarts it. Longer than daemon.stall_ms because start-up work is not the accept loop and a loaded machine slows it; once the loop has run, daemon.stall_ms applies, and a loop that has returned (a clean drain) is never judged. |
| `daemon.stuck_ms` | `8000` | `AH_ENGINE_STUCK_MS` | ms | A worker that makes no progress on its request for longer than this trips a drain and exit (a hung worker). Progress is a check starting or finishing and the script interpreter running, so a worker a loaded machine only slows down is not stuck; the time without progress is what a blocked host call (a lock, a child process, a disk sync) adds. |
| `daemon.thread_restart_backoff_ms` | `100` |  | ms | Sleep before a supervised daemon service thread restarts after a panic. |
| `daemon.thread_restart_max` | `3` |  |  | Panics a daemon service thread may recover from before the daemon requests a clean restart. |
| `daemon.watchdog_tick_ms` | `250` | `AH_ENGINE_WATCHDOG_TICK_MS` | ms | How often the watchdog thread wakes to look at heartbeats. |
| `daemon.worker_wait_ms` | `200` |  | ms | How long an idle worker sleeps on the queue before looking again. |
| `daemon.workers` | `4` | `AH_ENGINE_WORKERS` |  | Worker threads evaluating requests. |
| `daemon.write_ms` | `1000` | `AH_ENGINE_WRITE_MS` | ms | Time allowed to write a reply. |

### engine.toml / defaults_load

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `defaults_load.backup_infix` | `.bak-` |  |  | What separates a defaults file's name from the time stamp of its one-time backup, taken before the first heal writes the file. |
| `defaults_load.lkg_keep` | `3` |  |  | How many last-known-good copies of the defaults (one per engine version, plugin root and shipped content) the state directory keeps; older ones are removed. |
| `defaults_load.msg_fallback` | `defaults {file} {key} rejected ({why}): using the {layer} copy` |  |  | Event-log detail when a defaults file or setting was rejected and another layer answered. Placeholders: {file}, {key} (empty for a whole file), {layer} (lkg or pristine), {why}. |
| `defaults_load.msg_heal` | `defaults {file}: added missing {keys} from the pristine copy (backup {backup})` |  |  | Event-log detail (and `config heal` output) when missing settings were added to an edited defaults file from the pristine copy. Placeholders: {file}, {keys}, {backup} (the backup file, or empty when one already existed). |
| `defaults_load.msg_heal_failed` | `defaults {file}: could not add missing {keys}: {err}` |  |  | Event-log detail (and `config heal` output) when missing settings could not be added. Placeholders: {file}, {keys}, {err}. |
| `defaults_load.msg_heal_held` | `defaults {file}: missing keys {keys}: not written during a deploy hold; the n...` |  |  | Event-log detail when missing settings were not written because a deploy hold (the daemon-down marker) is active: a deploy is replacing the plugin files, and a heal from the binary being replaced would write into the half-synced defaults. Placeholders: {file}, {keys}. |
| `defaults_load.msg_heal_none` | `nothing to heal: the edited defaults have every setting of the pristine copy` |  |  | Printed by `config heal` when no edited defaults file lacks a setting of the pristine copy. |
| `defaults_load.msg_heal_skipped` | `defaults {file}: missing keys {keys}: run `ah-engine config heal` to add them` |  |  | Event-log detail when missing settings were not written because the plugin root is a version-controlled checkout. Placeholders: {file}, {keys}. |
| `defaults_load.msg_lkg_failed` | `could not write the last-known-good defaults: {err}` |  |  | Event-log detail when the last-known-good copy of the defaults could not be written. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `defaults_load.vcs_markers` | `.git` |  |  | Entries (a directory or a file) that mark a version-controlled checkout: when the plugin root or a directory above it holds one, missing settings are never written into its files automatically (only `ah-engine config heal` writes there). |

### engine.toml / discard

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `discard.log_interval_ms` | `60000` |  | ms | A best-effort operation that fails (a state write the engine fails open on) is logged once per reason code in this many milliseconds; repeats inside the window are dropped so a failing disk cannot flood the event log. |
| `discard.log_kind` | `discard` |  |  | The event-log kind of every line a best-effort operation writes when it fails; the reason code is the line's code. |

### engine.toml / env

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env.allocator` | `AH_ENGINE_ALLOCATOR` |  |  | Selects the daemon's allocator: jemalloc (default) or system. The client sets it from `diagnostics.allocator` on the daemon it spawns, unless it is already set; the daemon reads it before its first allocation. |
| `env.auto_update` | `AH_ENGINE_AUTO_UPDATE` |  |  | Read by `ah-hook update --auto`: off, stable or dev overrides the `engine.autoUpdate` setting for one run. |
| `env.bin` | `AH_ENGINE_BIN` |  |  | Test-only: the engine binary the thin client runs instead of the installed one. The thin client ignores it unless AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1 is also set, so a stray value can never turn the safety net into a silent allow. |
| `env.bootstrap` | `AH_ENGINE_BOOTSTRAP` |  |  | Set to 0 or 1 to turn the automatic download of the sha256-pinned engine binary off or on (default off: the explicit install is `sh hooks/install.sh --download`); overrides the `engine.bootstrap` setting. Read by `ah-hook install --auto` and hooks/install.sh. |
| `env.debug` | `AH_ENGINE_DEBUG` |  |  | When set to anything but 0 or empty, turns debug mode (diagnostics.debug_mode) on for that process. |
| `env.dir` | `AH_ENGINE_DIR` |  |  | Overrides the state directory (default: base_dir/state_dir under the home directory). |
| `env.done_file` | `AH_ENGINE_DONE_FILE` |  |  | A file the dispatcher creates once it has dispatched an event and decided its exit code (D87). The thin client sets it, so that an engine exit code of a hook's own (1, say) is told from an engine failure and is not answered by running every hook a second time. |
| `env.fail_open_file` | `AH_ENGINE_FAIL_OPEN_FILE` |  |  | A file the client appends one line to (`<reason> <check>`) for every engine-level fail-open the daemon reported in a reply (GitHub #201). The launcher sets it inside its per-call run directory and counts the lines after the engine exits, so its own stats and log know the call failed open. |
| `env.home` | `HOME` |  |  | Home directory variable. |
| `env.home_alt` | `USERPROFILE` |  |  | Fallback home directory variable (used by the git check when the home variable is unset). |
| `env.hook_engine_min` | `AH_ENGINE_HOOK_ENGINE_MIN` |  |  | Set by the hook launcher (ah-hook) on the engine client it runs, to the lowest engine version that launcher supports. It travels with each request (`request_env.allow`) and the daemon checks it against its own version (`compat` in status). |
| `env.hook_version` | `AH_ENGINE_HOOK_VERSION` |  |  | Set by the hook launcher (ah-hook) on the engine client it runs, to the launcher's own build version. It travels with each request (`request_env.allow`) and the daemon reports the last one it saw as `hook_version` in status and pulse. |
| `env.install_lock_token` | `AH_ENGINE_INSTALL_LOCK_TOKEN` |  |  | Set by an installer (`ah-hook update`) for the integrity check: the token of the install lock it already holds, so recording the expected sha256 runs under the caller's hold instead of waiting on it. |
| `env.live_kit` | `AH_LIVE_KIT` |  |  | Test and operator override: the live kit directory (default: updater.kit_dir below the base directory). |
| `env.nospawn` | `AH_ENGINE_NOSPAWN` |  |  | When set, the client never starts a daemon (tests, and hosts that manage the daemon themselves). |
| `env.plugin_root` | `AH_ENGINE_PLUGIN_ROOT` |  |  | Plugin install directory, used by built-in checks that build override commands (a rule's `options.plugin_root` wins). |
| `env.release_base` | `AH_ENGINE_RELEASE_BASE` |  |  | Test-only: download base URL for the engine binary (http allowed). Honored by `ah-hook install` and hooks/install.sh only with AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1. |
| `env.rules` | `AH_ENGINE_RULES` |  |  | Overrides the rules file path. |
| `env.session` | `AH_ENGINE_SESSION` |  |  | Session id a `proj` write is spooled under; spooled writes keep their order per session (D24). |
| `env.test_hooks` | `AH_ENGINE_TEST_HOOKS` |  |  | When set, the daemon accepts the test-only control verbs (sleep, stall, panic). Never set in production. |
| `env.tmpdir` | `TMPDIR` |  |  | Temporary directory variable, used for the short-path socket fallback. |
| `env.version` | `AH_ENGINE_VERSION` |  |  | Overrides the version this build reports and compares for handoff (the plugin version in production, arbitrary in tests). |
| `env.wait_file` | `AH_ENGINE_WAIT_FILE` |  |  | A file the client creates while it waits on the daemon and keeps when the daemon answered BUSY/ERR, so the call is handed to its Node hooks; it removes it when the daemon answered with nothing left for Node to decide (an OK reply whose entries defer to Node hooks keeps it until the call's final result is ready), gave no reply in the wait window, or none was there. The thin client sets it, so that its watchdog can tell a call that is still deciding (give it up to client.slow_fallback_max_ms) from a hung engine (kill at the normal budget). |
| `env.wrapper_diag` | `AH_ENGINE_WRAPPER_DIAG` |  |  | Test-only: absolute path of a file the thin client appends its diagnostic lines to. Honored only with AH_WRAPPER_TEST=1. |

### engine.toml / files

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `files.advised_dir` | `advised` |  |  | Directory with one empty file per session that has already seen the failure advisory. |
| `files.backups_dir` | `backups` |  |  | Directory inside the state directory that holds backups and pre-restore snapshots (D27); nothing in it is ever deleted by the engine. |
| `files.breaker_until` | `breaker.until` |  |  | Marker holding the time (ms since the epoch) until which the client breaker stays open. |
| `files.cli_crash` | `cli-crash.json` |  |  | Last panic of a non-daemon process (a CLI verb or the hook client). Kept apart from last-crash.json so it never counts as a daemon crash or restart. |
| `files.cold_guard_notice` | `cold-guard.notice` |  |  | Holds the session id that already got the cold-start notice, so the notice is shown once per session (the next session overwrites it). |
| `files.crash_breadcrumb` | `crash-breadcrumb.json` |  |  | Last request/job/check breadcrumb written at boundary entry so an abnormal exit can be reported with context on the next start. |
| `files.crashloop_bin` | `crashloop.bin` |  |  | Holds the size, modification time and sha256 of the binary the crash-loop rule tripped on. A cooldown ends early when the binary is replaced by a different one. |
| `files.crashloop_until` | `crashloop.until` |  |  | Marker holding the time until which respawning is stopped after a crash loop. |
| `files.daemon_down_marker` | `daemon.down.until` |  |  | Short-lived client marker: when a hook client finds the daemon absent or hung, other clients skip connecting until this expires. |
| `files.failure` | `failure.json` |  |  | Last recorded failure, for the once-per-session advisory. |
| `files.fallback_switch` | `fallback.node` |  |  | Marker file (state directory) of the Node fallback switch (the Node backup, stage 2): present = the launcher runs the original Node hooks directly instead of the engine. Written and removed by `ah-engine fallback node\|off`; read by the thin client (`ah-hook`). |
| `files.healthy_binary` | `healthy.binary` |  |  | Holds the sha256 of the engine binary that last stayed up for daemon.healthy_after_s. The integrity check promotes that binary to the known-good copy; a binary with no entry here has never proven itself. |
| `files.heartbeat` | `daemon.heartbeat` |  |  | The daemon's liveness heartbeat: names the daemon's process generation, one field per line (pid, start time and executable as the operating system reports them, and the state dir); the watchdog thread touches its modification time at the start of every daemon.watchdog_tick_ms tick, before any maintenance, apart from request handling. A client past its deadline reads it to tell a slow daemon (heartbeat fresh) from a stopped or wedged one (stale, see client.heartbeat_stale_ms). |
| `files.heartbeat_suspect` | `daemon.heartbeat.suspect` |  |  | Client suspicion carried between hook calls: when a stale heartbeat (client.heartbeat_stale_ms) was first seen (monotonic clock), and which heartbeat (modification time and generation). A later call confirms the hang only when that same heartbeat is still unchanged client.heartbeat_confirm_ms later. |
| `files.integrity_log` | `integrity.log` |  |  | Log of the integrity check (checks, promotions, roll-backs), inside the state directory. |
| `files.last_crash` | `last-crash.json` |  |  | Last panic or stale-run-marker crash report, shown by status and doctor. |
| `files.launcher_drops` | `launcher.drops` |  |  | Count of the log lines the launcher dropped at the hard log size, inside the state directory. |
| `files.launcher_log` | `launcher.log` |  |  | The launcher's bounded failure log, inside the state directory. |
| `files.launcher_spawn_lock` | `launcher.spawn.lock` |  |  | Lock file that lets only one launcher at a time ask for a cold daemon start, inside the state directory. |
| `files.launcher_spawn_log` | `launcher.spawns` |  |  | Times (epoch ms, one per line) of the daemon starts the launcher asked for, inside the state directory; the crash-loop window counts them. |
| `files.log` | `ah-engine.log` |  |  | Event log file name (state directory). |
| `files.reaped_prefix` | `daemon.run.reaped.` |  |  | Prefix of the temporary name a stale run marker is renamed to when it is claimed (the pid is appended). |
| `files.rollback_last` | `rollback.last` |  |  | One line the integrity check writes when it rolls the engine binary back (time, reason, which binary was set aside). Shown by status and doctor. |
| `files.rollback_request` | `rollback.request` |  |  | Written when the crash-loop rule trips on a binary with no healthy history: asks the integrity check to restore the known-good binary. Holds the sha256 of the binary to replace. |
| `files.run_marker` | `daemon.run` |  |  | Written while a daemon runs; a leftover one with a dead pid is logged as one crash. |
| `files.schedules_override` | `schedules.json` |  |  | User overrides of the shipped schedules (D33): JSON, `{"jobs": {"<name>": {...}}}`; read when the daemon starts. |
| `files.slow_streak` | `daemon.slow.streak` |  |  | Client marker holding the count of consecutive slow (late) daemon replies and when the streak began; a normal reply removes it. |
| `files.spawn_lock` | `daemon.spawn.lock` |  |  | Short-lived client single-flight lock: only the client that creates it attempts to restart a missing daemon. |
| `files.spool` | `spool.log` |  |  | The write spool: project writes a client could not deliver, applied by the daemon in order (D24). |
| `files.spool_quarantine` | `spool.quarantine` |  |  | Spool records that could not be parsed or that the store refused for good, kept with their reason, never dropped (D24). |
| `files.starts` | `starts` |  |  | Counter of daemon starts, surfaced as `starts` and `restarts` in status. |
| `files.telemetry_inbox` | `telemetry-inbox.jsonl` |  |  | Events recorded by processes other than the daemon (the hook dispatcher, one-shot commands), one JSON line each, in the state directory; the daemon reads and empties it on every telemetry flush. |
| `files.unreachable_notice` | `unreachable.notice` |  |  | Holds the session id that already got the engine-unreachable notice, so the notice is shown once per session (the next session overwrites it). |
| `files.wrapper_fail_log` | `wrapper.fails` |  |  | Epoch seconds, one per line, of the thin client's engine failures (timeout, signal death, no answer). The integrity check counts them against rollback.fail_n. |

### engine.toml / health

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `health.advised_cap` | `500` |  |  | When more session stamps than this exist, stamps older than advised_expire_s are removed. |
| `health.advised_expire_s` | `172800` |  | s | Age after which a session stamp may be removed. |
| `health.advisory_ttl_ms` | `3600000` |  | ms | A recorded failure older than this no longer produces an advisory. |
| `health.context_events` | `PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SubagentStart` |  |  | Hook events whose output carries `additionalContext`; other events use `systemMessage` when an advisory is merged. |
| `health.crashy_kinds` | `crash, panic, start_fail, watchdog, rss` |  |  | Event kinds that count toward the crash-loop threshold. |
| `health.degraded_kinds` | `defaults_fallback, defaults_heal_skipped` |  |  | Event-log kinds that mark the engine degraded while one is in the degraded window (a defaults file or setting that fell back to the last-known-good or pristine copy, or missing settings that could not be healed). |
| `health.degraded_window_s` | `3600` |  | s | The window over which `status` counts self-restarts and Node fallbacks, and over which a restart marks the engine degraded (shown by `status`, the shadow report and, once per session, in the session context). |
| `health.diag_lines` | `8` |  |  | Event-log lines included in the diagnostic block of a permanent-failure advisory. |
| `health.error_codes` | `3 entries, 3 entries, 3 entries, 3 entries, 3 entries` |  |  | Error-code classification: environment-class codes get a plain self-fix hint (a message key); every other code is a permanent failure that asks for an issue. |
| `health.event_text_max` | `300` |  | chars | Longest kind, code or detail written to one log line (newlines and tabs become spaces). |
| `health.group_breaker` | `breaker` |  |  | Group name of the client breaker in a degraded reason. |
| `health.group_crashloop` | `crashloop` |  |  | Group name of the crash-loop breaker in a degraded reason. |
| `health.group_defaults` | `defaults` |  |  | Group name of a defaults fallback in a degraded reason. |
| `health.group_fail_open` | `fail_open` |  |  | Group name of an unhealthy fail-open window in a degraded reason. |
| `health.group_restart` | `restart` |  |  | Group name of a self-restart in a degraded reason. |
| `health.judged_kinds` | `crashloop, crashloop_reset, reset` |  |  | Event kinds that mark a crash-loop judgement (a trip, a reset by a new binary, an operator reset): crashes and daemon starts logged before the latest of them no longer count toward the next trip. |
| `health.log_batch` | `256` |  |  | Most queued lines the daemon's log thread writes in one append. |
| `health.log_cap` | `65536` |  | bytes | Event log size above which it is trimmed to its last log_keep_lines lines. |
| `health.log_flush_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | Longest the daemon waits at exit for its queued event-log lines to reach the file. |
| `health.log_keep_lines` | `200` |  |  | Lines kept when the event log is trimmed. |
| `health.log_queue` | `4096` |  |  | Lines the daemon's log thread can hold before a worker appends its line itself. The daemon queues every event-log line to one thread that writes them in batches (the per-line stat, lock, open and write were where the four workers waited under load); other processes still append directly. |
| `health.pid_probe` | `ps, -p, {pid}, -o, command=` |  |  | Command used to read a process's command line when checking whether a pid is a live engine: the program, then its arguments with `{pid}` substituted. |
| `health.probe_poll_ms` | `2` |  | ms | How often a running probe command is checked for completion. |
| `health.probe_timeout_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | Longest a pid or memory probe command (health.pid_probe, health.rss_probe) may run; it runs on the hook path, so a wedged one is cut off and reads as no answer. |
| `health.proc_cmdline` | `/proc/{pid}/cmdline` |  |  | Where Linux keeps a process's command line (NUL-separated); read instead of running the pid probe. `{pid}` is substituted. |
| `health.resolved_by_start_kinds` | `defaults_fallback, defaults_heal_skipped` |  |  | Event kinds from `health.degraded_kinds` that a daemon start resolves: one logged before the latest `health.start_kind` event does not count toward degraded. |
| `health.rss_probe` | `ps, -o, rss=, -p, {pid}` |  |  | Command used to read this process's resident set where /proc is unavailable (macOS): the program, then its arguments with `{pid}` substituted. |
| `health.scrub_patterns` | `7 items` |  |  | Patterns removed from anything that goes into a diagnostic: each item is [regex, replacement]. Order matters. |
| `health.serve_arg` | `serve` |  |  | Subcommand a daemon is started with; also how a live engine is recognised in the process list. |
| `health.start_crash_kinds` | `crash, panic` |  |  | Lifecycle event kinds proving the next actual start follows an unrecovered crash. Stale run-marker reaping writes crash, including when the hook client reaped it before serve. |
| `health.start_doctor_line` | `daemon starts (retained): {counts}; last ts={timestamp} reason={reason}` |  |  | The doctor's one-line retained daemon-start summary. Placeholders: counts (JSON), timestamp (last start Unix milliseconds, 0 if none), reason. |
| `health.start_fields` | `6 entries` |  |  | Field names of a start row and its health summary: timestamp is Unix milliseconds; counts cover the retained bounded ring. |
| `health.start_kind` | `start` |  |  | The event-log kind the daemon writes when it starts. A defaults fallback logged before the latest one is answered by that start (the daemon reloads every defaults file then), so it no longer marks the engine degraded. |
| `health.start_lifecycle_kinds` | `start, exit, crash, panic, system_restart` |  |  | Event kinds that delimit daemon lifecycle evidence. The latest event after the prior ring start decides recovery; a clean exit or system reboot supersedes an old crash. |
| `health.start_reason_flag` | `--start-reason` |  |  | The serve argument actual launchers use to identify their trigger. Plain serve defaults to manual. |
| `health.start_reasons` | `6 entries` |  |  | Allowed start reasons: hook client, install/deploy routine, installed service managers, plain serve, and evidenced crash recovery. Crash recovery retains the original trigger in its own field. |
| `health.start_ring_bytes` | `65536` |  | bytes | Maximum bytes read or written for the start ring; oversized or unreadable history is ignored, without preventing daemon startup. |
| `health.start_ring_file` | `starts-reasons.json` |  |  | The bounded JSON ring of actual daemon starts, relative to the engine state directory. Refused duplicate serve processes do not count. |
| `health.start_ring_rows` | `128` |  |  | Maximum retained daemon-start rows; status starts_by_reason counts this retained history. |
| `health.start_ring_write_kind` | `daemon_start_ring_write` |  |  | The discard diagnostic key when writing daemon-start provenance fails; startup continues. |
| `health.system_restart_slack_ms` | `0` |  | ms | How much later than a dead daemon's last sign of life (its newest breadcrumb, or its start) the operating system must have booted for the unclean stop to be reported as a `system_restart` (the machine stopped under it) instead of a `crash`. A margin against clock steps. |

### engine.toml / hook

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hook.agent_keys` | `agent_id, agentId` |  |  | Payload fields that can carry the subagent id, tried in order (recorded with a guard block; absent on the main thread). |
| `hook.event_keys` | `hook_event_name, hookEventName, event` |  |  | Payload fields that can carry the event name, tried in order (Claude Code and Codex send `hook_event_name`). |
| `hook.session_keys` | `session_id, sessionId` |  |  | Payload fields that can carry the session id, tried in order (recorded with a guard block). |
| `hook.tool_keys` | `tool_name, toolName` |  |  | Payload fields that can carry the tool name, tried in order (recorded with a guard block). |
| `hook.warn_prefix` | `anti-hall warning: ` |  |  | Prefix of a `warn` rule's message in agent-visible output. |

### engine.toml / hooks_form

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hooks_form.hooks_dir_word` | `/hooks` |  |  | The directory below the plugin root that holds the hook scripts (stripped to find the plugin root variable of an old command). |
| `hooks_form.host_args_codex` | ` --host codex` |  |  | What a Codex hook command adds after the event. |
| `hooks_form.host_claude` | `claude` |  |  | The name of the Claude host. |
| `hooks_form.host_codex` | `codex` |  |  | The name of the Codex host (the value of --host). |
| `hooks_form.node_word` | `node` |  |  | The program name that marks Node on an entry path. |
| `hooks_form.old_markers` | `ah-hook.sh, ah-run.sh` |  |  | Text in a hook or statusLine command that marks the retired shell wrappers. |
| `hooks_form.repair_done` | `rewrote {n} retired anti-hall hook command(s) in {file}; backup saved beside ...` |  |  | Successful hook launcher migration, after an exclusive backup and atomic replacement. Placeholders: n, file. |
| `hooks_form.repair_id` | `hooks-launcher` |  |  | Report identifier of the unstamped, idempotent retired-hook-launcher migration. |
| `hooks_form.repair_targets` | `2 entries, 2 entries, 2 entries, 2 entries` |  |  | Hook registrations upgraded by update and doctor repair. Only matched anti-hall commands change; home and cwd cover user and project Codex installs, root covers both shipped host registrations. |
| `hooks_form.retired_command_re` | `^\s*(?:exec\s+)?sh\s+"(?P<launcher>(?P<prefix>[^"\r\n]+)/hooks/ah-hook\.sh)"\...` |  |  | Complete retired anti-hall hook command accepted by launcher repair and missing-launcher diagnosis. Captures: launcher, prefix, event, host; arbitrary shell commands are left alone. |
| `hooks_form.statusline_old_form` | `/scripts/ah-run.sh" --stdin statusline` |  |  | Texts that all appear in a statusLine command that runs the retired shell wrapper (after hooks_form.statusline_old_prefix). |
| `hooks_form.statusline_old_prefix` | `sh ` |  |  | How a statusLine command that runs the retired shell wrapper starts. |
| `hooks_form.statusline_template` | `"{client}" statusline` |  |  | The statusLine command in the thin-client form, which the migration (update, doctor --repair) writes in place of one that runs the retired shell wrapper. Placeholder: {client} (the installed ah-hook, absolute). |
| `hooks_form.template` | `[ -x "$HOME/.anti-hall/ah-engine/bin/ah-hook" ] && exec "$HOME/.anti-hall/ah-...` |  |  | A hook command in the direct form: run the installed thin client, else the installer. Placeholders: {event}, {host_args}, {prefix} (the plugin root variable or path). |

### engine.toml / install

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `install.asset_name` | `ah-engine-v{version}-{triple}.tar.gz` |  |  | Name of the release archive for this platform, also its key in the lock's asset table. Placeholders: {version}, {triple}. |
| `install.connect_timeout_s` | `10` |  | s | Connect timeout of the download. |
| `install.cpu_arm` | `arm64, aarch64` |  |  | uname -m spellings of the 64-bit ARM architecture. |
| `install.cpu_arm_name` | `aarch64` |  |  | The architecture part of the release triple for ARM. |
| `install.cpu_x86` | `x86_64, amd64` |  |  | uname -m spellings of the 64-bit x86 architecture. |
| `install.cpu_x86_name` | `x86_64` |  |  | The architecture part of the release triple for x86. |
| `install.curl_cmd` | `14 items` |  |  | The download command. Placeholders: {connect}, {max_time}, {max_size}, {out}, {url}. |
| `install.curl_cmd_test` | `9 items` |  |  | Test-only form of the download command (http and file URLs allowed); used only with the test flag. |
| `install.dir_lock` | `bootstrap.lock` |  |  | Directory (inside the state directory) that keeps two installers from downloading at once. |
| `install.file_attempt` | `bootstrap.attempt` |  |  | Marker of the last failed attempt: <epoch> <version> <asset sha256>. Read by the retry limit. |
| `install.file_log` | `bootstrap.log` |  |  | Install log, inside the state directory. |
| `install.file_marker` | `bootstrap.installed` |  |  | Marker of what the installer put in place: <version> <asset sha256> <engine sha256> [<ah-hook sha256>]. A binary that does not match it (a local build) is never overwritten. |
| `install.file_notice` | `install.notice` |  |  | Holds the id of the session that already got the one notice of hooks/install.sh (inside the state directory). |
| `install.kill_grace_s` | `2` |  | s | How long a timed-out command gets after TERM before it is killed. |
| `install.libc_default` | `gnu` |  |  | The libc part of the Linux triple when musl is not detected. |
| `install.libc_musl` | `musl` |  |  | The libc part of the Linux triple on a musl system. |
| `install.lock_schema` | `1` |  |  | The only ah-engine.lock schema this installer understands. |
| `install.log_keep_lines` | `200` |  |  | Lines the install log keeps when it is cut back. |
| `install.log_max_bytes` | `65536` |  | bytes | The install log is cut back to install.log_keep_lines lines once it is larger than this. |
| `install.max_filesize` | `134217728` |  | bytes | Largest archive the download accepts. |
| `install.max_time_s` | `120` |  | s | Total time limit of the download. |
| `install.member_dir` | `ah-engine-v{version}-{triple}` |  |  | Directory inside the archive that holds the binaries. Placeholders: {version}, {triple}. |
| `install.member_engine` | `ah-engine` |  |  | File name of the engine binary in the archive and in the binary directory. |
| `install.member_hook` | `ah-hook` |  |  | File name of the thin client in the archive and in the binary directory. A release that does not ship it leaves the installed one alone. |
| `install.musl_globs` | `/lib/ld-musl-, /usr/lib/ld-musl-` |  |  | Dynamic-loader paths whose presence means a musl system (a trailing * matches any file name). |
| `install.musl_probe` | `ldd, --version` |  |  | A command whose output names musl on a musl system (searched case-insensitively for install.musl_word). |
| `install.musl_word` | `musl` |  |  | The word install.musl_probe prints on a musl system. |
| `install.os_linux` | `Linux` |  |  | uname -s of Linux (WSL included). |
| `install.os_macos` | `Darwin` |  |  | uname -s of macOS. |
| `install.poll_ms` | `100` |  | ms | How often the installer looks at a running command. |
| `install.prev_suffix` | `.prev` |  |  | Suffix of the copy of the replaced binary (bin/ah-engine.prev, bin/ah-hook.prev). |
| `install.release_base` | `https://github.com/talas9/anti-hall/releases/download` |  |  | Download base URL of the release archives: <base>/<install.release_dir>/<install.asset_name>. https only (the test-only override env.release_base also allows http and file). |
| `install.release_dir` | `ah-engine-v{version}` |  |  | Release directory below the base URL. Placeholder: {version}. |
| `install.retry_s` | `21600` |  | s | After a failed attempt for a version, the next automatic attempt waits this long. |
| `install.rosetta_sysctl` | `hw.optional.arm64` |  |  | macOS sysctl that is 1 on an Apple-silicon machine, even for a process running under Rosetta (which reports x86_64). |
| `install.run_s` | `20` |  | s | Hard limit for one command the installer runs (download, extract, the version check of the new binary); a child that ignores TERM is killed install.kill_grace_s later. |
| `install.setting_key` | `bootstrap` |  |  | Key of the setting that turns the automatic download on (opt-in: absent means off). |
| `install.setting_off` | `false, off, no, 0` |  |  | Spellings of the setting's value that mean off. |
| `install.setting_on` | `true, on, yes, 1` |  |  | Spellings of the setting's value that mean on (booleans and numbers are read as such). |
| `install.setting_section` | `engine` |  |  | Section of the setting that turns the automatic download on. |
| `install.settings_file` | `settings.json` |  |  | The user settings file, inside the base directory (~/.anti-hall). |
| `install.stale_lock_s` | `600` |  | s | install.dir_lock (one installer at a time) held longer than this is taken over. |
| `install.tar_cmd` | `tar, -xzOf, {archive}, {member}` |  |  | The command that writes one member of the archive to stdout. Placeholders: {archive}, {member}. |
| `install.tmp_prefix` | `tmp.` |  |  | Prefix of the installer's scratch directory inside the state directory; <prefix><pid>. |
| `install.triple_linux` | `{cpu}-unknown-linux-{libc}` |  |  | Release triple on Linux. Placeholders: {cpu}, {libc}. |
| `install.triple_macos` | `{cpu}-apple-darwin` |  |  | Release triple on macOS. Placeholder: {cpu}. |
| `install.wget_cmd` | `7 items` |  |  | The download command when curl is not installed. Placeholders: {max_time}, {out}, {url}. |
| `install.wsl_word` | `microsoft` |  |  | Kernel release text (case-insensitive) that marks WSL. |

### engine.toml / launcher

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `launcher.arg_auto` | `--auto` |  |  | The argument the session start gives `ah-hook install` for the automatic form (installs only when the opt-in setting or the environment variable says so). |
| `launcher.arg_builtin` | `--builtin` |  |  | The argument that makes `ah-hook doctor` run its built-in diagnosis even when the engine runs. |
| `launcher.arg_tool_from_payload` | `--tool-from-payload` |  |  | The hook argument that makes the launcher read the tool name from the payload (implied on launcher.nodeback_tool_events). |
| `launcher.cli_doctor_verb` | `doctor` |  |  | The ah-hook command-line verb of the built-in doctor (`ah-hook doctor [--builtin] [--check] [--repair [--dry-run]]`); it hands over to the engine's doctor when the engine runs. |
| `launcher.cli_install_verb` | `install` |  |  | The ah-hook command-line verb that installs the pinned engine (and thin client) from the release archive (`ah-hook install [--lock FILE] [--print-target] [--auto] [-v]`). |
| `launcher.cli_integrity_verb` | `integrity` |  |  | The ah-hook command-line verb that runs the binary integrity check and roll-back (`ah-hook integrity record\|accept\|check\|fail\|status\|lock\|unlock`); the launcher starts itself with it in the background. |
| `launcher.cli_lowercase_verbs` | `1` |  |  | 1: a first argument that starts with a lowercase letter is an engine command (`ah-hook <verb> [args...]` runs `ah-engine <verb> [args...]` by exec); hook event names are PascalCase, so they never match. 0: every first argument is a hook event. |
| `launcher.cli_no_engine_exit` | `127` |  |  | Exit code of `ah-hook <verb>` when no engine can run the command (msg.run_engine_missing goes to stderr; nothing else runs). |
| `launcher.cli_update_verb` | `update` |  |  | The ah-hook command-line verb that runs the updater (`ah-hook update --from FILE \| --channel stable\|dev \| --rollback \| --auto`). |
| `launcher.connect_timeout_ms` | `50` |  | ms | Bound on the launcher's probe connection to the daemon socket (it only tells a live daemon from a stale socket file). |
| `launcher.cpu_hard_s` | `5` |  | s | Hard limit on the launcher's own CPU time (RLIMIT_CPU, whole seconds): past it the launcher stops the engine and lets the hook through. The engine does not inherit it. |
| `launcher.cpu_soft_ms` | `500` |  | ms | Soft limit on the launcher's own CPU time: past it the launcher warns and counts it (at exit). |
| `launcher.crashloop_max` | `5` |  | count | Daemon starts the launcher may ask for inside launcher.crashloop_window_s; past it the launcher stops asking and the hook is let through. |
| `launcher.crashloop_window_s` | `60` |  | s | Window over which the launcher counts the daemon starts it asked for. |
| `launcher.diag_env` | `AH_ENGINE_WRAPPER_DIAG` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable naming a file the launcher appends its diagnostic lines to (an absolute path). |
| `launcher.engine_bin_name` | `ah-engine` |  |  | Name of the engine binary looked up on PATH when none is installed. |
| `launcher.engine_bin_rel` | `bin/ah-engine` |  |  | Path of the installed engine binary below the engine state directory. |
| `launcher.engine_lock_file` | `ah-engine.lock` |  |  | File name, in the plugin root, of the engine lock: when present the session start may bootstrap the engine. |
| `launcher.err_cap_bytes` | `1048576` |  | bytes | Most engine standard error the launcher keeps (same rule as launcher.out_cap_bytes). |
| `launcher.fallback_list_claude` | `hooks/ah-fallback.list` |  |  | Path, inside the Node backup directory (nodeback.node_dir), of the Claude fallback list: the per-event timeouts and the Node hooks the launcher runs while the Node fallback switch is on. |
| `launcher.fallback_list_codex` | `hooks/ah-fallback.codex.list` |  |  | Path, inside the Node backup directory, of the Codex fallback list. |
| `launcher.fallback_map_claude` | `hooks/ah-fallback.map.json` |  |  | Path, inside the Node backup directory, of the Claude fallback map: the dispatch-table id of each fallback command, used to name its shadow-ledger row. |
| `launcher.fallback_map_codex` | `hooks/ah-fallback.codex.map.json` |  |  | Path, inside the Node backup directory, of the Codex fallback map. |
| `launcher.help_doctor` | `usage: ah-hook doctor [--builtin] [--check] [--repair [--dry-run]]\n\nDiagnos...` |  |  | Usage printed by `ah-hook doctor --help`; nothing is checked or repaired. |
| `launcher.help_install` | `usage: ah-hook install [--lock <file>] [--print-target] [--auto] [-v]\n\nInst...` |  |  | Usage printed by `ah-hook install --help`; nothing is installed. |
| `launcher.help_integrity` | `usage: ah-hook integrity <record\|accept\|check\|fail\|status\|lock\|unlock>\n\nRec...` |  |  | Usage printed by `ah-hook integrity --help`; no record or check runs. |
| `launcher.help_selftest` | `usage: ah-hook --selftest [--engine <file>]\n\nRun the thin client's built-in...` |  |  | Usage printed by `ah-hook --selftest --help`; no check runs. |
| `launcher.hosts` | `claude, codex` |  |  | The hosts the launcher serves (the --host values); the first is the default. |
| `launcher.in_process_env` | `AH_ENGINE_DISPATCH_IN_PROCESS` |  |  | Environment variable that, set to 1, runs the engine's dispatch in process; the launcher then ignores the daemon-down marker. |
| `launcher.io_chunk_bytes` | `65536` |  | bytes | Size of the fixed buffer the launcher moves the payload and the engine's output with. Memory stays this size however large the payload is. |
| `launcher.io_drain_ms` | `100` |  | ms | How long, after the engine has exited, the launcher waits for its output pipes to reach end of file before it treats a helper still holding them as a failure. |
| `launcher.knob_doctor_rosetta` | `AH_DOCTOR_ROSETTA` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable naming the file whose presence means Rosetta is installed (honoured only when the test flag is set). |
| `launcher.knob_engine_bin` | `AH_ENGINE_BIN` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces the engine binary (honoured only when the test flag is set). |
| `launcher.knob_fallback_list` | `AH_FALLBACK_LIST` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces the fallback list file. |
| `launcher.knob_fault` | `AH_LAUNCHER_FAULT` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that injects a fault into the launcher (panic, hang, spin or alloc) so its never-panic and hard-limit paths can be tested end to end. |
| `launcher.knob_install_retry_s` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_RETRY_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces install.retry_s. |
| `launcher.knob_install_run_s` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_RUN_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces install.run_s. |
| `launcher.knob_integrity_park` | `AH_INTEGRITY_PARK` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable naming a path prefix; the integrity verbs stop at their race points (`validated`, `before_break`, `after_break`) while the file <prefix>.<point> exists, and create <prefix>.<point>.parked when they arrive. Honoured only when the test flag is set. It makes the install-lock interleavings deterministic. |
| `launcher.knob_kill_grace_s` | `AH_KILL_GRACE_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that sets the kill grace in whole seconds. |
| `launcher.knob_libc` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_LIBC` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that names the libc (gnu or musl) instead of detecting it. |
| `launcher.knob_sweep_age_s` | `AH_HOOK_SWEEP_AGE_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable of the retired shell wrapper's run-directory sweep age (accepted for parity, unused by the thin client). |
| `launcher.knob_timeout_ms` | `AH_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that sets the hook budget in milliseconds. |
| `launcher.knob_timeout_s` | `AH_HOOK_TIMEOUT_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that sets the hook budget in whole seconds. |
| `launcher.knob_uname_m` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_UNAME_M` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces `uname -m` for the platform detection. |
| `launcher.knob_uname_r` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_UNAME_R` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces `uname -r` for the platform detection. |
| `launcher.knob_uname_s` | `AH_BOOTSTRAP_UNAME_S` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces `uname -s` for the platform detection (honoured only when the test flag is set). |
| `launcher.knob_update_api_base` | `AH_UPDATE_API_BASE` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces updater.api_base (honoured only when the test flag is set). |
| `launcher.knob_update_download_base` | `AH_UPDATE_DOWNLOAD_BASE` |  |  | Test-only: environment variable that replaces updater.download_base. |
