### agent_tracker.toml / agent_tracker

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_tracker.act_setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the switch of the stuck-agent action is read from (agents.actOnStuck, default on): on, a child whose nudge was escalated to the owner and is still open past agent_tracker.escalate.act_after_ms is stopped by the means its kind allows (a one-shot Codex run: SIGTERM by the pid that holds its rollout open, re-checked; a DevSwarm workspace: the stop request of `agents send`; a subagent or teammate: a stop request to its live coordinator). Primaries are never acted on. Off, it is only escalated. |
| `agent_tracker.channels` | `7 entries` |  |  | The names of the delivery channels, as they appear in telemetry and the status table. |
| `agent_tracker.claude_cli` | `15 entries` |  |  | The Claude Code CLI as a data source, used only where it beats parsing a transcript. bin: the program name (the environment variable named by env.claude_bin overrides it); version_args: how its version is read; agents_args: the JSON listing of background and interactive sessions (verified: no human-formatted output is ever parsed); verified: the Claude Code version each source was last verified on (a different version re-probes the source before it is trusted, and a failed probe falls back to the transcripts); busy / waiting / blocked / failed: the status words the listing uses; fields: the listing's field names. |
| `agent_tracker.codex` | `10 entries` |  |  | Field names of a Codex rollout file (Codex's format): its first line is a session_meta record whose payload carries the session id, the working directory and the originator (exec_originators: the originators of one-shot runs, which end for good when a turn ends). A turn is marked in the file by a record of one of start_types or terminal_types (marker: how such a type appears in a record, {} = the type); the last mark in the tail decides whether the turn ended. |
| `agent_tracker.cooldowns` | `12 entries` |  |  | Per signal: cooldown_ms (least time between two reminders of the same signal about the same agent), max_per_day (reminders of that signal about that agent per day (UTC), 0 = no cap), once (optional: one reminder per spell the signal stays up, so an unchanged state never repeats), confirm_ticks (optional: ticks the signal must stay up before its first reminder; the limit of the same name when absent). |
| `agent_tracker.cost_limit` | `50` |  |  | The most agents the cost report (`telemetry summary`, key `agent_cost`) lists, most tokens first. |
| `agent_tracker.cost_outcome_units` | `commits + pushes + finished steps + passing test runs + files edited` |  |  | What the cost report counts as an outcome when it divides an agent's tokens (input plus output): the work units the tracker keeps per agent. |
| `agent_tracker.counts` | `7 entries` |  |  | Names of the summary counts in the status JSON. Live = not done. sessions: main and workspace sessions (matches the claude processes in `ps`), subagents, teammates, codex; headless: one-shot runs left out; done_hidden: finished agents older than limits.done_keep_ms left out of the list. |
| `agent_tracker.devswarm_fields` | `18 entries` |  |  | Field names of the DevSwarm descriptor, plan, wake-watch lock and workspace name-cache files the tracker reads (the DevSwarm format); title is the field of the name cache that holds a workspace's display title. |
| `agent_tracker.escalate` | `4 entries` |  |  | The owner's channel and the stop action for stuck agents (src/agents/escalate.rs, used by the nudge loop of agent_nudge.toml). act_after_ms: a nudge that was escalated to the owner and is still open this long after it was first sent runs the action of the child's kind (agent_tracker.act_setting), once. exempt_kinds: kinds never nudged about or acted on (a Primary may run for hours; a DevSwarm Primary's session is exempt by its descriptor prefix agent_tracker.primary_prefix). codex_hung_ms: a one-shot Codex run quiet this long with no terminal record, whose process still holds its rollout open, is hung (a nudge to the session that launched it). term_cmds: the command substrings a process must show to be signalled for a Codex row (one-shot runs only: a shared Codex server holds many sessions' rollouts and never matches). |
| `agent_tracker.escalate_words` | `3 entries` |  |  | The action words the stop action writes to telemetry (field action). |
| `agent_tracker.fmt` | `13 entries` |  |  | Layout of the status table: columns (the header words, in order), the separator between columns, and the word for an absent value. ago_units: the suffixes used for seconds, minutes, hours and days in an age. count_steps / count_units: the divisors and suffixes of a token count in a message (995687 reads 995k, 1500000 reads 1.5M). count_decimal_below_tenths: a count below this many tenths of its unit shows one decimal (1.5M), at or above it whole units (12M). |
| `agent_tracker.guard_inactive_states` | `done, dead, stale` |  |  | Tracker states that conclusively exclude a retained row from live guard counts; absent or unreadable evidence remains unknown. |
| `agent_tracker.guard_job_kind` | `shell` |  |  | Kind of a background shell job exposed to task coverage from the tracker's unfinished bg_ids; jobs expire using the existing limits.bg_bash_ms. |
| `agent_tracker.guard_live_states` | `running, waiting` |  |  | Tracker states that prove a task owner or spawn-ceiling row is live, when its backing transcript is readable and fresh. Finished, dead and stale rows never count as live. |
| `agent_tracker.headless` | `3 entries` |  |  | Headless one-shot runs (a plugin's `claude -p` judge calls, SDK runs) are not agents: they are never tracked, listed or counted. A transcript is headless when its first lines carry key = one of values (the host's entrypoint field: sdk-cli), or when its project directory name contains one of dir_contains (directories only such runs write to). |
| `agent_tracker.kinds` | `6 entries` |  |  | The names of the kinds of agent the tracker follows: main (a Claude Code session), subagent (a subagent or background task of a session), teammate (an in-process teammate of an agent team: a subagent transcript whose meta names it one), codex (a Codex CLI session, from its rollout file), workspace (a DevSwarm workspace's session), heartbeat (an agent known only by its heartbeat file). |
| `agent_tracker.limits` | `58 entries` |  |  | Bounds and thresholds of one tick (milliseconds unless the name says otherwise). active_window_ms: a transcript untouched this long is not tracked. max_agents: most agents followed (newest first). first_read_bytes: how much of the end of a transcript is read the first time it is seen (its totals then count from there). read_max_bytes: most read from one transcript per tick. hung_ms: a running agent with no activity this long is hung; hung_pending_ms: the same while a tool call is still unanswered (a long build or wait is legitimate). loop_window: how many recent tool calls are compared; loop_repeats: identical calls in that window that make a loop; loop_edit_repeats: the same for edits of one file; loop_span_ms: the repeats must fall within this much time of the newest one (the same poll every few minutes is not a loop); error_window, error_repeats: the same for an identical error text. waste_window_ms: the window tokens and progress are compared over; waste_min_span_ms: the least history needed before it is judged; waste_min_tokens: tokens spent in the window below which nothing is wasted; waste_max_progress: progress units in that window at or below which the spend is waste; cache_read_pct: how much a cache-read token counts toward the spend, in percent. drift_min_events: edits and commands seen under the current step before drift is judged; drift_max_overlap_pct: the share of the step's words the recent work may share before it is drift; drift_min_step_words, drift_min_word_len: how small a step or a word is too small to judge; work_words_max: how many recent work words are kept. heartbeat_stale_ms: a running agent heartbeat older than this is stale (the Node watchdog default). monitor_min_bg: background tasks running before a missing wake path is reported; bg_bash_ms: how long a background shell command counts as running. confirm_ticks: ticks a signal must stay up before its first reminder. outcome_timeout_ms: a reminded signal still up after this is recorded as not recovered. fp_min_progress: progress that makes a cleared, un-reminded flag a false positive. samples_max: samples kept per agent. files_max: distinct edited files remembered per agent. series_every_ms: how often an agent's series sample is written to the telemetry store and the series file. series_retention_ms, series_max_bytes: age and size cut of the series file. day_retention: days of daily totals kept. state_max_bytes: a state file bigger than this is discarded (it is only a cache). delivered_max: delivered rows read per tick. text_cap: characters kept of a command, a step or an evidence line. claude_cli_timeout_ms: bound of one `claude` subprocess. probe_ttl_ms: how long a cached capability probe is trusted when the version did not change. cli_list_ttl_ms: how long the host's session listing (`claude agents --json`, one heavy process) is trusted before it is asked again; between listings each agent keeps the host state and gone flag of the last one, and a listing is also taken at once when a main or workspace agent appears that the last listing did not see. stale_lock_ms: a wake-watch lock older than this does not count as armed (the DevSwarm wake-watch rule). queue_keep_ms: a fully delivered queue file is removed after this. idle_open_ms: a subagent or workspace that finished its turn with a task still open and has been silent this long is idle with open work (the wake signal idle_open_task). exit_keep_ms: how long an ended background shell task stays reported by the signal watched_exit. max_codex: most Codex sessions followed (newest first, on top of max_agents). codex_days: how many of the newest day directories of the Codex tree are looked at. codex_running_ms: a Codex rollout written to this recently is running, an older one waits (Codex has no process registry to join). codex_first_line_max: most bytes read of a rollout's first line (its session metadata). rollout_stamp_len: characters of the timestamp and dash between the prefix and the session id in a rollout file name. done_keep_ms: how long a finished agent (state done) stays in the status list after its last output; live agents always show. headless_head_bytes: how much of the start of a transcript is read to find its entrypoint. pid_start_slack_ms: a registered process that started later than its session plus this is a reused pid, not that session. codex_done_after_ms: a one-shot Codex run (`codex exec`) with no output for this long is done even without a terminal record. codex_stale_after_ms: any Codex rollout with no output for this long is done (an interactive session idle that long is over). codex_tail_bytes: how much of the end of a rollout is read to find whether its last turn ended. dead_idle_ms: a subagent, teammate or session with no live process, silent this long, whose parent session is not live either, is dead (one whose transcript or project directory is gone is dead at once). |
| `agent_tracker.live_plan` | `2 entries` |  |  | The live facts of a DevSwarm workspace's work that the roster shows beside its plan (the plan is the workspace's own `heartbeat --step` report and goes stale). dir: the folder under the tracker's directory holding one file per workspace (task-list completions, commits, pushes, merges and deploys, when it last shipped); stale_ms: how far after the plan's last report a commit, push, merge or deploy must be before the roster says the plan is behind. |
| `agent_tracker.meta` | `6 entries` |  |  | Field names of a subagent's meta file (the host's format). task_kind and teammate: a subagent whose task_kind field equals teammate is an in-process teammate of an agent team; name: its team name for it; description: the task description the launcher gave it (a stop of the teammate is answered with this text); team: the team; finished: true once the host recorded the agent as finished. |
| `agent_tracker.native_wake` | `5 entries` |  |  | The native wake of an idle DevSwarm workspace (`workspace reactivate-child`, run after a mesh send to the workspace and by `agents send`; switched with agents.wakeWatch). idle_ms: how long a running-looking workspace must have been silent before it is woken (one that ended its turn is woken at once); cooldown_ms: the least gap between two wakes of one workspace; timeout_ms: the bound of each hivecontrol call; text_cap: characters of a preview or an error kept; dir: the folder (under the tracker's base) holding each workspace's last-wake stamp. |
| `agent_tracker.no_work` | `5 entries` |  |  | The no_work signal requires a valid transcript scanned from its start through its current end. Partial, truncated or unread scans are unknown and never notify. Rescue wrappers (agent type or Codex job id in a result) are excluded because their work happens elsewhere. max_tools controls the threshold. |
| `agent_tracker.no_work_states` | `4 entries` |  |  | No-work evidence states in agents status: unknown means incomplete scan, excluded a Codex-rescue wrapper, no_work a proven empty finished child, clear otherwise. |
| `agent_tracker.owner_setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the owner-notification switch is read from (agents.ownerNotify, default off): on, routes that name the owner channel append a notice to the owner notices file. |
| `agent_tracker.paths` | `31 entries` |  |  | Where the tracker reads and writes. Relative to the user home unless noted: projects (the Claude Code transcripts), base (the anti-hall directory), dir (the tracker's own directory under base), state, series, reminders (one queue file per agent or session), delivered (what the hook delivered), outbox (reminders for DevSwarm workspaces, for the mesh action layer), notices (owner notices), probe (the cached Claude Code capability probe), heartbeats (the agent heartbeat files, under base), devswarm (the DevSwarm directory, under base), subagents (sub-directory of a session directory that holds its subagent transcripts), sessions (the host's registry of live sessions, one file per process), codex (the Codex session tree: year/month/day directories of rollout files), rollout_prefix (the start of a rollout file name). |
| `agent_tracker.patterns` | `15 entries` |  |  | Regular expressions (Rust syntax, case-insensitive) over a shell command: commit (a git commit), push (a git push, counted by the cost report), guard_fire (a tool result that carries an anti-hall guard block heading, counted by the cost report), test (a test run), test_pass (output that says tests passed), test_fail (output that says they failed), task_created (the result of a task-list create: captures the new task id), bg_started (the result of a background shell command: captures the task id whose end notice is awaited), ci_wait (a command that checks or watches CI), merge (a pull-request merge, counted as an outcome), deploy (a deploy command, counted as an outcome), build (a compile or check: cargo build, check, clippy, or an npm/go/make/flutter build), build_pass (output that shows it finished), build_fail (output that shows it failed). |
| `agent_tracker.primary_prefix` | `primary-` |  |  | The id prefix of a DevSwarm Primary's descriptor. A Primary with no live child is not armed by the DevSwarm wake-watch (its idle-skip), so the tracker does not tell it to; its own wake path is the session wake-watch. |
| `agent_tracker.progress_request_text` | `Progress requested from the dashboard: reply with a short status (what is don...` |  |  | The reminder an agent gets when the dashboard asks it for progress. |
| `agent_tracker.registry` | `9 entries` |  |  | The host's registry of live sessions (agent_tracker.paths.sessions: one JSON file per running process, removed when it exits) as a liveness source: a session whose process is alive is running or waiting, never done, however old its transcript. Fields: pid, session (the session id), cwd, started (ms), status, name. busy / waiting / blocked: the status words (the same words as claude_cli's, plus the registry's own: shell = a shell command is running). A status in none of the lists decides nothing and the transcript does. |
| `agent_tracker.remind_setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the reminder switch is read from (agents.reminders, default on): off, signals are still raised and recorded but nothing is queued for any agent. |
| `agent_tracker.roles` | `2 entries` |  |  | The names of the derived role of a session in the status JSON: primary (it coordinates at least one other agent) and solo (it does not). |
| `agent_tracker.roster` | `7 entries` |  |  | The host's team roster as a liveness source for teammates: <dir>/<team>/<file> lists the members of an agent team (field `members`, each with a `name`); the host removes a teammate when it is stopped or finishes, but writes nothing into the teammate's own transcript, which reads running for as long as it is tracked. A teammate whose meta file names a team and whose name is missing from that team's readable roster, or is listed with a `joined` time later than the agent's start plus rejoin_slack_ms (the name belongs to a newer spawn), is finished. grace_ms: how long a teammate must have been followed before its absence counts (the roster is written at spawn, but a tick may read it between the two writes). A roster that is missing or unreadable decides nothing. |
| `agent_tracker.routes` | `12 entries` |  |  | Where each signal goes, by target name (see agent_tracker.targets). self: the agent itself (its session queue, or the mesh for a DevSwarm workspace); coordinator: the session that launched it; wake: the same session through its wake feed, so an idle coordinator is woken; owner: the owner notices file (only while agents.ownerNotify is on). |
| `agent_tracker.setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the tracker's on/off switch is read from (agents.tracker, default on): off, a tick does nothing. |
| `agent_tracker.signals` | `12 items` |  |  | The signals the tick evaluates, in order. A name not listed here is never raised. |
| `agent_tracker.sources` | `4 entries` |  |  | The names of where an agent's numbers come from (process: a live process in the host's session registry; codex: a Codex rollout file), as they appear in telemetry and the status JSON. |
| `agent_tracker.spam` | `4 entries` |  |  | Spam control: max_per_tick (reminders queued in one tick, all agents), max_pending (undelivered reminders queued for one agent before more are held back), max_per_delivery (reminders put in front of an agent by one hook event), max_text (characters of one reminder). |
| `agent_tracker.states` | `5 entries` |  |  | The names of an agent's states: running, waiting (finished its turn with no tool call open, or the host says it waits for input; a host "busy" over an ended turn is a background shell, not work), done (a subagent that finished), stale (running but its heartbeat or transcript went quiet past the active window), dead (no live process and its project directory or transcript is gone, or silent past limits.dead_idle_ms with no live parent: out of the live list, its flags cleared, nothing deleted). |
| `agent_tracker.stop_request_text` | `Stop requested from the dashboard: finish or park what you are doing, report ...` |  |  | The reminder an agent gets when the dashboard asks it to stop on its own. |
| `agent_tracker.stop_result` | `7 entries` |  |  | How the tracker reads a stop of an in-process teammate in its launching session's transcript. use_type: the block type of a tool call; name / desc: the fields of the launching call that name the teammate and describe its task; result: the entry field holding a tool's structured result; kind: the field of that result naming the task type, teammate: its value for an in-process teammate; command: the field holding the task's description, which the stop's answer repeats. |
| `agent_tracker.summary` | `Delivers the agent tracker's queued reminders and advisories to the session o...` |  |  | One-line description of the agent-reminders check in the generated reference. |
| `agent_tracker.targets` | `5 entries` |  |  | The route targets a signal may name. to: whose session the reminder is for (self: the agent itself; coordinator: the session that launched it, a subagent's parent, the newest active main session for a heartbeat, the agent itself for a main session); via: how it is delivered (queue: the session's reminder queue, delivered by its hook at the next turn, and the mesh outbox for a workspace's parent; wake: the session's wake feed, which its idle wake-watch Monitor turns into a stdout line that wakes it; owner: the owner notices file, only while agents.ownerNotify is on). A new target is a row here, then named in routes. |
| `agent_tracker.tick_verb` | `tick` |  |  | The subcommand the scheduled job `agent_tick` runs. |
| `agent_tracker.tools` | `9 entries` |  |  | Tool names by role: edit (change a file), shell (run a command), agent (launch a subagent), todo (a task list rewrite), task_create (a new task-list item), task_update (a single task update), monitor / cron / wakeup (arm a wake path). |
| `agent_tracker.transcript` | `42 entries` |  |  | Field and value names of the Claude Code transcript lines the tracker reads (the host's own format). |
| `agent_tracker.wake` | `4 entries` |  |  | How long each kind of wake path keeps the session reachable, in milliseconds: monitor (a Monitor without persistent: true, which ends at its own cap), persistent (a persistent Monitor), cron (a CronCreate job), wakeup_slack (added to a ScheduleWakeup's own delay). |
| `agent_tracker.wake_command` | `exec "$HOME/.anti-hall/ah-engine/bin/ah-engine" devswarm wake-watch --auto` |  |  | The Monitor command that arms the DevSwarm wake-watch. It names the stable engine path and no plugin root: the engine finds the plugin itself, and a root pinned to one cached version goes stale at the next update. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_flag_auto` | `--auto` |  |  | The option the plugin's monitor entry passes: the harness started the watcher at session start, so the expected refusals (switched off, no session id, already armed) print nothing. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_poll_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | How often the wake-watch looks at its session's wake feed (a size check of one file), in milliseconds. A quiet session costs no tokens. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_prefix` | `anti-hall wake:` |  |  | The first words of the prompt `workspace reactivate-child` queues. DevSwarm stores that prompt as a direct mesh row from the parent, so the engine recognises a wake row by this prefix and never counts it as mail: not in a workspace's unread count, not in the direct total the wake-watch edge-triggers on. The wake prompt is built from it (`msg.native_wake_prompt`). |
| `agent_tracker.wake_session_env` | `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, ANTIHALL_SESSION_ID` |  |  | The variables that name the session the wake-watch belongs to, in order; the first non-empty one is the key of its wake feed. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the off switch of the session wake-watch is read from (agents.wakeWatch, default on): off, `agents wake-watch` arms nothing (the cron and ScheduleWakeup fallbacks are unaffected) and a main session is no longer reported as unarmed. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_stamp_ms` | `30000` |  | ms | How often the wake-watch renews its armed stamp, in milliseconds; the stamp counts as live for limits.stale_lock_ms. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_verb` | `wake-watch` |  |  | The `ah-engine agents` subcommand that runs the session wake Monitor. |
| `agent_tracker.wake_walk_depth` | `8` |  |  | When no session variable is set (a Monitor's shell has none), how many parent processes the wake-watch walks up to find the process the host registered for a session. |
| `agent_tracker.weights` | `8 entries` |  |  | Progress units each kind of work is worth: commit (a successful git commit), step (a plan or task step completed), test (a test run that passed), file (a file edited for the first time), push (a successful git push), build (a compile or check that finished), merge (a successful pull-request merge), deploy (a successful deploy command). A commit, a push or a finished build also restarts the waste window (agent_waste.toml). |
| `agent_tracker.words` | `3 entries` |  |  | Words left out when a step is compared with the work done (drift), as one list; the split characters that cut a path or command into words. |

### agent_tracker.toml / env

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `env.claude_bin` | `AH_ENGINE_CLAUDE_BIN` |  |  | Overrides the Claude Code program the agent tracker asks for its session listing (tests point it at a stand-in). |

### agent_tracker.toml / job

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job.agent_tick` | `11 entries` |  |  | One agent-tracker tick: read what each agent did since the last tick, raise or clear signals, deliver reminders, record telemetry. Runs as a subprocess so a timeout kills it and anything it started; 0 turns it off. |

### agent_tracker.toml / schedule

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `schedule.agent_tick_ms` | `60000` | `AH_ENGINE_AGENT_TICK_MS` | ms | Interval of the agent_tick job; 0 turns the tracker's ticks off. |

### agent_waste.toml / agent_stall

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_stall.limits` | `7 entries` |  |  | Time-based no-outcome signals of the waste sensor. stalled_call_ms: one tool call (not exempt, not a background command) in flight longer than this, at near-zero CPU, is `stalled_call` (soft level; at stalled_call_ms * hard_factor_pct / 100 it is hard). check_after_ms: a call must be this old before the process table is read for it (so ordinary short calls never cost a `ps`). min_cpu_span_ms: least wall time between two CPU readings before a rate is trusted. idle_pm: CPU at or under this many thousandths of a core counts as idle. no_outcome_ms: a subagent, teammate or workspace with no outcome unit (commit, finished step, passing check, new file) for this long is `no_outcome_time`, whatever it spent (soft; hard at the same factor); no_outcome_other_ms: the same for the kinds not in agent_waste.policy.hard_kinds (main session, Primary), which are only warned. A read-heavy role (agent_waste.relief names) gets no_outcome_ms times relief.divisor_pct / 100. Both signals are 0 = off. |
| `agent_stall.policy` | `1 entries` |  |  | Tool names (lower case) whose calls legitimately run long and are never a stalled_call: spawning and waiting on other agents, monitors, questions to the owner. |
| `agent_stall.procs` | `2 entries` |  |  | The commands that read the process table, as argv. ps: pid, parent pid, instantaneous CPU percent, accumulated CPU time, command, no header. lsof: the open files of one path with their lock flag (fields p pid, c command, f fd, l lock), the path is appended after the `--`. |
| `agent_stall.texts` | `7 entries` |  |  | Reason fragments the stall signals add to the waste reason. Placeholders: {label} (the running call), {min} (minutes), {cpu} (one of the cpu words). |

### agent_waste.toml / agent_waste

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_waste.head` | `4 entries` |  |  | Where a worktree's checked-out commit is read (no process is run): the HEAD file, its `ref: ` prefix, the commondir file of a linked worktree, and packed-refs. A HEAD that moved while the agent's own commit and push counts did not (the coordinator committed for it) is the agent's outcome. |
| `agent_waste.judge_sections` | `4 entries` |  |  | Headings-free section names of the evidence pack sent to the judge (must match the sections of evidence.cfg.agentWaste). |
| `agent_waste.limits` | `14 entries` |  |  | Bounds of one evaluation. window_ms: the rolling window tokens, outcomes and calls are compared over. min_span_ms: the least history in the window before an agent is scored. min_tokens: tokens spent in the window below which nothing is wasted. cache_read_pct: how much a cache-read token counts toward the spend, in percent. readonly_pct: percent taken off the score when every call in the window only looks (scaled by the share that does; see patterns.readonly). eps_pct: the epsilon of the formula, in hundredths of an outcome unit (progress units are those of agent_tracker.weights: commit, step, test, file). judge_cooldown_ms: least time between two judge calls about one agent (a verdict is also trusted for twice this). max_judge_per_tick: judge calls one tracker tick may make, all agents. goal_cap: characters of the goal sent to the judge. call_cap: most recent tool calls summarised for the judge. line_cap: characters of one summarised call. fail_cap: failed commands in the window at which the failing-streak factor is full. min_calls: tool calls in the window below which the ratios are not trusted (they count as zero). evidence_min_tokens: tokens spent in the window below which nothing is waste on the formula alone and no action is ever hard (a silent agent spends nothing: the tracker's hung signal covers it, not the waste sensor). |
| `agent_waste.multipliers` | `5 entries` |  |  | How much each ratio (0 to 1) raises the score, in percent: factor = 1 + weight/100 * ratio. reread: Reads and Greps of something already read in the window. repeat: identical tool inputs. poll: sleep, status and listing loops. wait: time blocked on a lock or a background task. fail: failed commands in the window over fail_cap. |
| `agent_waste.outcome_lifetime` | `lifetime: {commits} commits, {checks} passing checks, {steps} steps done, {fi...` |  |  | Evidence line for the judge: the agent's lifetime outcomes. Placeholders: {commits}, {checks}, {steps}, {files}. |
| `agent_waste.outcome_window` | `window: {outcome} outcome units` |  |  | Evidence line for the judge: the outcome units in the window. Placeholder: {outcome}. |
| `agent_waste.patterns` | `5 entries` |  |  | How calls are classified (the recent-call label is `<Tool> <what>`, matched case-insensitively from its start). readonly: label prefixes of calls that only look (read, search, git history, PR and run status, listing, sampling): investigation, which lowers the score by limits.readonly_pct percent times their share of the calls. reads: tool names that read. poll: label prefixes that poll (sleep, status checks, listing loops). wait: label substrings that wait on a lock or a background task. wait_tools: tool names that wait for a background task. |
| `agent_waste.policy` | `3 entries` |  |  | What a confirmed waste does, by agent kind. hard_kinds: kinds that are escalated to a hard action (the burn breaker may pause or block them); every other kind (the main session and the Primary, Codex sessions, heartbeats) is only warned and the owner is told. waste_verdicts: judge verdicts that count as waste; ok_verdicts: verdicts that clear it. |
| `agent_waste.reason_fmt` | `{tokens_k}k tokens for {outcome} outcome units; re-read {reread}%, repeated {...` |  |  | The one-line reason built from the signals. Placeholders: {tokens_k}, {outcome}, {reread}, {repeat}, {poll}, {wait}, {fail} (percentages for the ratios). |
| `agent_waste.relief` | `2 entries` |  |  | Roles expected to read a lot spend tokens without outcome by design: an agent whose name contains one of these words (case-insensitive) has its score divided by divisor_pct/100. |
| `agent_waste.setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the waste sensor's on/off switch is read from (agents.wasteSense, default on): off, no agent is scored, judged or flagged for waste. |
| `agent_waste.thresholds` | `2 entries` |  |  | Score thresholds, in thousands of tokens per outcome unit after the multipliers: soft (ask the judge, warn if it confirms) and hard (act on the formula alone when the judge is unavailable, and escalate a confirmed verdict). Calibrated so the 2026-10-23 incident pattern (1.5-7.7M tokens in 30 minutes, no commit, many re-reads, queued on a lock) scores far over hard while a productive lane (about 1M tokens, 3 commits, few re-reads) scores far under soft. |
| `agent_waste.words` | `9 entries` |  |  | Words the sensor writes: the source of a decision (judge or formula), the actions (warn, hard) and the telemetry class. |

### agent_waste.toml / lock_watch

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lock_watch.limits` | `6 entries` |  |  | interval_ms: least time between two watchdog passes. min_span_ms: least wall time between two CPU readings of the holder before a rate is trusted. idle_pm: the holder's process tree at or under this many thousandths of a core is idle. idle_after_ms: idle this long, with at least one process waiting on the same lock, raises the alert. renotify_ms: least time between two alerts for one holder. term_after_ms: idle this long, with waiters, before the auto-action (only when the term switch is on). |
| `lock_watch.locks` | `~/.anti-hall/work/cargo-heavy*.lock` |  |  | The shared lock files to watch. A leading `~/` is the home directory; the file name may hold one `*`. |
| `lock_watch.setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the lock-holder watchdog's on/off switch is read from (agents.lockWatch, default on): off, no lock file is watched. |
| `lock_watch.term_setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the watchdog's auto-action switch is read from (agents.lockWatchTerm, default OFF): on, a holder idle for limits.term_after_ms with waiters is sent SIGTERM, by its verified pid (re-checked to still hold the lock right before), never by name. |
| `lock_watch.waiters` | `lockf, flock` |  |  | Names (command basename) of the lock wrapper programs. A process running one of them with the lock path on its command line, that is not the holder or below it, is a waiter. |
| `lock_watch.words` | `5 entries` |  |  | Words the watchdog writes: the telemetry class and events, the wake signal name, and the lock characters of the lsof lock field that mean a held lock. |

### agent_nudge.toml / agent_nudge

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_nudge.answers` | `6 entries` |  |  | The answer words of the nudge verb: stop (the parent stops the child; verified), msg (it redirects or unblocks it; acted when new output follows), snooze (it knows, it is fine, remind later; minutes capped), other (any other reason, required; handled as a snooze with the default time). prose: what a reply in free words is recorded as before the nudgeReply judge classifies it. acted: the parent spawned a replacement for the child (found from its tool calls, counted like a stop). |
| `agent_nudge.cmd` | `"$HOME/.anti-hall/ah-engine/bin/ah-engine" agents nudge` |  |  | The command a nudge tells the parent to answer with (works the same from Claude Code and Codex shells). |
| `agent_nudge.codex_tools` | `8 entries` |  |  | Codex tool names that count for the turn matching, each mapped to the tool word of agent_nudge.match it behaves as (shell commands are checked for the stop and send verbs; send_message to an agent is a message; close_agent a stop; spawn_agent a spawn). A Codex tool not listed is not kept. |
| `agent_nudge.codex_turn` | `14 entries` |  |  | Field and value names of the Codex rollout lines read for the turns of a watched Codex parent (the host's own format): a line of type item holds a payload; a payload of type message with the assistant role has content items of type text_item carrying text; a payload of type call has a name and a JSON string args. |
| `agent_nudge.daemon_uptime_key` | `uptime_s` |  |  | The field of `ah-engine status` that gives the daemon's uptime in seconds (the this-daemon roll-up window starts there). |
| `agent_nudge.dead_gone` | `its transcript or folder is gone` |  |  | Why a child was marked dead: its transcript or folder is gone. |
| `agent_nudge.dead_silent` | `silent with no live parent` |  |  | Why a child was marked dead: silent with no live parent. |
| `agent_nudge.evidence_fmt` | `6 entries` |  |  | The evidence fragments of a nudge, joined by join. idle ({min}), stuck ({step}: the call in flight or the signal's step), waste ({tokens} spent with no outcome), ci_wait (its latest calls check or watch CI: a legitimate wait), judge ({label}, {ref}: the agentHealth verdict and the evidence line it cited). |
| `agent_nudge.health_busy` | `busy` |  |  | The agentHealth label that holds the nudge for a re-check (the child is legitimately busy). |
| `agent_nudge.health_integration` | `agentHealth` |  |  | The Jev evidence integration that judges whether a flagged child is really unhealthy (jev_evidence.toml evidence.cfg). |
| `agent_nudge.kind_words` | `5 entries` |  |  | The word a nudge uses for the child's kind (by tracker kind); other: any kind not listed. |
| `agent_nudge.limits` | `30 entries` |  |  | Windows and caps of the nudge loop (milliseconds unless the name says otherwise). cadence_ms: least time between two nudges about one child while it has no answer (each is a short reminder). window_ms: how long after an answer the engine waits before it verifies it (stop: still running then = said_not_done; msg: no new output then = back to reminding). ignored_escalate: reminders without answer or change before the owner's channel is told. max_reminders: reminders after which the nudge is closed as ignored. snooze_default_min, snooze_min_min, snooze_max_min: the snooze given when none (or other) is asked, the shortest (also given for a reason the nudgeReason judge rates implausible) and the longest, in minutes. snoozes_escalate: snoozes after which the owner's channel is told. walk_max: ancestors tried past a parent that is not live. health_per_tick: agentHealth judge calls one tick may make (a latency bound: each is a model call). health_recheck_ms: a child the judge called busy (or a Codex run with no live process) is looked at again after this. health_calls: recent tool calls sent to the judges. step_cap, name_cap, reason_cap: characters of a step or call, a child name, a stored reason. idle_min_show: minutes without output from which the nudge says so. dead_notice_window_ms: a child that died longer ago than this is not looked at. dead_fresh_ms: a child that died longer ago than this when first marked dead is recorded in telemetry only, no notice. dead_per_target: dead notices one target gets in a tick before they are sent as one summary line. answers_max: answer rows read per tick. log_max: closed nudges kept in the state. top_parents: parents listed in the roll-up's most-ignoring list. turns_max, turn_text_cap: turns of a parent kept for matching (and characters of each). prose_per_tick: nudgeReply calls the turn matching may make per tick. match_name_min: shortest child name (characters) a reply or command may mention it by. match_id_prefix_min: shortest id prefix a tool call may name the child by. ref_len, ref_tries: characters of a nudge's ref token, and attempts to find one no open nudge has. replay_bytes: how far back in an already-read transcript a parent that starts being watched late is read for turns since the delivery. |
| `agent_nudge.match` | `6 entries` |  |  | How the parent's turns after a delivered nudge are matched to it (no verb needed). stop_tools / msg_tools / spawn_tools: tool names whose call on the child counts as stop / msg / acted; shell_tools: tools whose command is checked for the stop and send verbs below; fields: the tool input fields kept as the call's values (command only for shell tools); ref_words: words that make a reply about the nudge when it is the only one open for that parent. |
| `agent_nudge.match_send_cmd` | `agents send` |  |  | The command text that makes a shell command a message to the agent it names. |
| `agent_nudge.match_stop_cmd` | `agents stop` |  |  | The command text that makes a shell command a stop of the agent it names. |
| `agent_nudge.match_text_kind` | `text` |  |  | The kind word of a kept reply turn. |
| `agent_nudge.match_tool_kind` | `tool` |  |  | The kind word of a kept tool-call turn. |
| `agent_nudge.outcomes` | `7 entries` |  |  | The verified outcomes a nudge closes with: acted_stopped (said stop and the child stopped), acted_progress (the child produced new output and its unhealthy signals cleared), finished (the child finished), said_not_done (said stop, still running after the window: recorded, then reminding resumes), ignored (closed after max_reminders without answer or change), snoozed (the state while a snooze runs), child_died. |
| `agent_nudge.outcomes_line` | `commits {commits}, steps done {steps}, passing checks {checks}, files edited ...` |  |  | The outcomes section line sent to the agentHealth judge. Placeholders: {commits}, {steps}, {checks}, {files}. |
| `agent_nudge.paths` | `1 entries` |  |  | Files of the nudge loop, under the tracker's directory: answers (one row per answer the verb recorded). |
| `agent_nudge.reason_integration` | `nudgeReason` |  |  | The Jev evidence integration that rates a snooze or other reason against the child's activity. |
| `agent_nudge.reason_plausible` | `plausible` |  |  | The nudgeReason label that lets the requested snooze stand. |
| `agent_nudge.ref_alphabet` | `abcdefghjkmnpqrstuvwxyz23456789` |  |  | The characters a nudge's ref token is made of (lower case and digits, no look-alikes). |
| `agent_nudge.reply_integration` | `nudgeReply` |  |  | The Jev evidence integration that classifies a prose reply into an answer word. |
| `agent_nudge.setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where the nudge loop's switch is read from (agents.nudge, default on): on, an unhealthy child's signals go to its direct parent as a nudge (the plain reminder routes stay quiet about them); off, the plain reminder routes of agent_tracker.routes deliver them as before. |
| `agent_nudge.sources` | `5 entries` |  |  | Where an answer came from, as telemetry carries it (answer_source): verb (the agents nudge verb; wins), ref (a reply of the parent that starts with the nudge's ref token), tool (the parent's own tool call that stops, messages or replaces the child), prose (a reply of the parent that mentions the child, classified by nudgeReply), none (no answer). |
| `agent_nudge.triggers` | `7 entries` |  |  | Which tracker signals make a child a nudge candidate, and the trigger kind each counts as (hung, idle, loop, waste). Waste signals are raised only with real tokens spent. codex_hung: the kind of a one-shot Codex run quiet past agent_tracker.escalate.codex_hung_ms with no end record and a live process. A signal not listed here never nudges. |
| `agent_nudge.units` | `4 entries` |  |  | Token counts in nudge texts: thousands and millions, and their suffixes. |
| `agent_nudge.unknown_parent` | `unknown` |  |  | How a walked nudge names a direct parent that could not be told. |
| `agent_nudge.verb` | `nudge` |  |  | The `ah-engine agents` subcommand that records a parent's answer to a nudge. |
| `agent_nudge.why_ignored` | `its parent left the reminders unanswered` |  |  | Escalation reason: the parent left the reminders unanswered. |
| `agent_nudge.why_no_parent` | `no live parent or ancestor can take it` |  |  | Escalation reason: no live parent or ancestor. |
| `agent_nudge.why_snoozed` | `its parent keeps snoozing it` |  |  | Escalation reason: the parent kept snoozing. |
| `agent_nudge.words` | `20 entries` |  |  | Words the loop writes: the telemetry class and its events, the reminder signal name (the delivered rows match on it), the delivery path words, the owner-file target, the dead trigger and the roll-up window names. |

### devswarm_act.toml / devswarm_act

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devswarm_act.archive_refused_flag` | `archived` |  |  | A zero-exit archive whose JSON body has this key set to false did not archive anything and counts as a failure. |
| `devswarm_act.archive_retry_re` | `could not confirm` |  |  | A failed archive whose error matches this (case-insensitive) is retried once: the known-flaky terminal confirmation. |
| `devswarm_act.argv_archive` | `workspace, archive, {id}` |  |  | Argv of an archive; `{id}` is the workspace UUID (Node: ['workspace','archive',id]). |
| `devswarm_act.argv_check_merge` | `workspace, check-merge` |  |  | Argv of the informational check run before a merge. |
| `devswarm_act.argv_create` | `workspace, create` |  |  | Fixed head of a create; the owner's own arguments follow unchanged, except the anti-hall flag in devswarm_act.create_strip. |
| `devswarm_act.argv_delete` | `workspace, delete, {id}` |  |  | Argv of a delete (Node: ['workspace','delete',id]). |
| `devswarm_act.argv_merge` | `workspace, merge-into-source` |  |  | Fixed head of a merge; the owner's own arguments follow unchanged. |
| `devswarm_act.argv_title` | `workspace, update-title, -b, {branch}, {title}` |  |  | Argv of the best-effort title follow-up of a create; `{branch}` and `{title}` are the request's. |
| `devswarm_act.argv_version` | `--version` |  |  | Argv of the capability probe. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_default_days` | `7` |  |  | The default window of the audit in days (`--since 7d` or a day count overrides it). |
| `devswarm_act.audit_enabled` | `true` |  |  | The action audit view and its doctor section. On by default: it only reads the ledger, the witness file and the telemetry act/mistake events. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_event_limit` | `20000` |  |  | Most act and most mistake events the audit reads from telemetry. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_failure_warn_pct` | `20` |  |  | The doctor warns for a feature whose finished actions failed or timed out more often than this percentage. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_mismatch_top` | `10` |  |  | How many recent witness mismatches the audit lists. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_mistake_warn_pct` | `5` |  |  | The doctor warns for a feature where more than this percentage of completed actions drew a mistake signal. |
| `devswarm_act.audit_outcomes` | `4 entries` |  |  | Which ledger outcome words map to which telemetry outcome of an `act` event: allow (the action ran and was verified), block (refused or stale or unverifiable), error, timeout. Any other word is `skip`. |
| `devswarm_act.auto_archive_kind` | `auto-archive` |  |  | The kind word of the automatic archive in the Node log's `action` field. |
| `devswarm_act.auto_archive_state_file` | `.anti-hall/devswarm/auto-archive-state.json` |  |  | Node's `auto-archive-state.json` (relative to the home directory): the ids the last sweep owns, read by the parent-inbox nag so it stays quiet for them. The engine writes the same shape after a sweep in mode on. |
| `devswarm_act.automatic_kinds` | `auto-archive, poke, escalate` |  |  | The only actions a trigger without an owner request may start (Node's automatic set: the supervisor's auto-archive and its poke/escalate). Everything else needs an owner request; delete is never automatic. |
| `devswarm_act.caller_env` | `ANTIHALL_CALLER` |  |  | Environment variable naming the caller of a delete. |
| `devswarm_act.create_strip` | `--from-local` |  |  | Arguments removed from a create request before it reaches hivecontrol (anti-hall's own flag; Node: spawn.js `--from-local`). |
| `devswarm_act.deferred_kinds` | `recover, drain, read-messages` |  |  | Actions the engine does not execute and answers with `deferred` (nothing written): `recover` as an act-layer request (the owner verb `ah-engine devswarm recover` is separate: the engine gates it and Node's recovery code does the kill), `drain` and `read-messages` are destructive reads that must be folded into the store in the same step. |
| `devswarm_act.err_chars` | `200` |  |  | Most characters kept of a hivecontrol answer quoted in an error (Node: archive.js slice(0, 200)). |
| `devswarm_act.event_kinds` | `lifecycle, activity, pr` |  |  | The state-change kinds that mark a workspace dirty for the event path. |
| `devswarm_act.events_file` | `dsact.events` |  |  | NDJSON of every automatic archive / nag attempt and every mistake signal: feature, action, target (id, doneHead), the value of each gate, outcome (ok / refused / failed) with reason, latency (state directory). |
| `devswarm_act.feature_names` | `auto-archive, nag` |  |  | The feature words of the telemetry, in the order auto-archive, nag. |
| `devswarm_act.gate_names` | `8 items` |  |  | The auto-archive gates in report order; a gate not blocking is recorded as `pass`. |
| `devswarm_act.git_pushed_args` | `branch, -r, --contains` |  |  | Git arguments (the HEAD is appended) that list the remote branches containing a commit: a non-empty answer means the workspace's HEAD is pushed. |

| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_on` | `on` |  |  | The word that turns the hivecontrol guard on. |
| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_path_env` | `PATH` |  |  | The variable whose directories a bare hivecontrol name is looked up in when the guard resolves it. |
| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_refused` | `hivecontrol refused: '{bin}' resolves to '{resolved}', which is not a test st...` |  |  | Log line when the guard refuses a call. Placeholders: bin, resolved, var. |
| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_root_home` | `{home}` |  |  | The prefix of a root entry that is relative to the home directory. |
| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_root_temp` | `{temp}` |  |  | The root entry that stands for the system temp directory. |
| `devswarm_act.hc_guard_roots` | `{temp}, /tmp, /private/tmp, /var/folders, {home}/.anti-hall/work` |  |  | Scratch directories a stub hivecontrol may live in while the guard is active (a real DevSwarm install is never there). `{temp}` is the system temp dir, `{home}/x` is under the home directory. Symlinks are followed before the check. |

### devswarm_wire.toml / devswarm_rt

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devswarm_rt.act.auto_archive.executor` | `engine` |  |  | Who runs the automatic archive of finished workspaces: engine \| node \| off. The engine honours the Node setting devswarm.autoArchive.{mode,idleMin,maxPerSweep,ignorePings} unchanged. With `engine` the Node supervisor's autoArchive must be switched off for the same machine (ANTIHALL_DEVSWARM_AUTO_ARCHIVE_MODE=off in the supervisor job's environment); the durable auto-archived.json still stops either side from repeating an archive at one HEAD. |
| `devswarm_rt.act.escalate.executor` | `auto` |  |  | Who escalates a stale workspace once its pokes are used up (its descriptor's escalateCommand, once, and the one-time notice to the parent): auto \| engine \| node \| off. Same default and guard as poke. |
| `devswarm_rt.act.poke.executor` | `auto` |  |  | Who pokes a stale workspace (its descriptor's nudgeCommand): auto \| engine \| node \| off. Default auto: the engine once devswarm_sup.mode is `engine` (the engine owns every supervisor duty and the Node supervisor job is off), otherwise node. An explicit `engine` while the Node supervisor still runs is held back by the double-run guard (devswarm_sup.guard_ms). |

### devswarm_wire.toml / devswarm_wire

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `devswarm_wire.role_words` | `main, child, subagent, codex` |  |  | The roles a caller can have, in this order: main (the interactive main session), child (a DevSwarm workspace child), subagent (a spawned agent or any automated caller), codex (a Codex session). |

| `devswarm_wire.transcript_min_interval_ms` | `5000` |  | ms | The least time between two reactions to one workspace's transcript growing (a Jev sweep mark and a stuck re-check). ### actions.toml / actions

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `actions.features` | `2 entries` |  |  | The acting features that record into the log, with the actions and the mistake kinds each can have. The report lists exactly these; a record of another feature is still counted, under its own name. |
| `actions.file` | `actions.ndjson` |  |  | The action log (one JSON line per action, refusal, mistake signal or follow-up result), relative to the engine state directory. |
| `actions.followup_cap` | `500` |  |  | The most pending follow-ups kept per feature (the oldest are dropped first, each with a logged follow-up record that says it expired). |
| `actions.followups_file` | `actions-followups-{feature}.json` |  |  | The pending follow-ups of one feature ({feature} is filled in), relative to the engine state directory: checks made some time after an action to see whether it was a mistake. |
| `actions.msg_mistake_usage` | `usage: ah-engine telemetry actions --mistake <feature> <action> <target> <kin...` |  |  | Printed when `telemetry actions --mistake` lacks its arguments. |
| `actions.read_bytes` | `8388608` |  | bytes | The most bytes of the newest action log the report reads. |
| `actions.report_digits` | `3` |  |  | Decimal places of the success and mistake rates in the report. |
| `actions.rotate_bytes` | `8388608` |  | bytes | The action log is renamed to actions.<epoch ms>.ndjson (never deleted) and a new one started once it is larger than this. |
| `actions.stall` | `5 entries` |  |  | How the stall feature (pokes and escalations of silent workspaces) names itself in the action log and its two mistake signals: a poke after which the workspace showed no new activity, an escalation after which it did. |
| `actions.token_chars` | `-_:#@./` |  |  | The characters besides letters and digits that a target, reason or feature keeps when it goes into a telemetry field (everything else is dropped, so a field never carries free text). |
| `actions.token_max` | `120` |  |  | The most characters of one telemetry field of an action or mistake event. |
| `actions.window_ms` | `604800000` |  | ms | The default window of `ah-engine telemetry actions`; records older than this are not counted. 0 counts everything in the log. |

### devswarm_sup.toml / devswarm_sup

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `devswarm_sup.act_block_outcomes` | `refused` |  |  | The outcome words that count as a refusal (block) in an act telemetry event of the supervisor (a recover request the engine refused). |
| `devswarm_sup.act_duty` | `duty-{duty}` |  |  | The action word of the act telemetry event of one duty's tick outcome ({duty} = the duty name). |
| `devswarm_sup.act_recover_reasons` | `8 entries` |  |  | The reason word of the act telemetry event for each way a recover request is refused (caller, id, request, duplicate, descriptor, max, switched_off, native_refused). |
| `devswarm_sup.act_skip_outcomes` | `skipped` |  |  | The outcome words that count as a skip (not applicable, nothing done) in an act telemetry event of the supervisor; a word in action_success is an allow, one in act_block_outcomes a block, any other an error. |
| `devswarm_sup.action_feature` | `devswarm-supervisor` |  |  | The feature name of the supervisor's action lines. |
| `devswarm_sup.action_kind` | `action` |  |  | The kind of an action line of the action ledger. |
| `devswarm_sup.action_log` | `.anti-hall/logs/devswarm-sup-actions.ndjson` |  |  | The action ledger of the supervisor, one JSON line per action it took (kind = action_kind: feature, action, target, inputs, outcome, reason, latency_ms, action_id) and per mistake signal found later (kind = mistake_kind, naming the action_id), relative to the home directory. Each line also goes to telemetry as a `cmd` event (h = the action, e = the outcome), counted in `ah-engine telemetry summary` under detail.cmd. |
| `devswarm_sup.action_success` | `ok, ran, marked, retired, pruned` |  |  | The outcomes that count as success in telemetry; any other counts as an error (a notice that had to be parked, a write that failed). |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_failed` | `failed` |  |  | The outcome word of a marker that could not be written. |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_left` | `left` |  |  | The outcome word of a marker left in place (the reason is in the ledger row). |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_mark` | `dssup-app-archived-marker` |  |  | The action word of an archived marker the app sync wrote (action ledger, telemetry `cmd` h). Without any Node on the machine the engine writes markers on its own plan; with Node present it still writes only when Node's dry run names the same workspaces. |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_marked` | `marked` |  |  | The outcome word of a marker written. |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_retire` | `dssup-app-retire-marker` |  |  | The action word of a stale marker retire (action ledger). |
| `devswarm_sup.as_action_retired` | `retired` |  |  | The outcome word of a marker retired. |
| `devswarm_sup.as_age_1d` | `86400000` |  | ms | The second age bucket. |
| `devswarm_sup.as_age_1h` | `3600000` |  | ms | The first age bucket of the message gap report. |

| `devswarm_sup.duties` | `7 items` |  |  | The duties of one tick, in order (the order of Node's main(): log rotation, the liveness sweep, reconcile, deferred stage, app sync, retention, housekeeping; auto-archive is the engine's own action layer and poke / escalate its action sweeps). |
| `devswarm_sup.duties_off` | `` |  |  | The diagnostic switch of each duty: a duty named here (log_rotate, verdicts, reconcile, deferred, app_sync, retention, housekeeping, or recover for the on-demand recovery) does nothing, and says so: its record is `disabled` (a recover request is `refused`), logged and counted. Empty (the default): every duty runs natively. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.app_sync` | `2 entries` |  |  | Sync the DevSwarm app state (archived markers, titles, message gaps) into app-state.json and the names cache. Native: one read of the app database per tick, no process on a quiet tick; a marker is written from the engine's own plan. Retiring a stale marker (restoring a descriptor) has no native port and is held. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.deferred` | `2 entries` |  |  | One stage of the deferred post-update sweep per tick (fold-all-stores, heal-orphan-partitions, fold-archived-rows, heal-registry-rows, in rotation), only when its marker says work is pending. The rotation cursor (deferred-sweep-state.json), the marker peek and the stage itself (the engine's recon ports) are native; a stage the engine does not take is held and comes round again. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.housekeeping` | `5 entries` |  |  | Disk hygiene: sweep the reaped-workspace logs and the child-gate files by the doctor's repair rules. Node's housekeeping-sweep-state.json keeps the cool-down. Native: removes only files older than the retention window, one directory level, only the sweep's own suffix. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.log_rotate` | `2 entries` |  |  | Rotate the supervisor log (and the engine's own tick log) to one .1 generation when it passes set_log_rotate_bytes. Native. Only the supervisor's own bounded log is touched. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.reconcile` | `5 entries` |  |  | The reconcile sweep: drain stranded per-worktree queues into the shared store (reconcile) and fold duplicate mesh rows, project by project, natively. The active-workspace probe and start-up sampling of Node's sweep have no native port and are held. Node's state file reconcile-sweep-state.json keeps the cool-down. |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.retention` | `2 entries` |  |  | Bounded growth of the message stores: archive-first tombstoning of old, fully read message bodies (never a row delete; positions and dedupe depend on every row staying). The engine plans twice and writes only when the plans are identical. The journal fold and the archive-cap eviction remove data for good and are owner-gated (rt_fold_alone, rt_cap_alone, both off by default: held). |
| `devswarm_sup.duty.verdicts` | `2 entries` |  |  | The liveness sweep: compute and write every workspace's liveness verdict file natively, send the forced parent notice and re-send parked escalation notices when the engine owns poke and escalate. The per-workspace tail work (Jev blocker label, straying signals) and a workspace the engine cannot prove it decides like Node are held (counted native_unable, named in the record). |
| `devswarm_sup.engine_log` | `.anti-hall/logs/devswarm-supervisor-engine.ndjson` |  |  | The engine's own record of its ticks (one JSON line each), relative to the home directory. Kept apart from the Node log so the engine never trips its own guard. |

| `devswarm_sup.esc_hash` | `escalate:{id}:{since}` |  |  | The notice row's dedupe hash: one row per escalation, whoever sends it how often. |

| `devswarm_sup.esc_skipped` | `skipped` |  |  | The outcome word of a notice that was not built. |

| `devswarm_sup.esc_why_no_worktree` | `no-worktree` |  |  | Why no notice is sent: the workspace has no worktree to name its parent from. |

| `devswarm_sup.gate_duties` | `verdicts, app_sync, retention` |  |  | The duties the input gate applies to (each needs entries in gate_inputs and gate_max_unchanged_ms). An empty list runs every duty on every tick. |
| `devswarm_sup.gate_env_prefix` | `ANTIHALL_` |  |  | Environment variables whose names start with this are part of a gated duty's signature (the supervisor's switches and thresholds are read from them), so a changed switch runs the duty at once. The settings in force (a config reload) and who pokes are always part of it. |
| `devswarm_sup.gate_ignore_suffixes` | `-shm` |  |  | File-name suffixes the gate ignores in a listing: a SQLite -shm index changes whenever any process opens the database, even a reader, and holds no data. |
| `devswarm_sup.gate_inputs` | `3 entries` |  |  | Per gated duty, what its signature covers: appdb (the app database and its -wal), ds-dir:<dir> / ds-tree:<dir> (a directory under the DevSwarm state directory, tree = one level of subdirectories too), home-dir:<dir> / home-tree:<dir> / home-file:<file> (under the home directory). Outputs of the duties are not listed. A duty is only armed by a quiet run: the liveness sweep with a stale workspace, a forced notice or a parked notice keeps running every tick (nudge windows and retries are not file changes). verdicts leaves the heartbeats out on purpose (every working child rewrites its beat every few seconds, so the gate would never skip); a beat is picked up within gate_max_unchanged_ms. |
| `devswarm_sup.gate_max_unchanged_ms` | `3 entries` |  |  | Per gated duty, the longest it goes unrun while its inputs are unchanged (0 = never skipped). | `devswarm_sup.gate_subdir_depth` | `ds-tree, home-tree` |  |  | The gate_inputs kinds that also list one level of subdirectories. |
| `devswarm_sup.guard_ms` | `360000` |  | ms | The Node supervisor counts as running when its log (or the rotated copy) was written within this long. While it runs, the engine's supervisor duties AND the engine's poke / escalate stand down, so two actors never run one duty. Node writes one line per sweep and sweeps at least every 120 s. |
| `devswarm_sup.hk_day_ms` | `86400000` |  |  | Milliseconds in the retention sweep's day. |
| `devswarm_sup.hk_max_depth` | `1` |  |  | How many directory levels below the swept directory the age sweep looks (one: a date-partitioned directory). Bounds the walk against a link loop. |

Every nap is a wake-up of an otherwise idle thread, so a shorter value costs idle CPU for every project; it is also the longest a waiting drain takes to notice a stop. A drain that is working checks the flag between steps (devswarm_ingest.stop_poll_ms is the poll of the stop-side joins). |

Each call is a Node process of the DevSwarm CLI whose CPU (about 70 ms) is its start-up, not its polling, so the pause is what bounds the cost: 30 s halves the calls per minute, and a native message waits at most this long longer (the native queue is the discouraged channel; the mesh is not affected). |

| `devswarm_ingest.transient_cap_ms` | `300000` |  | ms | The longest backoff after a transient failure. |
| `devswarm_ingest.wal_kind` | `monitor` |  |  | The WAL kind of the monitor reader (the file is `<kind>-<repo key>.ndjson`). |
| `devswarm_ingest.wal_prefix_spill` | `spill ` |  |  | The text before the reason when the spill directory cannot be written. |
| `devswarm_ingest.wal_prefix_wal` | `WAL ` |  |  | The text before the reason when the WAL itself cannot be written. |
| `devswarm_ingest.wal_rotate_bytes` | `1048576` |  |  | A WAL at least this big with nothing pending is renamed into the archive. |
| `devswarm_ingest.wal_suffix` | `.ndjson` |  |  | The suffix of a WAL file. |
| `devswarm_ingest.worker_idle_wait_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | How long an idle drain worker blocks on the job queue before it looks at its own stop flag again. A job, a stop message or the queue closing wakes it at once; but a stop message goes to whichever idle worker takes it first, so the worker that was told to retire (a lowered cap) can only learn it by this timeout. Longer means fewer idle wake-ups and a slower retirement. |
| `devswarm_ingest.worker_thread_name` | `ah-ingest-worker` |  |  | The name of a drain worker thread (what `status --threads` and a stack sample call it). |
