### realtime.toml / realtime

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `realtime.backend` | `auto` |  |  | How a watched directory is observed: auto (OS file events: FSEvents on macOS, inotify on Linux; a directory on a filesystem listed in fs_poll_types, or one the OS refuses to watch, is polled instead) or poll (always compare file signatures every poll_ms). An unknown word is read as auto. |
| `realtime.cpu_budget_permille` | `5` |  |  | The CPU the idle watcher may use, in thousandths of one core (5 means 0.5 percent); the benchmark test and the rollout gate compare against it. |
| `realtime.debounce_ms` | `100` | `AH_ENGINE_RT_DEBOUNCE_MS` | ms | A changed file is reported once it has been quiet this long, so a burst of writes becomes one report. |
| `realtime.fs_poll_types` | `14 items` |  |  | Filesystem types whose watched directories are always polled because OS change events do not arrive there (WSL2 /mnt drives report 9p or drvfs; network and FUSE filesystems report no events). A trailing or leading * matches any text. |
| `realtime.ignore_suffixes` | `-shm` |  |  | File-name suffixes a watched directory never reports, in every backend. A SQLite shared-memory index (-shm) is rewritten or has its attributes touched whenever any process opens the database, even a read-only reader, and it never holds data (a commit lands in the database or its -wal): a consumer that watches the directory of a database it reads would otherwise wake itself on every read, in a loop. |
| `realtime.latency_target_ms` | `1000` |  | ms | The detection latency (change to report) the watcher must stay within at the 95th percentile, for OS events and for polled directories alike; the benchmark test and the rollout gate compare against it. |
| `realtime.max_delay_ms` | `1000` | `AH_ENGINE_RT_MAX_DELAY_MS` | ms | A file that keeps changing is still reported at least this often (the ceiling on debounce_ms), so a busy source is never starved. |
| `realtime.max_entries` | `2048` |  |  | The most matching files one watched directory is tracked for. A directory with more reports a rescan signal when it changes, so a huge directory cannot grow the watcher's memory. |
| `realtime.mounts_file` | `/proc/self/mounts` |  |  | The file that lists mounted filesystems with their types on Linux (including WSL2); the longest mount point that holds a watched directory names its filesystem type. macOS asks the system (statfs) instead. |
| `realtime.msg_too_many_files` | `more than {cap} matching files` |  |  | Why a directory is polled instead of watched with events when more files than the cap match; {cap} is `realtime.max_entries`. |
| `realtime.poll_ms` | `750` | `AH_ENGINE_RT_POLL_MS` | ms | How often a polled directory is listed and its watched files stat'ed, in milliseconds. Only directories that cannot use OS events are polled (9p, drvfs, NFS, SMB, FUSE, a directory that does not exist yet, backend = poll), so this is the detection latency of those: at most this plus debounce_ms. Polling costs CPU in proportion to the files watched divided by this interval. |
| `realtime.queue_cap` | `512` |  |  | The most distinct changed files held before they are reported. Past it the held changes are dropped and ONE rescan signal is sent instead (the consumer reconciles everything), so the queue and its output stay bounded however large the storm. |
| `realtime.sqlite_suffixes` | `-wal, -shm, -journal` |  |  | Suffixes of the files SQLite keeps beside a database (write-ahead log, shared memory, rollback journal). Watching a database name also watches the name plus each suffix, because a commit lands in the -wal file and a checkpoint can truncate it. |

### github_rt.toml / github_rt

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `github_rt.advisory_kinds` | `ci_red, ci_green, pr_merged, changes_requested, conflict, ready` |  |  | The edges a session is told about (once per session each): ci_red, ci_green, pr_merged, pr_closed, changes_requested, approved, conflict. Empty turns the advisory off. |
| `github_rt.advisory_max_age_ms` | `1800000` |  | ms | An edge older than this is no longer told to a session. |
| `github_rt.advisory_max_per_prompt` | `3` |  |  | The most edges told in one prompt. |
| `github_rt.advisory_summary` | `Advisory (UserPromptSubmit, engine-only): tells a session about GitHub edges ...` |  |  | One-line description of the gh-rt-advisory check in the generated reference. |
| `github_rt.assumed_limit` | `5000` |  |  | The hourly limit assumed until a response has reported the real one. |
| `github_rt.auth_retry_ms` | `1800000` |  | ms | After gh said it is not logged in, how long before it is tried again. |
| `github_rt.backoff_max_doublings` | `20` |  |  | The backoff doubles at most this many times before backoff_max_ms, so the shift cannot overflow. |
| `github_rt.backoff_max_ms` | `3600000` |  | ms | The longest backoff wait, and the longest Retry-After honoured. |
| `github_rt.backoff_ms` | `60000` |  | ms | The first wait after a 403/429 that is a secondary limit or that carries Retry-After without one longer; it doubles with every repeat. |
| `github_rt.budget_pct` | `10` |  |  | The share, in percent, of the hourly rate limit the polling may use in total. A 304 answered from an ETag costs nothing (measured: the `used` counter does not move) and is not counted unless count_304 is 1. |
| `github_rt.cadence_fallback` | `poll_idle_ms` |  |  | The setting (one of the poll_*_ms) a repo is polled by when the rules script gives no answer for its status. |
| `github_rt.call_timeout_ms` | `20000` |  | ms | The time one gh call may take. |
| `github_rt.count_304` | `0` |  |  | 1 counts a 304 answer against the budget (the cautious reading), 0 does not (what was measured: see `ah-engine gh status`, section measure). |
| `github_rt.cwd_ttl_ms` | `7200000` |  | ms | A working directory seen by a hook this recently makes its repo followed; an older one is dropped. |
| `github_rt.edge_cooldown_ms` | `600000` |  | ms | The same edge (repo, kind, pull request or commit) is recorded at most once in this time. |
| `github_rt.edges_read_bytes` | `262144` |  |  | The most bytes of the edge file the advisory script reads. |
| `github_rt.enabled` | `true` |  |  | Follow the pull request and CI state of the repos of the user's live sessions. Off stops the polling and records no directories; what was recorded stays. |
| `github_rt.endpoints` | `8 entries` |  |  | The API paths, per call ({owner} {repo} {branch} {sha} {number} {base}). pulls: the pull requests whose head is the branch; pull: one pull request (mergeability); reviews: its reviews; checks: the check runs of the head commit; runs: the workflow runs of the head commit; rules: the branch rules of the base branch (the required checks); merge_info: the pull request again, read after a merge for its merge commit; commits: the newest commits of the base branch ({base}), read to see whether a merge was reverted. |
| `github_rt.error_chars` | `200` |  |  | The most characters of gh's error text kept as the last error. |
| `github_rt.etag_cap` | `400` |  |  | ETags kept (the oldest used are dropped past this). |
| `github_rt.files` | `6 entries` |  |  | Where GitHub realtime keeps its files, relative to the engine state directory: the recent directories, the state, the edge log, the ledger of ready notices and merges (one line per idempotency key). |
| `github_rt.gh` | `3 entries` |  |  | The GitHub CLI call: argv is the command and its fixed arguments (the endpoint is appended after the api -i arguments), etag_header is the request header that carries the ETag ({etag}), accept the Accept header. Replace argv[0] to point at another gh. |
| `github_rt.git` | `7 entries` |  |  | The read-only git commands used ({root} is the directory; {gitdir} is added where named). toplevel: the repo root of a directory; branch: the current branch (the word HEAD when detached); sha: the head commit; remote: the origin URL; dirs: the git dir and the common git dir, one per line. timeout_ms bounds each. |
| `github_rt.headers` | `7 entries` |  |  | The response headers read (lower case): the rate limit (limit, remaining, used, reset in epoch seconds), retry_after (seconds), poll_interval (seconds, a floor on the cadence), etag. |
| `github_rt.http` | `2 entries` |  |  | HTTP status codes that mean a rate limit or a server fault: rate_limited (always backs off) and server_error_from (this and above back off like a rate limit). |
| `github_rt.jobs_shown` | `5` |  |  | The most failing job names written into an edge line. |
| `github_rt.max_cwds` | `200` |  |  | The most directories kept in the record of recent working directories. |
| `github_rt.max_edges` | `100` |  |  | The most edges kept in the edge file. |
| `github_rt.max_repos` | `12` |  |  | The most repos followed at once (the most recently active first). |
| `github_rt.min_remaining` | `200` |  |  | Polling stops while the remaining requests the API reports are below this, until the limit resets. |
| `github_rt.note_every_ms` | `60000` |  | ms | The daemon records a directory it saw at most this often (the hook path only checks a map in memory between). |
| `github_rt.notify_argv` | `` |  |  | The command run for an owner notification ({title} {text} are filled in); empty means none. Example: ["osascript", "-e", "display notification \"{text}\" with title \"{title}\""]. |
| `github_rt.notify_kinds` | `` |  |  | The edges that also notify the owner (opt-in; empty, the default, notifies nothing) by running notify_argv. |
| `github_rt.offline_retry_ms` | `120000` |  | ms | After a gh call failed for lack of a network, how long before it is tried again. |
| `github_rt.patterns` | `4 entries` |  |  | Case-insensitive substrings that classify a failed call. secondary: a 403/429 body that means a secondary (abuse) limit; unauth: gh's text when it is not logged in; offline: gh's text when it could not reach GitHub; missing_repo: a 404 body for a repo that is gone or private to this login. |
| `github_rt.pct_base` | `100` |  |  | What budget_pct is a share of (100 for a percentage). |
| `github_rt.poll_done_ms` | `1800000` |  | ms | How often a repo whose pull request is merged or closed, with its checks finished, is polled. |
| `github_rt.poll_error_ms` | `1800000` |  | ms | How long a repo that answered 403/404 (no access, no such repo) is left alone. |
| `github_rt.poll_idle_ms` | `180000` |  | ms | How often a repo with an open pull request and no check running is polled. |
| `github_rt.poll_nopr_ms` | `600000` |  | ms | How often a repo whose branch has no pull request is polled (its commit's checks only); a push polls at once. |
| `github_rt.poll_running_ms` | `30000` |  | ms | How often a repo is polled while its checks are queued or running. |
| `github_rt.push_signature` | `4 entries` |  |  | The files, relative to the git dir (head) or the common git dir (the others), whose change means a commit, a checkout or a push: head, the branch ref ({branch}), the remote ref of the branch ({branch}) and packed-refs. |
| `github_rt.push_watch_ms` | `180000` |  | ms | After a push (the remote ref of the branch changed) or a checkout, a repo with no checks yet is polled at the running cadence for this long, since the checks of a new commit appear a few seconds late. |
| `github_rt.ready_actions` | `10 entries` |  |  | How merge readiness names itself in the action log: the feature, its two actions and its two mistake signals (with the text logged for each). |
| `github_rt.ready_app_db` | `` |  |  | The DevSwarm app database the scope check reads; empty (default) uses the detected one. For installs in a non-standard place. |
| `github_rt.ready_auto_merge` | `false` |  |  | ACT: when every ready condition holds for the current head commit, re-checked live right before, merge the pull request with `gh pr merge --merge` (ready_merge_argv; never --admin, so GitHub's branch protection and required reviews still decide and may refuse). Once per head commit (key merge:<repo>#<number>:<sha>), recorded in the ledger and the action log, with follow-up checks for a revert or a red base branch. Default OFF (owner rule: no auto-merge); turn it on with github_rt.ready_auto_merge = true in settings.json (section github_rt) or the engine config file. |
| `github_rt.ready_auto_merge_scope` | `workspaces` |  |  | Which pull requests the auto-merge may merge: `workspaces` (default) only those whose head branch is the branch of a live, non-primary DevSwarm workspace (matched against the app database's builders and their worktrees), never a release pull request (dev into main), a dependency bot's or a person's; `all` any pull request of a followed branch that is ready. Drafts are never ready, whatever the scope. |
| `github_rt.ready_behind_states` | `behind` |  |  | The mergeable_state values that mean the branch is behind its base. |
| `github_rt.ready_enabled` | `true` |  |  | Detect when the pull request of a followed branch becomes ready to merge (CI green on its head commit with every required check present, no changes requested, approved when ready_require_approval, no conflict, GitHub's mergeable state clean) and record a `ready` edge, once per head commit. Off: no ready edge, no auto-merge. |
| `github_rt.ready_followup` | `4 entries` |  |  | How the merge is checked afterwards for mistakes: wait_ms after the merge the checks of the merge commit on the base branch and the base's recent commits are read (CI red, or a revert of this pull request, is a mistake signal); retry_ms between reads while the checks are still running; give_up_ms after which an unfinished check is recorded as unknown; revert_window_ms the total time a revert is looked for. |
| `github_rt.ready_merge_argv` | `9 items` |  |  | The merge command ({number} {slug} {sha} are filled in). --match-head-commit makes GitHub refuse the merge if the head moved after the live re-check. Do not add --admin: that would bypass branch protection. |
| `github_rt.ready_merge_timeout_ms` | `60000` |  | ms | The longest the merge command may run. |
| `github_rt.ready_notify` | `true` |  |  | Tell the sessions of the repo about a ready pull request (the `ready` edge reaches the gh-rt-advisory check, once per session). Off: the edge is still recorded and logged, but no session is told. |
| `github_rt.ready_ok_states` | `clean, has_hooks` |  |  | The mergeable_state values GitHub reports that count as mergeable and clean. |
| `github_rt.ready_refusal_patterns` | `11 items` |  |  | Case-insensitive substrings of the merge command's output that mean GitHub (or gh) refused the merge by rule, not that something broke: branch protection or review requirements, a head that moved, a pull request that is not mergeable. Those are logged as `refused`, other failures as `failed`. |
| `github_rt.ready_require_approval` | `true` |  |  | A pull request is ready only with an approving review (and no pending request for changes). Off: a pull request without review rules is ready as soon as CI is green and it is mergeable. |
| `github_rt.ready_require_up_to_date` | `true` |  |  | A pull request that is behind its base branch (mergeable_state in ready_behind_states) is not ready. Off: being behind does not stop it. |
| `github_rt.remote` | `2 entries` |  |  | How an origin URL is read: host_patterns are the hosts that are GitHub (a remote on any other host is not followed); slug_re captures the owner and the repository from the part after the host (group 1 and 2), the .git suffix being dropped. |
| `github_rt.rules_ms` | `900000` |  | ms | How often the branch rules that name the required checks of the pull request's base branch are read (an ETag-conditional call). |
| `github_rt.rules_script` | `rules/gh-rt` |  |  | The plugin script (under engine/logic/) that holds the GitHub realtime rules: summaries, status, edges, edge text, statusline pieces and polling cadence. |
| `github_rt.stale_ms` | `1800000` |  | ms | A repo state older than this is shown as stale (the segment is left empty). |
| `github_rt.status_edges` | `10` |  |  | The newest edges `gh status` lists. |
| `github_rt.statuses` | `9 entries` |  |  | How check and run fields are read. running_statuses: a check or run in one of these is not finished; failing: conclusions that count as failed; passing: conclusions that count as passed (the rest, such as skipped, neither); review_changes, review_approved: review states; merged_conflict_states: mergeable_state values that mean the branch conflicts. |
| `github_rt.statusline_kinds` | `checks, pr, review` |  |  | What the statusline segment shows for the repo of the current directory, in this order of importance: any of checks, pr, review. |
| `github_rt.window_ms` | `3600000` |  | ms | The length of the budget window (the rate limit's own window is one hour). |
| `github_rt.words` | `34 entries` |  |  | The words GitHub realtime writes. Placeholders: {slug} {branch} {number} {sha} {jobs} {n} {title}. Edge lines: ci_red, ci_green, pr_merged, pr_closed, changes_requested, approved, conflict, ready. advisory_head is the first line of an advisory. segment_*: the statusline pieces; gh states: ok, missing, logged_out, offline, backoff, budget, disabled. |

### github_rt.toml / job

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job.gh_poll` | `11 entries` |  |  | GitHub realtime tick: for each repo of a recent session, notice a push (HEAD or branch refs changed), poll what is due within the rate budget and record the edges (CI red or green, PR merged, changes requested). Runs as a subprocess so a timeout kills it and every gh call it started. |

| `opcli.migration_heading` | `Node-to-engine migration: {native} native, {partial} partial, {node} node, {m...` |  |  | Migration report heading. Placeholders: {native}, {partial}, {node}, {missing}. |
| `opcli.migration_kind_duty` | `duty` |  |  | Migration report kind of a DevSwarm supervisor duty (devswarm_sup.duties). |
| `opcli.migration_kind_hook` | `hook` |  |  | Migration report kind of a registry check. |
| `opcli.migration_kind_stage` | `stage` |  |  | Migration report kind of a post-update stage (update_post.stages). |
| `opcli.migration_kind_switch` | `switch` |  |  | Migration report kind of a Node switch (opcli.migration_switches). |
| `opcli.migration_kind_verb` | `verb` |  |  | Migration report kind of a command of the registry (cmd.*). |

| `opcli.migration_missing` | `missing` |  |  | Migration report: the count (and the human status) of entries whose source does not say where they stand. A test holds it at 0. |
| `opcli.migration_status_native` | `native` |  |  | Migration status word: the path runs in the engine with no Node path left. |
| `opcli.migration_status_node` | `node` |  |  | Migration status word: Node still answers (a check with a Node twin, a duty that runs as Node's function, a post-update stage that names a Node function, a planned command). Also the duty kind that names a Node function. |
| `opcli.migration_status_partial` | `partial` |  |  | Migration status word: the engine answers, but a Node path remains (a real deferral, a Node witness, a Node key that still ships, a Node switch that is on). |
| `opcli.migration_switches` | `0 entries` |  |  | Migration report: the Node switches, name to defaults key; native when the key is 0, partial otherwise. |
| `opcli.migration_verb_node_keys` | `0 entries` |  |  | Migration report: per command, the defaults keys whose presence means a Node path of that command remains (the command is then partial). A lane that removes the Node path removes the key, and the report follows. |
| `opcli.migration_why_defer` | `defer` |  |  | Migration reason: the check's script (or a script it includes) has a real deferral (opcli.migration_defer_re outside comments). |
| `opcli.migration_why_fallback` | `fallback` |  |  | Migration reason prefix: the native post-update stage names a Node function it falls back to when the port cannot answer. |
| `opcli.migration_why_fn` | `fn` |  |  | Migration reason prefix: the post-update stage names this Node function. |

| `opcli.migration_why_node_kind` | `node_kind` |  |  | Migration reason: the duty's kind is still node (it runs as Node's function, or natively with a Node witness or remainder). |
| `opcli.migration_why_switch` | `switch` |  |  | Migration reason prefix: this Node switch is not 0. |
| `opcli.migration_why_twin` | `node_twin` |  |  | Migration reason: the check is not classified in script.engine_only_checks, so a script failure has no declared policy. |
| `opcli.no_change_verbs` | `status, , test, review-due` |  |  | The `jev-setup` verbs that change nothing, so a successful run does not count as a change in the telemetry (an empty word is the bare command). |
| `opcli.review_after_days_default` | `7` |  |  | jev.reviewAfterDays when the setting is zero or not a number (Node: `Number(x) \|\| 7`). |
| `opcli.review_day_ms` | `86400000` |  |  | Milliseconds in a day (the review windows and the snooze are counted in whole days). |
| `opcli.review_head` | `jev review-due:` |  |  | `review-due` heading above the due integrations. |
| `opcli.review_hour_ms` | `3600000` |  |  | Milliseconds in an hour (the due-to-reviewed latency is said in hours). |

| `opcli.review_max_time_ms` | `8640000000000000` |  |  | The largest instant a date can hold, in milliseconds (a snooze past it has no date). |

| `opcli.review_state_bad` | `review state: the entry of {id} is not an object; fix or remove ~/.anti-hall/...` |  |  | The review state holds an entry that is not an object, which the verb cannot update (nothing is written). Placeholder: {id}. |
| `opcli.review_state_file` | `jev-review-state.json` |  |  | The durable shadow-review state, relative to the anti-hall home directory. |

| `opcli.review_stats_max_files` | `64` |  | count | How many decision-log files the review scan keeps totals for (the log and its numbered generations); the least recently used are dropped first and read again from their start. |

| `opcli.reviewed_usage` | `reviewed: usage is `reviewed <integration>`` |  |  | `reviewed` without an integration. |

| `opcli.test_label_fallback` | `fallback` |  |  | `test` label of the fallback transport. |
| `opcli.test_label_primary` | `primary` |  |  | `test` label of the primary transport. |
| `opcli.test_not_enabled` | `test: jev is not enabled — run `enable` first` |  |  | `test` while Jev is off. |
| `opcli.test_ok` | `ok — latency {ms}ms, confidence {confidence} ({tag})` |  |  | `test` line of a target that answered. Placeholders: {ms}, {confidence}, {tag}. |
| `opcli.test_question` | `3 entries` |  |  | The yes/no question `test` asks (a Noul question: instructions, then the labels of true and false). |
| `opcli.test_rejected_hint` | `the key was rejected — check the key is correct AND that the transport (verce...` |  |  | What `test` adds when the key was rejected. |

| `opcli.test_state` | `On a clear day, the sky appears blue.` |  |  | The text `test` has Jev judge. |
| `opcli.test_tag_one` | `transport: {transport}` |  |  | `test` tag when one transport is tested. Placeholder: {transport}. |
| `opcli.test_tag_two` | `{label}, transport: {transport}` |  |  | `test` tag when primary and fallback are both tested. Placeholders: {label}, {transport}. |

### wake_watch.toml / wake_watch

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `wake_watch.active_cache_file` | `hivecontrol-active.json` |  |  | The supervisor's cache of the hivecontrol active list, under the DevSwarm state directory (isAppArchived reads it for a worktree under the app's repos root that the app database has no opinion on). |
| `wake_watch.active_max_age_mult` | `2` |  |  | How many reconcile-sweep intervals old the active-list cache may be and still be believed (one missed sweep is tolerated, two is not). |
| `wake_watch.archived_recheck_floor_ms` | `100` |  |  | Smallest accepted value of the archived re-check override. |
| `wake_watch.archived_recheck_ms` | `120000` |  |  | How often a child watcher asks again whether its own workspace is archived (it reads the app database), in milliseconds. |
| `wake_watch.cache_dir` | `cache` |  |  | The cache directory under the plugins directory (one directory per marketplace, plugin and version). |
| `wake_watch.diag_lock_held` | `[wake-watch] another watcher already holds the lock for {role} {id} (holder p...` |  |  | Printed on stderr when a live watcher already holds the lock. {role} {id} {pid} {age} {session} {acquired} {version}. |
| `wake_watch.diag_no_cwd` | `[wake-watch] the working directory is not readable; exiting.\n` |  |  | Printed (stderr) when the working directory is gone; exit 1, as Node's uncaught `process.cwd()` failure does. |
| `wake_watch.diag_no_home` | `[wake-watch] no home directory; exiting.\n` |  |  | Printed (stderr) when no home directory can be found; exit 1, as Node's uncaught `os.homedir()` failure does. |
| `wake_watch.diag_no_identity` | `[wake-watch] could not resolve a DevSwarm identity for cwd={cwd}; exiting qui...` |  |  | Printed on stderr when DevSwarm is active but no identity resolves. {cwd}. |
| `wake_watch.diag_not_devswarm` | `[wake-watch] not a DevSwarm session; exiting quietly (not arming).\n` |  |  | Printed on stderr when the session shows no sign of DevSwarm. |
| `wake_watch.diag_rebin_failed` | `[wake-watch] cannot restart from the replaced binary {path}: {why}; re-arm th...` |  |  | Printed (stderr) when the watcher could not re-execute the replaced binary; it ends (exit 1) and must be re-armed. {path}, {why}. |
| `wake_watch.diag_restamp_stale` | `[wake-watch] lock restamp failed transiently for longer than the lock stale t...` |  |  | Printed on stderr when the lock could not be re-stamped for longer than it stays valid. |
| `wake_watch.diag_restamp_transient` | `[wake-watch] lock restamp failed transiently (not lock loss) - retrying next ...` |  |  | Printed once on stderr when the lock could not be re-stamped for a transient reason. |
| `wake_watch.dir_archive_ignore` | `archive-ignore` |  |  | The directory of the owner's per-workspace archive-ignore markers, under the DevSwarm state directory. |
| `wake_watch.dir_inbox` | `inbox` |  |  | The directory of the children's durable inboxes, under the DevSwarm state directory. |
| `wake_watch.dir_summaries` | `summaries` |  |  | The directory of the projects' derived summaries, under the DevSwarm state directory. |
| `wake_watch.dir_wake` | `wake` |  |  | The directory of the watchers' private cursors, under the DevSwarm state directory. |
| `wake_watch.enabled_plugins_field` | `enabledPlugins` |  |  | The settings member that maps an install key to whether it is enabled. |
| `wake_watch.env_active_max_age` | `ANTIHALL_DEVSWARM_ARCHIVED_CACHE_MAX_AGE_MS` |  |  | The variable that overrides how old the active-list cache may be and still be believed (a positive integer, milliseconds). |
| `wake_watch.env_archived_recheck` | `ANTIHALL_DEVSWARM_WAKE_WATCH_ARCHIVED_RECHECK_MS` |  |  | Test knob: overrides the archived re-check interval (milliseconds). |
| `wake_watch.env_handoff` | `ANTIHALL_WAKE_WATCH_HANDED_OFF` |  |  | Set by a watcher that hands over to a newer build: the version it handed over to, so a chain of handoffs only ever moves forward. |

| `wake_watch.env_source_branch` | `DEVSWARM_SOURCE_BRANCH` |  |  | The variable whose non-blank value marks a DevSwarm child workspace. |

| `wake_watch.label_sep` | ` ` |  |  | Between a channel label and the word after it. |

| `wake_watch.set_archived_grace_ms` | `6 entries` |  |  | The setting devswarm.archivedGraceMs: how much newer than a child's descriptor the active-list snapshot must be before the child's absence from it reads as archived (milliseconds). |

| `wake_watch.set_enabled` | `5 entries` |  |  | The setting devswarm.wakeWatch: off refuses to arm (the cron wake fallback is unaffected). |
| `wake_watch.set_idle_skip` | `6 entries` |  |  | The setting devswarm.wakeWatchIdleSkip: a Primary with no live child workspace need not arm (Node prints its one idle line). |
| `wake_watch.set_poll_ms` | `7 entries` |  |  | The setting devswarm.wakeWatchPollMs: the tick of the watcher in milliseconds (lock heartbeat, parent check, stale-build check, reads). A change of a watched file wakes the tick early. |
| `wake_watch.sweep_fallback_ms` | `900000` |  |  | The reconcile-sweep interval the cache age bound uses when the setting is no positive number: 15 minutes. |
| `wake_watch.tmp_suffix` | `.tmp` |  |  | End of the temporary file a cursor is written to before the rename. |
| `wake_watch.user_settings_rel` | `.claude/settings.json` |  |  | The user's harness settings file, relative to the home: it says which installs are enabled. |
| `wake_watch.verb` | `wake-watch` |  |  | The `ah-engine devswarm` verb that runs the idle-wake Monitor. |
| `wake_watch.word_unavailable` | `unavailable` |  |  | Said where the session of a lock holder is not recorded. |
| `wake_watch.word_unknown` | `unknown` |  |  | Said where a role, id or version is not known. |
| `wake_watch.word_unknown_error` | `unknown read error` |  |  | Said where a failed read gave no reason. |

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |

| `devswarm_compat.outputs` | `workspace info:id,branch,path,worktreePath,sourceBranch,parentBranch,startup,...` |  |  | Parsed CLI output dependencies; inventory only, not certified by help. No messaging queue is read by the probe. |
| `devswarm_compat.paths` | `macOS: Library/Application Support/DevSwarm/devswarm.db, Linux: XDG_CONFIG_HO...` |  |  | External app path defaults and anti-hall descriptor fields used by both orchestration ports; inventory, not proof of producer behavior. |

| `devswarm_compat.reason_no_probe` | `no compatibility probe cached` |  |  | The reason of a compatibility report when no probe result is cached. |
| `devswarm_compat.reason_partial` | `Help and schema only; output fields, environment semantics and descriptor pro...` |  |  | The reason of a compatibility report that only checked help and schema. |
| `devswarm_compat.reason_stale` | `cached probe differs from current version or dependency manifest` |  |  | The reason of a cached compatibility report whose version or dependency manifest no longer matches. |
| `devswarm_compat.schema` | `builders:id,repositoryId,sourceBranch,branchName,worktreePath,terminalId,labe...` |  |  | App SQLite read-only schema contract: table followed by required columns. Column presence does not prove row semantics. |
| `devswarm_compat.semantic_conflicts` | `workspace monitor\\|Without a pane ID\\|Plain-shell monitor excludes messages p...` |  |  | Known incompatible help semantics: command\|help marker\|diagnostic. Detection is advisory only; never acknowledges or consumes mail. |
| `devswarm_compat.total_budget_ms` | `20000` |  | ms | Total wall-clock budget for version-change compatibility help probes; skipped dependencies stay unverified. SessionStart only queues this native background refresh. |

### refresh.toml / job

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job.refresh` | `11 entries` |  |  | Handle the session-cache refresh requests (L06): runs `ah-engine refresh --json` as a subprocess, so a timeout kills it and every probe it started. Off when refresh.every_ms is 0. |

### refresh.toml / refresh

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `refresh.claude_cli_bins` | `claude` |  |  | The programs the Claude Code probe asks, in order. |
| `refresh.devswarm_bins` | `devswarm, hivecontrol` |  |  | The programs the DevSwarm probe asks, in order (the CLI, then the hivecontrol shim). |
| `refresh.every_ms` | `60000` | `AH_ENGINE_REFRESH_MS` | ms | How often the refresh job looks for requests; a request waits at most this long (plus jitter). Cheap when there is none: it reads a few small files. 0 turns the job off. |
| `refresh.full_version_re` | `(?-u:\b)v?([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)(?-u:\b)` |  |  | A full X.Y.Z version token (leading v optional; ASCII digits and word boundaries, as the JavaScript pattern of the Node scripts); exactly one distinct token in a stream is the version, more is ambiguous. |
| `refresh.git_program` | `git` |  |  | The git program the version probe runs (resolved through PATH). |
| `refresh.handled_file` | `handled.json` |  |  | The job's record of the newest request it handled per probe (`{"<probe>": <requestedAt>}`), relative to the request directory; a request at or below its record is done. |
| `refresh.lock_boot_slop_s` | `5` |  |  | Two boot times closer than this many seconds are the same boot (lock owner liveness). |
| `refresh.lock_file` | `run.lock` |  |  | The run lock (Node lock protocol), relative to the request directory, so a manual run and the job never handle a request twice. |
| `refresh.lock_reclaim_stale_ms` | `10000` |  | ms | A takeover marker of the run lock older than this is taken over. |
| `refresh.lock_release_step_ms` | `10` |  | ms | The pause between those tries. |
| `refresh.lock_release_tries` | `20` |  |  | How many times a release tries to take the takeover marker. |
| `refresh.lock_stale_ms` | `960000` |  | ms | A run lock older than this is taken over (longer than the job's timeout). |
| `refresh.lock_step_ms` | `50` |  | ms | The pause between tries for the run lock. |
| `refresh.lock_wait_ms` | `0` |  | ms | How long a run waits for a held run lock before giving up (the next tick tries again). |
| `refresh.log_kind` | `refresh` |  |  | The event-log kind of the refresh lines. |
| `refresh.msg_action` | `action={action_id} probe={probe} target={target} outcome={outcome} reason={re...` |  |  | The event-log line of one action: what was done, to what, why, how long it took and its id. |
| `refresh.msg_busy` | `another refresh run holds the lock; nothing handled` |  |  | The result when another run holds the run lock. |
| `refresh.msg_no_home` | `refresh: no home directory (set HOME or pass --home)` |  |  | The error when no home directory is known. |
| `refresh.outcome_failed` | `failed` |  |  | The outcome word of a probe that wrote nothing (no answer, no network, a write refused). |
| `refresh.outcome_refreshed` | `refreshed` |  |  | The outcome word of a probe that wrote its cache or a repair that ran. |
| `refresh.outcome_skipped` | `skipped` |  |  | The outcome word of a probe with no new request. |
| `refresh.partial_version_re` | `(?-u:\b)v?([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)(?-u:\b)` |  |  | An X.Y token, used only when a stream has no full token; again exactly one distinct token or nothing. |
| `refresh.poll_ms` | `20` |  | ms | How often the bounded runner checks whether a probe has finished. |
| `refresh.probe_timeout_ms` | `15000` |  | ms | Longest one probe subprocess (`git ls-remote`, `<cli> --version`) may run; its process group is killed at the limit (the Node refresh scripts used the same bound). |
| `refresh.probes` | `version, claude_cli, devswarm, repair` |  |  | The probes in the order a run handles them. `version`: the remote-latest anti-hall release tag (version-alert); `claude_cli` and `devswarm`: the installed CLI versions (drift probes); `repair`: the reload repair (repair-on-reload). |
| `refresh.reason_cooldown` | `cooldown` |  |  | Reason word: a repair ran at this version within the cooldown (live re-check). |
| `refresh.reason_exit` | `repair-failed` |  |  | Reason word: the repair exited non-zero or did not finish in time. |
| `refresh.reason_forced` | `forced` |  |  | Reason word: `--force`. |
| `refresh.reason_locked` | `locked` |  |  | Reason word: another repair holds its lock. |
| `refresh.reason_no_output` | `no-output` |  |  | Reason word: no source answered. |
| `refresh.reason_no_tag` | `no-tag` |  |  | Reason word: the sources answered but named no release tag. |
| `refresh.reason_requested` | `requested` |  |  | Reason word: a check asked for it. |
| `refresh.reason_write_failed` | `write-failed` |  |  | Reason word: the cache or record could not be written. |
| `refresh.repair_args` | `doctor, --repair, --migrations-only, --quiet` |  |  | The engine arguments of the reload repair (the engine's port of `doctor.js --repair --migrations-only --quiet`); `--home` and, when the request names it, `--plugin-root` are appended. |
| `refresh.repair_lock_file` | `repair-on-reload.lock` |  |  | The repair lock of the reload repair (the Node lock protocol), relative to the anti-hall directory, so the engine and a Node repair never run together. |
| `refresh.repair_lock_stale_ms` | `660000` |  | ms | A repair lock older than this is taken over (longer than refresh.repair_timeout_ms, so a live engine repair is never taken over). |
| `refresh.repair_timeout_ms` | `600000` |  | ms | Longest the reload repair may run; its process group is killed at the limit. |
| `refresh.request_dir` | `.anti-hall/refresh` |  |  | Where the checks write their requests, relative to the home directory: one `<probe>.json` per probe, `{"requestedAt": <ms>, ...}`. |
| `refresh.request_ext` | `.json` |  |  | The file ending of a request file after the probe name. |
| `refresh.request_max_bytes` | `65536` |  | bytes | Largest request or record file the job reads; a larger one is ignored as unreadable. |
| `refresh.tag_args` | `ls-remote, --tags` |  |  | The git arguments that list a remote's tags; the remote is appended. |
| `refresh.tag_fallback_remote` | `origin` |  |  | The remote asked next, inside the local marketplace clone (session.marketplace_dir), when the first gave no output. |
| `refresh.tag_re` | `refs/tags/(v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)$` |  |  | A release tag line of `git ls-remote --tags` (a trailing CR is stripped first); group 1 is the tag. Peeled refs never match. |
| `refresh.tag_remote` | `https://github.com/talas9/anti-hall` |  |  | The remote the version probe asks first (live network). |
| `refresh.version_arg` | `--version` |  |  | The argument that makes a CLI print its version. |

| `routine.detail_chars` | `160` |  |  | Characters of an event detail or error text shown in a problem line. |
| `routine.dirty_suffix` | `-dirty` |  |  | The ending of a build stamp made from uncommitted changes. |

| `routine.env_roots` | `AH_DEPLOY_ROOTS` |  |  | Environment variable naming the plugin roots to install into (colon separated); when set it replaces the lookup below. Tests and scratch homes use it. |
| `routine.failed_job_codes` | `failed, timeout` |  |  | The outcome codes of that kind that count as a failed job. |
| `routine.files_dir` | `files` |  |  | Sub-directory of a saved copy that holds the replaced plugin files. |
| `routine.flag_allow_leftovers` | `--allow-entry-leftovers` |  |  | Owner override: install a plugin tree although the entry-path audit lists js/sh leftovers (the override is printed). |

| `routine.flag_hook_bin` | `--hook-bin` |  |  | The thin client (ah-hook) to install, when it is not at one of routine.hook_candidates. |

| `routine.flag_source` | `--source` |  |  | Where the build came from, recorded in the install record (one of routine.sources). |

### guards_v1.toml / api_guard_v1

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `api_guard_v1.max_code_chars` | `600000` |  |  | A code chunk longer than this (JavaScript string length) is not checked, as in the Node guard. |
| `api_guard_v1.max_modules` | `8` |  |  | Most module groups probed per language (one interpreter run each), as the Node guard bounds them. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_instead` | `verify the API names and correct the references.` |  |  | Block message: what to do instead. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_item_prefix` | `  • ` |  |  | Prefix of each fabricated reference listed under the block message. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_override` | `only if you target a NEWER version where it exists: write ~/.anti-hall/skip.j...` |  |  | Block message: the override. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_timeout` | `anti-hall api-guard: API verification skipped (probe for "{bin}" timed out af...` |  |  | The one stderr line when a probe timed out, was killed or could not run in the time left and nothing was blocked (the edit is allowed unchecked); {bin} is the interpreter, {ms} the asked budget. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_what` | `this edit references APIs missing from the installed runtime.` |  |  | Block headline; {versions} lists the interpreters' version lines. |
| `api_guard_v1.msg_why` | `These attributes are absent from the real module/object; they look like fabri...` |  |  | Block message: why. |
| `api_guard_v1.node_args` | `-e` |  |  | Arguments before the JavaScript probe's source and its two JSON arguments. |
| `api_guard_v1.node_bin` | `node` |  |  | The JavaScript runtime probed for require() modules and global builtins: the user's own `node` on the request's PATH (when it is not installed, JavaScript references are not checked). |
| `api_guard_v1.node_probe` | `const mods = JSON.parse(process.argv[1]);\nconst globals = JSON.parse(process...` |  |  | The JavaScript probe: requires each module once and walks each global path, answering 1 (present), 0 (missing) or 2 (unknown) per attribute; it runs in the hook's working directory so installed packages resolve. |
| `api_guard_v1.python3_version_pattern` | `Python 3\.` |  |  | What a usable Python's version output (stdout and stderr joined) must contain. |
| `api_guard_v1.python_args` | `-I, -c` |  |  | Arguments before the Python probe's source and its JSON check list: -I (isolated: no user site-packages, no environment, no current directory on sys.path) and -c. |
| `api_guard_v1.python_bins` | `python3, python` |  |  | The Python interpreters tried, in order; the first whose version probe exits 0 and prints api_guard_v1.python3_version_pattern is used. |
| `api_guard_v1.python_probe` | `import sys, json, os\ncwd = os.getcwd()\nsys.path[:] = [p for p in sys.path i...` |  |  | The Python probe: drops the working directory from sys.path, imports each base module once, walks the receiver path and answers 1 (attribute present), 0 (missing) or 2 (unknown) per [receiver, attribute] pair of its JSON argument. |
| `api_guard_v1.spawn_timeout_env` | `ANTIHALL_API_GUARD_SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS` |  |  | Environment variable that replaces api_guard_v1.spawn_timeout_ms when it holds a positive integer (the Node guard's test knob). |
| `api_guard_v1.spawn_timeout_ms` | `15000` |  | ms | The per-probe timeout the guard asks for (the Node guard's own); the spawn primitive cuts it to host_spawn.timeout_max_ms and the request's deadline. |
| `api_guard_v1.tmpdir_default` | `/tmp` |  |  | The Python probe's directory when api_guard_v1.tmpdir_env is unset or not absolute. |
| `api_guard_v1.tmpdir_env` | `TMPDIR` |  |  | The request environment variable naming the temporary directory the Python probe runs in (never the repository). |
| `api_guard_v1.version_args` | `--version` |  |  | Arguments that make an interpreter print its version (the Python check and the version list of the block message). |
| `api_guard_v1.version_joiner` | `, ` |  |  | Separator between the interpreter version lines in the block message. |

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hook_proc.cwd_envs` | `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, HOME` |  |  | Stand-ins for the hook process's working directory, which a Node guard read (process.cwd()) when the payload had no cwd or a relative one: the first of these request variables that holds an absolute path. Claude Code runs a hook in the session's directory, which CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR names. |
| `hook_proc.cwd_last` | `/` |  |  | The hook process's working directory when no stand-in in hook_proc.cwd_envs is absolute. |

### guards_v1.toml / host_spawn

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `host_spawn.cache_enabled` | `true` |  |  | Whether `ahHost.spawnProbeCached` keeps completed probe answers (an interpreter's version line) per daemon. Off: every call runs the program. |
| `host_spawn.cache_key_env` | `PATH, PYENV_VERSION, ASDF_PYTHON_VERSION, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA_PREFIX, CONDA_DE...` |  |  | Request environment variables whose values are part of a kept probe answer's key, because they pick the interpreter version behind a shim (pyenv, asdf, virtualenv, conda); a different value probes again. |
| `host_spawn.cache_skip_stdout` | `^\s*\[[^\]]*\b2\b` |  |  | A regular expression: a probe run whose stdout matches is not kept, because its answer depends on what is installed and the key cannot see that (the Python probe's `[..., 2, ...]` means a module or attribute could not be resolved; installing the package changes it). Empty keeps every finished run. |
| `host_spawn.cache_ttl_ms` | `600000` |  | ms | How long a kept probe answer is served before the program is run again (a changed interpreter file re-probes at once, whatever this says). |
| `host_spawn.deadline_reserve_ms` | `60` |  | ms | Time kept back from the request's deadline when a spawned program's timeout is cut to it: the other checks of the event and the reply still need it. |
| `host_spawn.default_path` | `/usr/bin:/bin` |  |  | The search path used when the request carries no PATH: the default of the C library's execvp, which is what Node's spawn falls back to. |
| `host_spawn.max_calls` | `16` |  |  | Most programs one script call may start (api-guard: two version probes, one per module group up to api_guard_v1.max_modules, one Node probe, the version lines of the message). |
| `host_spawn.max_workers` | `4` |  |  | The most probe workers (kept-answer runs that outlive their request) alive at once, across all requests; a request that would exceed it fails open without starting one, so timed-out probes cannot pile up. |
| `host_spawn.min_run_ms` | `1` |  | ms | A spawn whose cut timeout is below this does not run at all (reported as skipped). |
| `host_spawn.output_max_bytes` | `262144` |  | bytes | Largest stdout or stderr a spawned program may write; more marks the run `overflow` (the Node probe's maxBuffer) and both streams are cut here. |
| `host_spawn.path_env` | `PATH` |  |  | The request environment variable that holds the search path for a spawned program. |
| `host_spawn.poll_ms` | `2` |  | ms | How often a running spawned program is checked for exit. |
| `host_spawn.prewarm` | `true` |  |  | Whether the daemon warms the probe cache at start (the interpreters' version probes the guards ask for first), on a background thread after the socket is listening, so the first guard call finds them kept instead of probing cold inside its deadline. Off: the first call probes. |
| `host_spawn.prewarm_programs` | `python3, python` |  |  | The programs whose version probe (the arguments of api_guard_v1.version_args) the start-up warm-up runs, in the daemon's own environment. Each must be one of host_spawn.programs. |
| `host_spawn.prewarm_timeout_ms` | `15000` |  | ms | How long one start-up warm-up probe may run on its background thread (a probe cut here is not kept). |
| `host_spawn.programs` | `python3, python, node` |  |  | The only programs a script may start through the spawn primitive: bare names, each looked up on the request's PATH (the user's own install), never the daemon's PATH or the plugin's files. api-guard probes these interpreters. |
| `host_spawn.scrub_env` | `^(NODE_OPTIONS\|NODE_PATH\|PYTHONSTARTUP\|PYTHONPATH\|PYTHONHOME\|PYTHONINSPECT\|PY...` |  |  | Names of request environment variables never passed to a spawned program (case-insensitive): interpreter start-up injection vectors, as the Node api-guard scrubs them. |
| `host_spawn.timeout_max_ms` | `15000` |  | ms | Ceiling of one spawned program's run, whatever the script asks; it is also cut to what the request has left (see host_spawn.deadline_reserve_ms), so a slow interpreter costs a fail-open notice, never the reply. |

| `inbox_read_v1.msg_store_what` | `a raw DevSwarm store read was stopped.` |  |  | Store-read block: what. |
| `inbox_read_v1.msg_store_why` | `The store is the write/derive layer; a raw read risks a partial view and a la...` |  |  | Store-read block: why. |
| `inbox_read_v1.store_cli_present` | `true` |  |  | Whether the wrapper's store-read command exists, so a raw read of the DevSwarm store (its database, sidecars and journal) is blocked as well as a raw inbox read. The store-read CLI is present in every shipped plugin since the journal store; the engine ships the same answer. |

### guards_v1.toml / output_verify_v1

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |

The engine receives the payload with its keys sorted; keys not listed here follow the listed ones, sorted. |

### diagnostics.toml / diagnostics

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diagnostics.abandoned_log_interval_ms` | `60000` |  |  | Per site, the least time between two event-log lines for an abandoned decision (every one is still counted; the line names the site, the reason and the key inputs, and says how many were counted since the last line). 0 logs every one. |
| `diagnostics.abandoned_log_keys_max` | `256` |  |  | How many (site, reason) pairs the abandoned-decision log limiter remembers before it forgets them all (bounds its memory; a forgotten pair logs once more). |
| `diagnostics.abandoned_no_reason` | `the site gave no reason` |  |  | The reason shown in the event-log line of an abandoned decision whose site gave none (the site name still says where). |
| `diagnostics.advisory_counter_kind` | `advisory` |  |  | The journal kind under which the advisory counters (flagged, asked, confirmed, injected, suppressed, jev_error per advisory kind) are kept in the shared counter journal. |
| `diagnostics.allocator` | `jemalloc` |  |  | Allocator for the daemon the client spawns: jemalloc (default) or system. The client passes it on as AH_ENGINE_ALLOCATOR unless that is already set. Changing it requires a daemon restart. |
| `diagnostics.allocator_choices` | `jemalloc, system` |  |  | Allocator names the client accepts from diagnostics.allocator; any other value is logged and the daemon starts with jemalloc. |
| `diagnostics.allocator_env` | `AH_ENGINE_ALLOCATOR` |  |  | Environment variable the client sets on the daemon it spawns to select the allocator (the daemon reads it before its first allocation). An existing value in the client's own environment wins. |
| `diagnostics.budget_cpu_hard_pct` | `10` |  | % | HARD CPU limit of the daemon, percent of one core (10, owner decision 2026-10-23), measured over the same daemon.cpu_check_ms windows and the same diagnostics.budget_cpu_windows count as the soft bar (diagnostics.budget_cpu_pct, which only warns and counts). Once it is crossed the daemon sheds OPTIONAL work and nothing else: scheduled and background duties are delayed (the schedule.cpu_backoff_ms backoff, renewed every window), the checks of events that cannot block (everything outside dispatch.guard_events) are not run only when diagnostics.shed_checks is 1 (shipped 0), and Jev is not consulted (every caller gets its baseline). Guards and block decisions never stop. The event is logged and counted (status budget: cpu_hard_breaches, shed_skipped). Shedding ends by itself on the first window under the soft limit. 0 turns the hard limit off. |
| `diagnostics.budget_cpu_pct` | `5` |  | % | SOFT CPU limit of the daemon (5 percent of one core, owner decision 2026-10-23; the 10 percent hard bar is web.pulse_cpu_bad_permille). A limit, not a target. CPU budget of the daemon, percent of one core. A breach is reported when the CPU over diagnostics.budget_cpu_windows consecutive daemon.cpu_check_ms windows stays at or above it; 0 turns the CPU budget off. |
| `diagnostics.budget_cpu_windows` | `2` |  |  | Consecutive daemon.cpu_check_ms windows over the CPU budget that make a breach (one busy window is a burst, not a breach). |
| `diagnostics.budget_mem_mb` | `125` |  | MB | SOFT memory limit of the daemon (125 MB, owner decision 2026-10-23; hard is mem.global_hard_bytes). Memory budget of the daemon in MB, measured with the figure daemon.mem_metric selects. A breach is reported while the daemon is over it; 0 turns the memory budget off. |
| `diagnostics.check_mem` | `true` |  |  | Measure the bytes each check allocates (total, peak growth, kept) from per-thread counters in the counting allocator. Off also stops the counting in the allocator. Cost is a few nanoseconds per allocation. |
| `diagnostics.check_mem_sample_every` | `1` |  |  | Measure every Nth check call (1 = every call). Raise it only if the measured cost of the per-thread counters becomes a problem. |
| `diagnostics.counter_name_max` | `96` |  |  | Longest site, duty or stage name kept in the counter journal (characters); longer names are cut. Whitespace and control characters in a name become `_`. |
| `diagnostics.counters_file` | `obs-counters.log` |  |  | Name (in the state directory) of the shared counter journal: processes that are not the daemon (hook calls, one-shot commands, post-update stages) append their hand-back and accounting counts here, and `status` folds them in. Never created by a read-only command. |
| `diagnostics.counters_hard_keys` | `2048` |  |  | Hard limit on distinct counters in the journal fold: a new counter past it is folded into `other` and counted in `counters_dropped`. |
| `diagnostics.counters_max_bytes` | `262144` |  | bytes | Size at which the counter journal is folded into one line per counter (atomically, under the journal lock), so it never grows without bound. |
| `diagnostics.counters_other_key` | `other` |  |  | The key under which counters past diagnostics.counters_hard_keys are folded. |
| `diagnostics.counters_soft_keys` | `512` |  |  | Soft limit on distinct counters (kind, key and outcome) the journal fold keeps; past it each new counter adds one to `counters_soft_hits`. |
| `diagnostics.debug_flag` | `--debug` |  |  | The command-line flag that turns debug mode on for one `serve` or `hook` process. |
| `diagnostics.debug_log_max_bytes` | `8388608` |  | bytes | Size at which the debug log is rotated (the old file is kept once, as <name>.1, replacing the previous one), so it never holds more than twice this. |
| `diagnostics.debug_mem_snapshot_ms` | `30000` |  | ms | In debug mode, how often the watchdog writes a memory line (resident set, footprint, allocator and component sizes) to the debug log; in normal mode memory is only snapshotted when the resident-set cap trips. |
| `diagnostics.debug_mode` | `false` |  |  | Debug mode: the same binary also writes verbose per-module logs to the debug log (files.debug_log), checks runtime invariants (a violation is logged and counted, never fatal), samples per-thread CPU every diagnostics.debug_thread_sample_ms and writes a memory line every diagnostics.debug_mem_snapshot_ms. Off in normal use; the cost of the switch while off is one atomic load per call site. The environment variable env.debug or the --debug flag (diagnostics.debug_flag) of `serve` and `hook` turns it on for that process regardless of this setting; this setting is read again on every change of the config files, so a running daemon follows it without a restart. |
| `diagnostics.debug_modules` | `` |  |  | Modules whose debug log lines are written (a module name such as `daemon/queue`, or a prefix ending in a slash such as `daemon/`). An empty list means every module. |
| `diagnostics.debug_thread_sample_ms` | `5000` |  | ms | In debug mode, how often the watchdog samples every thread's CPU time and logs the busiest threads and the work counters per second over that interval. |
| `diagnostics.debug_thread_top` | `8` |  |  | Threads (grouped by name) listed per per-thread CPU sample in the debug log. |
| `diagnostics.diag_top` | `15` |  |  | Rows shown per ranking in `diag hooks` and `diag fs`. |
| `diagnostics.diag_topics` | `11 items` |  |  | The topics of `ah-engine diag <topic>`: read-only reports over state the engine already keeps (not feature-gated). `trace` dumps the always-on trace ring. |
| `diagnostics.duration_units` | `4 entries` |  |  | Suffixes the `--for` duration of `ctl profile on` accepts, each with its length in milliseconds (a bare number is seconds). |
| `diagnostics.fd_dir` | `/dev/fd` |  |  | Directory that lists this process's open file descriptors (`diag fs` counts its entries). |
| `diagnostics.file_max_bytes` | `65536` |  |  | Most bytes `diag file <id>` reads from the end of a file. |
| `diagnostics.file_prefix_defaults` | `defaults:` |  |  | Id prefix of a shipped defaults file (`diag file defaults:<name>.toml`). |
| `diagnostics.file_prefix_state` | `state:` |  |  | Id prefix of a file in the state directory (`diag file state:<name>`); the name is a plain file name, never a path, and a database is refused. |
| `diagnostics.file_prefix_transcript` | `transcript:` |  |  | Id prefix of an agent's transcript (`diag file transcript:<agent id>`), found through the tracker state. |
| `diagnostics.file_refuse_ext` | `.db, .db-wal, .db-shm, .sock, .key, .pem` |  |  | File name endings `diag file` refuses (databases and their journals, key material). |
| `diagnostics.file_tail_lines` | `200` |  |  | Most lines `diag file <id>` returns (the last ones), each scrubbed of the home path and secrets. |
| `diagnostics.integrity_stores` | `hot.db, archive.db` |  |  | The databases `diag integrity <store>` checks, by file name in the state directory. |
| `diagnostics.malloc_stack_logging` | `` |  |  | Diagnostic label for an operator-run macOS `MallocStackLogging` repro (`lite` or empty). The engine only accepts and reports it; the OS facility must be enabled in the process environment before start. |
| `diagnostics.mem_log` | `true` |  |  | Append one NDJSON line per served request to the memory log: time, request kind, event, the checks that ran, resident set and allocator figures before and after, and the size of the transcript file. Costs a few microseconds and one small append per request; turn it off once the memory question is closed. |
| `diagnostics.mem_log_checks_cap` | `64` |  |  | Most checks whose per-call memory (`check_mem`: check, peak, allocated bytes) one request line of the memory log lists; further checks of the same request are left off the line. |
| `diagnostics.mem_log_max_bytes` | `4194304` |  | bytes | Size at which the memory log is rotated (the old file is kept once, as <name>.1, replacing the previous one), so the log never holds more than twice this. |
| `diagnostics.mem_snapshot` | `true` |  |  | When the resident-set cap trips, write one snapshot before the daemon exits: allocator figures, thread count, the interpreters and caches of every worker, and the platform's own memory map of the process. |
| `diagnostics.mem_snapshot_max_bytes` | `262144` |  | bytes | Largest the snapshot file may be; the platform memory-map text is cut to fit. |
| `diagnostics.mem_snapshot_probe` | `vmmap, --summary, {pid}` |  |  | Command whose output goes into the snapshot as the platform's memory map of the daemon (macOS: vmmap summary); the program, then its arguments with `{pid}` substituted. Where /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup exists it is used instead. An empty list or a missing program leaves the field empty. |
| `diagnostics.mem_snapshot_probe_ms` | `4000` |  | ms | Longest the memory-map command may run. |
| `diagnostics.mem_snapshot_wait_ms` | `3000` |  | ms | Longest the snapshot waits for every worker to report its interpreter and caches (a busy worker reports after its request); workers that have not reported by then are listed as missing. |
| `diagnostics.msg_abandoned` | `abandoned at {site} (x{n}): {why}` |  |  | The event-log line for an abandoned decision. {site} is the counted site, {why} the reason with its key inputs, {n} how many were counted at the site since the last line. |
| `diagnostics.msg_file_refused` | `refused: {why}` |  |  | Said when `diag file` refuses an id: {why}. |
| `diagnostics.msg_file_usage` | `usage: ah-engine diag file <state:NAME\|defaults:NAME.toml\|transcript:AGENT>` |  |  | Usage of `diag file`. |
| `diagnostics.msg_integrity_usage` | `usage: ah-engine diag integrity <{stores}>` |  |  | Usage of `diag integrity`: {stores} is diagnostics.integrity_stores. |
| `diagnostics.outcome_map` | `10 entries` |  |  | How a duty or stage record's own outcome word maps onto the five accounting outcomes (ok, error, disabled, held, refused). A record that also names a gate is looked up as `<word>+gate`. A word not listed here counts as `error` so a new outcome cannot hide. |
| `diagnostics.profile` | `off` |  |  | Baseline profiling mode: off (default; the cost is one atomic load per call), sample (record one call in diagnostics.profile_sample_every) or full (record every call). Per-check CPU and allocation spans go to the bounded file diagnostics.profile_file. `ah-engine ctl profile on --for <dur>` raises the mode for a limited time and falls back to this value when the time is up. |
| `diagnostics.profile_file` | `profile.jsonl` |  |  | Name (in the state directory) of the profile span file: one JSON line per recorded check call. |
| `diagnostics.profile_max_bytes` | `4194304` |  | bytes | Size limit of the profile span file. When it is reached recording stops and the mode falls back to off (counted and logged); the file is never rotated or grown past this. |
| `diagnostics.profile_max_secs` | `600` |  | s | Longest a runtime `ctl profile on` stays on; a longer `--for` is cut to this, and an `on` without `--for` runs this long. |
| `diagnostics.profile_on_mode` | `full` |  |  | Mode `ctl profile on` switches to when none is named: sample or full. |
| `diagnostics.profile_sample_every` | `10` |  |  | In `sample` mode one check call in this many is recorded. |
| `diagnostics.shed_checks` | `1` |  |  | 1 (shipped) = past the HARD CPU limit (diagnostics.budget_cpu_hard_pct) the PURE-ADVICE checks of events that cannot block are not run (their answers are dropped, counted as answers_dropped reason `shed`). Checks listed in diagnostics.shed_never always run, and so do all checks of guard events. 0 = nothing is shed. |
| `diagnostics.shed_never` | `21 entries` |  |  | Checks that are never shed past the HARD CPU limit, with the reason for each: bookkeeping, recorders and deliveries that later guards or the user's agents depend on (shedding them loses state or messages). Any check of a non-guard event not listed here is pure advice and is shed. |
| `diagnostics.summary_read_bytes` | `8388608` |  | bytes | Most of the memory log (newest part) `status --memory` reads to build its summary. |
| `diagnostics.summary_top` | `10` |  |  | Rows shown per ranking (events, checks) in the memory summary of `ah-engine status --memory`. |
| `diagnostics.tally_hard_keys` | `256` |  |  | Hard limit on the labelled work counters (and on exited-thread names): a new key past it is dropped and counted in `tally_dropped`; the existing keys keep counting. |
| `diagnostics.tally_soft_keys` | `64` |  |  | Soft limit on the labelled work counters `status --threads` carries (and on exited-thread names): past it every further new key adds one to `tally_soft_hits`. |
| `diagnostics.threads_ctl` | `threads` |  |  | The control request that asks the daemon for one snapshot of every thread's CPU time and the work counters (the client asks twice, the window apart, and reports the difference). |
| `diagnostics.threads_flag` | `--threads` |  |  | The `ah-engine status` flag that reports the live daemon's per-thread CPU and work counters over a short window (`status --threads [--json]`). |
| `diagnostics.threads_name_max` | `64` |  |  | macOS: the size of the buffer a thread name is read into (the OS limit, MAXTHREADNAMESIZE). |
| `diagnostics.threads_proc_dir` | `/proc/self/task` |  |  | Linux: the directory listing this process's threads (each has a `stat` file with its CPU ticks and name). |
| `diagnostics.threads_proc_stat` | `stat` |  |  | Linux: the per-thread file holding the CPU ticks (fields 14 and 15) and the name. |
| `diagnostics.threads_window_ms` | `1000` | `AH_ENGINE_THREADS_WINDOW_MS` | ms | The window of `status --threads`: per-thread CPU % and counters per second are measured over this long. |
| `diagnostics.trace_dump_file` | `trace-dump.jsonl` |  |  | Name (in the state directory) of the file the trace ring is written to when a hard limit trips; each dump replaces the previous one. |
| `diagnostics.trace_dump_min_ms` | `60000` |  | ms | Shortest time between two automatic trace-ring dumps (a hard limit that trips again inside this time does not rewrite the file). |
| `diagnostics.trace_entries` | `512` |  |  | Size of the always-on trace ring (the most recent check, duty, stage and hand-back records kept in memory). Dumped by `diag trace` and written to diagnostics.trace_dump_file when a hard limit trips. Read at daemon start. |
| `diagnostics.trace_reason_cpu` | `cpu-budget` |  |  | Reason recorded in a trace-ring dump taken when a request trips its CPU budget. |
| `diagnostics.trace_reason_mem` | `memory-hard-limit` |  |  | Reason recorded in a trace-ring dump taken when the memory registry's hard limit trips. |
| `diagnostics.trace_reason_rss` | `rss-cap` |  |  | Reason recorded in a trace-ring dump taken when the resident-set cap trips. |
| `diagnostics.why_ext` | `this kind of file is never shown` |  |  | Reason: the file's kind is never shown. |
| `diagnostics.why_not_found` | `not found` |  |  | Reason: the file does not exist. |
| `diagnostics.why_not_plain_name` | `the name must be a plain file name` |  |  | Reason: the id names a path, not a plain file name. |
| `diagnostics.why_unknown_id` | `unknown id` |  |  | Reason: the id has no known prefix. |

| Key | Default | Env override | Unit | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mem.agent_scan_walk_hard_bytes` | `33554432` |  | bytes | Bytes of retained transcript agent-scan walks at which an insert is refused and the cache is recycled. |
| `mem.agent_scan_walk_low_water_pct` | `80` |  |  | Percent of mem.agent_scan_walk_soft_bytes the retained walk cache is evicted down to when the soft limit is reached. |
| `mem.agent_scan_walk_soft_bytes` | `16777216` |  | bytes | Bytes of retained transcript agent-scan walks held before the least recently used are dropped down to the low-water mark. |
| `mem.buckets_hard_bytes` | `1048576` |  | bytes | Estimated bytes of daemon session and project token-bucket keys at which unknown keys are refused and recoverable buckets are recycled. |
| `mem.buckets_low_water_pct` | `80` |  |  | Percent of mem.buckets_soft_bytes token buckets are evicted down to when the soft limit is reached. |
| `mem.buckets_soft_bytes` | `262144` |  | bytes | Estimated bytes of daemon session and project token-bucket keys held before idle/full buckets are evicted down to the low-water mark. |
| `mem.db_kv_hard_bytes` | `8388608` |  | bytes | Estimated bytes of active project key-value items at which inserts are refused and the in-memory KV tier is recycled. |
| `mem.db_kv_low_water_pct` | `80` |  |  | Percent of mem.db_kv_soft_bytes active project key-value items are evicted down to when the soft limit is reached. |
| `mem.db_kv_soft_bytes` | `4194304` |  | bytes | Estimated bytes of active project key-value items held in memory before least recently used items are evicted down to the low-water mark. |
| `mem.defaults_leak_hard_bytes` | `33554432` |  | bytes | Bytes of leaked config values past which the daemon requests a clean restart (after mem.global_restart_after_s), so repeated config reloads cannot grow the process without bound. |
| `mem.defaults_leak_low_water_pct` | `80` |  |  | Percent of mem.defaults_leak_soft_bytes the leaked total must be at or under before the soft trigger re-arms (only a restart lowers it). |
| `mem.defaults_leak_soft_bytes` | `16777216` |  | bytes | Bytes of config values leaked on purpose (the `'static` snapshots of the defaults, the previous generation of every derived cache) that are logged as a soft excursion. Only a restart frees them; one load of the shipped config leaks about 3.4 MB (measured), and a reload adds only what changed. |
| `mem.devswarm_ingest_hard_bytes` | `1048576` |  | bytes | Estimated bytes held by DevSwarm ingest project scheduling state at which new idle project entries are refused and recoverable state is recycled. |
| `mem.devswarm_ingest_idle_ttl_ms` | `600000` |  | ms | How long a DevSwarm ingest project may be idle before its resident drain worker is stopped and its slot becomes available. |
| `mem.devswarm_ingest_low_water_pct` | `80` |  |  | Percent of mem.devswarm_ingest_soft_bytes the DevSwarm ingest project state is evicted down to when the soft limit is reached. |
