| `upfront.msg_skip_set` | `Guards skipped for this session on the owner's say-so: {guards}.` |  |  | Line for guard skips being active; {guards} the names. |
| `upfront.msg_spawn_stop` | `Agent spawning is stopped ({reason}): do the work inline, in small bounded st...` |  |  | Line for spawning being unavailable; {reason} is rendered from standdown.reasons. |
| `upfront.setting` | `6 entries` |  |  | Switch guards.upfrontNotice (default on): one short line when a session-wide switch changes (spawn stop, limit conserve, a guard skip set or expired), at the next prompt or tool call. |
| `upfront.summary` | `Run by the dispatcher on UserPromptSubmit and PreToolUse (an engine-only disp...` |  |  | One-line description of the switch-notice check in the generated reference. |

## Messages

Text lives in `messages.toml` (and `git.toml` for the git check's block messages); keys and what they are for:

| Key | When it is shown |
|---|---|
| `msg.advisory_defaults` | Appended to the degraded notice when defaults fell back to another layer. Placeholders: {count} fallbacks in the window, {last} the last one's detail. |
| `msg.advisory_degraded` | Once-per-session notice that the engine is running below full strength. Placeholders: {restarts} self-restarts and {fallbacks} fallbacks to Node in the last {mins} minutes, {log} the event-log path. |
| `msg.advisory_env` | Once-per-session advisory for an environment-class failure. Placeholder: {hint}. |
| `msg.advisory_permanent` | Once-per-session advisory for a permanent failure; nothing is ever filed automatically. Placeholders: {reason}, {diagnostics}. |
| `msg.backup_exists` | A backup destination already holds a snapshot. Placeholder: {path}. |
| `msg.cli_help` | Printed for `ah-engine <command> --help` (or -h): usage only, nothing runs. Placeholders: {command}, {args} (the command's argument form from the command registry), {doc} (what the command does). |
| `msg.cli_no_daemon` | Printed to stderr when a control command finds no daemon. |
| `msg.cli_not_running` | Printed in place of a report when no daemon is running (`--json` output carries running=false). |
| `msg.cli_planned` | Printed when a planned command is run. Placeholders: {command}, {decision}. |
| `msg.cli_unknown` | Printed to stderr for an unknown command. Placeholder: {command}. |
| `msg.cli_usage` | Usage text for an unknown or missing subcommand. The command list is generated from the command registry. |
| `msg.client_ack_timeout` | Health-log and exchange text: the daemon did not acknowledge a request within wire.ack_timeout_ms. |
| `msg.client_bad_frame` | Exchange failure when the reply frame was damaged. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.client_bad_socket` | Exchange failure when the socket path is not a socket owned by this user. |
| `msg.client_closed_before_ack` | Exchange text: the daemon closed the connection before it acknowledged the request. |
| `msg.client_connect` | Exchange failure when connecting failed. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.client_hung` | Log detail for a hook call that stopped waiting because the daemon's heartbeat is stale, seen for the first time (a suspicion, nothing is signalled). {pid} = the daemon, {age} = the heartbeat's age in ms. |
| `msg.client_hung_confirmed` | Log detail for a hook call that stopped waiting because the daemon's heartbeat stayed stale and unchanged past client.heartbeat_confirm_ms (a confirmed hang). {pid} = the daemon, {age} = the heartbeat's age in ms, {held} = how long the same heartbeat was seen unchanged in ms. |
| `msg.client_io` | Exchange failure for another I/O step. Placeholders: {what}, {err}. |
| `msg.client_no_verdict` | Event-log detail and stderr reason when the engine answered a hook call with no verdict (BUSY, ERR or a damaged reply) on a guard event: the event's configured failure mode (dispatch.failure_mode, path infra) answers. |
| `msg.client_skip` | Log detail for a hook call that skipped the daemon because a down marker, the breaker or the crash-loop cooldown was active. |
| `msg.client_timeout` | Exchange failure when the hard deadline passed. |
| `msg.client_unavailable` | Printed on stderr when stdin cannot safely be sent to the engine (undecodable or oversized). Guard events exit 2; non-guard events exit 0 with this note. |
| `msg.client_what_stat` | The step named in msg.client_io when the socket path cannot be examined (a permission or path error, not a missing socket). |
| `msg.cold_guard_notice` | Printed once per session on stderr when a guard event gave up waiting for a cold-starting daemon and was let through unchecked; {event} is the event name. |
| `msg.daemon_already_running` | Printed on stderr when a second daemon start finds an existing daemon/lock holder for the socket. Placeholders: {path}, {pid}, {live_engine}, {answers}. |
| `msg.dbg_cpu_window` | Debug-log line for one CPU self-check window of the daemon. Placeholders: {ms} (window length), {pct} (percent of one core). |
| `msg.dbg_hook` | Debug-log line for one finished hook invocation of the client. Placeholders: {code} (exit code), {out} and {err} (bytes written), {us} (microseconds spent). |
| `msg.dbg_request` | Debug-log line for a served daemon request. Placeholders: {request}, {event}, {depth} (queued connections), {busy} (busy workers). |
| `msg.diagnostics` | Secret-scrubbed diagnostic block attached to a permanent-failure advisory. Placeholders: {version}, {os}, {arch}, {code}, {log}. |
| `msg.dispatch_stdin_spool` | Reason (event log and stderr, with dispatch.defer_exit) when the hook's stdin payload cannot be read, or an over-cap payload cannot be spooled for the Node hooks. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.dispatch_stdin_utf8` | Reason in dispatch.msg_fail_closed when a guard event's stdin payload is not valid UTF-8. |
| `msg.docs_checks_note` | Paragraph under the checks heading of the generated reference. |
| `msg.docs_empty` | Printed to stderr when `docs` generated no text (the defaults it reads could not be used), so nothing is written. Placeholders: what (the format asked for), out (the --out file, left as it was; empty when printing). |
| `msg.docs_env_intro` | Introduction of the Environment variables section of the generated reference. |
| `msg.docs_flags_intro` | Introduction of the Flags section of the generated reference. |
| `msg.docs_intro` | Opening paragraph of the generated reference. |
| `msg.docs_rule_fields` | Paragraph listing the fields of a rule in the generated reference. |
| `msg.docs_write_failed` | Printed to stderr when `docs --out` could not write its file. Placeholders: out, err. |
| `msg.engine_unreachable_notice` | Printed once per session on stderr by the thin client when the engine is unreachable (not installed, crashed, did not answer in time, marked down): the call passes through unchecked because no fallback hooks exist. Placeholders: {event}, {why}. |
| `msg.engine_unreachable_why_daemon` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the client could not reach the engine's daemon (down, breaker open, crash-loop stop). |
| `msg.err_db_busy` | The storage writer queue is full. |
| `msg.err_db_journal` | The journal mode could not be set. Placeholder: {mode}. |
| `msg.err_db_schema` | A database was written by a newer build of the engine. Placeholders: {db}, {found}, {known}. |
| `msg.err_db_sql` | A storage operation failed inside SQLite. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.err_db_timeout` | A write did not commit in time; it may still commit, and its write id makes a retry harmless. |
| `msg.err_db_unavailable` | Storage is not open. |
| `msg.err_mailbox_full` | The project mailbox is full. |
| `msg.err_mesh_ambiguous_store` | The workspace id is in more than one project store. Placeholders: {id}, {stores} (comma separated repo keys). |
| `msg.err_mesh_backend` | A mesh reader refused a store directory whose BACKEND marker is not sqlite. Placeholders: {path}, {backend}. |
| `msg.err_mesh_missing` | A mesh reader was pointed at a store file that does not exist (a reader never creates one). Placeholder: {path}. |
| `msg.err_mesh_no_project` | The store reader was run without --db from a directory that is in no DevSwarm project (or whose project has no store yet). Placeholder: {cwd}. |
| `msg.err_mesh_range` | A store value is an integer JavaScript cannot represent exactly, which Node's reader rejects too. Placeholder: {value}. |
| `msg.err_mesh_read_id` | `mesh read` of the store reader was given no workspace id. The broadcast read is the mesh verb `mesh mesh read`. |
| `msg.err_mesh_sql` | A mesh read failed in SQLite or hit a value it cannot read the way Node does. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.err_mesh_usage` | The mesh command was called without a verb (or the store reader without a store). |
| `msg.err_not_dir` | A state or socket directory is not a plain directory. Placeholder: {path}. |
| `msg.err_path_io` | An OS error on a path. Placeholders: {path}, {err}. |
| `msg.err_rules_action` | A rule has an unknown action. Placeholders: {index}, {action}. |
| `msg.err_rules_check` | A rule names an unknown check. Placeholders: {index}, {name}. |
| `msg.err_rules_json` | Rules file is not valid JSON. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.err_rules_pattern` | A rule's pattern is not a valid regular expression. Placeholders: {index}, {id}, {err}. |
| `msg.err_rules_version` | Rules file version is not supported. Placeholder: {version}. |
| `msg.err_too_many_keys` | The project key limit was reached. |
| `msg.err_too_many_projects` | The project partition limit was reached. |
| `msg.err_unknown_check` | `check` was asked for a check that is not registered. Placeholder: {name}. |
| `msg.err_unknown_verb` | A project operation verb is not known. Placeholder: {verb}. |
| `msg.err_value_too_large` | A stored value exceeds the per-value cap. |
| `msg.err_wrong_owner` | A state or socket directory belongs to another user. Placeholders: {path}, {found}, {expected}. |
| `msg.exit_reason_handoff` | Drain reason for a handoff to a newer build or a stop request. |
| `msg.exit_reason_idle` | Drain reason for idle exit (only when daemon.idle_exit_s is set). |
| `msg.exit_reason_rss` | Drain reason for exceeding the memory cap. |
| `msg.exit_reason_sigterm` | Drain reason for SIGTERM. |
| `msg.exit_reason_stall` | Drain reason for a stalled loop. |
| `msg.exit_reason_stuck` | Drain reason for a stuck worker. |
| `msg.failure_stall` | Failure reason when the accept loop stalled. |
| `msg.failure_stuck` | Failure reason when a worker is stuck. |
| `msg.fallback_read_timeout` | Printed on stderr when the Node fallback finished but its output could not be read to the end in time, so no decision exists. In the legacy direct forced-fallback path this exits 2 for guard events and 0 for non-guard events; otherwise it exits 1. |
| `msg.hint_disk_full` | Self-fix hint when the disk is full (error code os28). |
| `msg.hint_fds` | Self-fix hint when the process ran out of file descriptors. |
| `msg.hint_memory` | Self-fix hint when the OS killed or starved the daemon. Placeholder: {env_mem}. |
| `msg.hint_socket_path` | Self-fix hint when the socket path is too long. Placeholder: {env_dir}. |
| `msg.hint_state_dir` | Self-fix hint when the state directory is not writable or not private. Placeholders: {state_dir}, {env_dir}. |
| `msg.impact_no_routing` | Status shown in place of a model-routing saving figure while no routing events are recorded. |
| `msg.install_done` | Printed by `hooks/install.sh --download` when it installed the binaries. Placeholders: {version}, {triple}, {path}. |
| `msg.install_failed` | Printed on stderr by `hooks/install.sh --download` when the install did not complete. Placeholder: {why}. |
| `msg.install_notice` | The one line per session hooks/install.sh prints on stderr while the thin client is not installed (hook calls pass through unchecked). |
| `msg.install_unsupported` | Printed by `ah-hook install --print-target` on a platform without a release build. |
| `msg.inv_busy_workers` | Invariant violation: more workers are marked busy than there are workers. Placeholder: {workers}. |
| `msg.inv_queue_pop` | Invariant violation: after a worker took a connection, the queue-depth counter and the queue length differ. Placeholders: {depth}, {len}. |
| `msg.inv_queue_push` | Invariant violation: after the accept loop queued a connection, the queue-depth counter and the queue length differ. Placeholders: {depth}, {len}. |
| `msg.inv_violated` | Debug-log line for a violated runtime invariant (checked only in debug mode). Placeholder: {what}, the specific check that failed. |
| `msg.jev_slow` | Log detail (code jev_slow, rate-limited) of a Jev call slower than its SOFT limit; its answer was still used. |
| `msg.launcher_bad_host` | Printed when --host names a host the launcher does not serve; the default host is used. |
| `msg.launcher_config_invalid` | Log line when a defaults file is missing or invalid and the built-in copy is used; {file} names it. |
| `msg.launcher_cpu_hard` | Printed when the launcher passed its hard CPU limit and let the hook through. |
| `msg.launcher_fail_closed` | Printed when a guard event is blocked because the launcher cannot run it safely; {event} is the event, {why} the reason. |
| `msg.launcher_fail_open_stop` | Printed instead of blocking when the event is a stop hook that is already active; {event} and {why} as above. |
| `msg.launcher_ignored_knobs` | Printed when test-only variables are set without the test flag; {vars} lists them. |
| `msg.launcher_integrity_status` | Printed by `ah-hook integrity status`. Placeholders: {binary}, {installed}, {expected}, {healthy}, {good}, {last} (the sha256s are empty when not known). |
| `msg.launcher_integrity_usage` | Printed by `ah-hook integrity` for a verb it does not know. |
| `msg.launcher_internal` | Printed (once) when the launcher itself failed and let the hook through; {what} is the failure. |
| `msg.launcher_mem_hard` | Printed when the launcher passed its hard heap limit and let the hook through. |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_merge_differs` | Written when the JSON answers of several fallback hooks carry different fields besides the merged additionalContext and systemMessage; the first hook's fields are kept. |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_script_missing` | Written when a fallback command names a script under the plugin root that does not exist; that hook is skipped and counted as an error. Placeholder: {path}. |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_why_hard` | The reason a guard event fails closed when a fallback hook died or could not be started and no hook blocked. |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_why_no_list` | The reason a guard event fails closed while the Node fallback switch is on and the fallback list is missing or empty. |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_why_no_match` | The reason a guard event fails closed when no fallback hook matches its tool (the list has no neutral answer). |
| `msg.launcher_nodeback_why_not_run` | The reason a guard event fails closed when matching fallback hooks existed but none finished. |
| `msg.launcher_selftest_fail` | Selftest line for a failing check; {check} names it, {why} the reason. |
| `msg.launcher_selftest_ok` | Selftest line for a passing check; {check} names it. |
| `msg.launcher_st_cannot_start` | Selftest reason: the engine binary could not be started; {errno} is the system error number. |
| `msg.launcher_st_incoherent` | Selftest reason: settings contradict each other; {rules} names the broken rules. |
| `msg.launcher_st_mem_below` | Selftest reason: the hard heap limit is below the heap already in use. |
| `msg.launcher_st_missing` | Selftest reason: shipped settings the launcher needs are missing or of the wrong type; {keys} names them. |
| `msg.launcher_st_no_engine` | Selftest reason: no engine binary is installed. |
| `msg.launcher_st_no_state` | Selftest reason: there is no state directory. |
| `msg.launcher_st_no_wall` | Selftest reason: the wall-clock backstop could not be armed. |
| `msg.launcher_st_not_exec` | Selftest reason: the named engine binary is not an executable file. |
| `msg.launcher_st_socket_len` | Selftest reason: the socket path is longer than the operating system allows. |
| `msg.launcher_st_unusable` | Selftest reason: a defaults file is missing or invalid; {files} names them. |
| `msg.launcher_st_ver_empty` | Selftest reason: the engine's version check printed nothing. |
| `msg.launcher_st_ver_exit` | Selftest reason: the engine's version check failed with exit code {code}. |
| `msg.launcher_st_ver_timeout` | Selftest reason: the engine's version check did not finish in {ms} ms. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_down` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the daemon-down marker is fresh. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_handed_back` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the engine handed the call back. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_missing` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when no engine is installed. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_not_started` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the engine could not be started. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_silent` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the engine exited without an answer. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_timed_out` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the engine did not answer in time. |
| `msg.launcher_unreachable_why_unfinished` | The {why} of the engine-unreachable notice when the engine did not finish. |
| `msg.launcher_update_no_settings` | Printed by `ah-hook update` when the plugin's settings lack a key it needs. Placeholder: {key}. |
| `msg.launcher_wall_hard` | Printed when the launcher passed its wall-clock backstop and let the hook through. |
| `msg.launcher_why_timeout_ms` | Reason: the milliseconds budget knob is not a positive integer. |
| `msg.launcher_why_timeout_s` | Reason: the seconds budget knob is not a positive integer. |
| `msg.log_accept_error` | Event-log detail (rate-limited) when the daemon's accept failed for a reason other than nothing pending. Placeholders: {code} (os<n>), {err}. |
| `msg.log_accept_recovered` | Event-log detail when the daemon accepts a connection again after accept failures (logged then, because a full descriptor table can keep the failure's own log line from being written). Placeholders: {n}, {code} (os<n> of the last failure). |
| `msg.log_allocator_invalid` | Event-log detail (kind alloc_invalid) when diagnostics.allocator holds a value that is not an accepted allocator; the daemon starts with jemalloc. Placeholder: {value}. |
| `msg.log_answer_dropped` | Event-log detail (kinds answer_dropped and guard_answer_dropped, at most one per check and reason per diagnostics.abandoned_log_interval_ms) when a check of a request gave no answer. Reasons: shed (CPU hard limit, diagnostics.shed_checks), client_gone (the client closed its connection), hard_deadline (the request passed daemon.request_hard_ms), cpu_budget (this check alone used more than daemon.eval_budget_us), check_deferred (the check itself gave no answer). The check's failure policy decides in its place. |
| `msg.log_bind_fail` | Start-failure detail when binding the socket fails. Placeholders: {path}, {err}. |
| `msg.log_budget` | Log detail when a rule evaluation exceeded its CPU budget. |
| `msg.log_budget_cpu` | Event-log detail when the daemon CPU budget is breached or back within budget. Placeholders: {state}, {value} (percent of one core over the last window), {limit} (the budget, percent). |
| `msg.log_budget_cpu_hard` | Event-log detail when the daemon passes its HARD CPU limit and starts shedding optional work, or recovers. Placeholders: {state}, {value} (percent of one core over the last window), {limit} (the hard limit, percent), {soft} (the soft limit, percent). |
| `msg.log_budget_crossed` | Log detail when a check ran and crossed the per-check CPU budget (daemon.eval_budget_us) alone, so its answer was dropped: the check's own thread CPU and wall time. |
| `msg.log_budget_mem` | Event-log detail when the daemon memory budget is breached or back within budget. Placeholders: {state}, {value} (MB), {limit} (the budget, MB). |
| `msg.log_budget_skipped` | Log detail when a check was not started because the request's CPU budget was already spent; `by` names the check that crossed it (empty when it was crossed before the first check). |
| `msg.log_budget_soft` | Log detail when a request used more thread CPU than its SOFT budget (a warning; nothing was cut). |
| `msg.log_client_panic` | Log detail when the hook client hit an internal error (a panic) and failed open. |
| `msg.log_cpu_sustained` | Event-log detail when the daemon CPU self-check observes sustained CPU and backs off scheduled jobs. Placeholders: {pct}, {ms}, {backoff_ms}. |
| `msg.log_crash_context` | Log detail when a daemon is found dead without a clean exit, with the last breadcrumb. Placeholders: {pid}, {context}. |
| `msg.log_crashloop_new_binary` | Log detail when a crash-loop cooldown ends because the binary was replaced. Placeholder: {sha}. |
| `msg.log_crashloop_rollback` | Log detail added when a crash-loop trip also requested a roll-back. |
| `msg.log_daemon_killed` | Log detail when the daemon was killed by a signal while starting. |
| `msg.log_daemon_spawn_failed` | Event-log detail (kind spawn_fail, code os<n>) when the client could not start the daemon (fork or exec failed: EAGAIN, ENOMEM, a missing executable). Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.log_deadline_soft` | Log detail when the client's fail-fast wait (the request's SOFT deadline) ended while a check was running: the request is {elapsed_ms} ms old and that check ran {ran_ms} ms. Nothing is cut: the checks keep running up to the hard deadline and the client uses the late reply. |
| `msg.log_deadline_soft_queued` | Log detail when the client's fail-fast wait (the request's SOFT deadline) had already ended before the first check of the request started, so the request waited {elapsed_ms} ms (queue, connection) before any check ran. {check} is the first check of the request. Nothing is cut. |
| `msg.log_debug_off` | Event-log detail when debug mode turns off (the setting was switched off and neither the environment variable nor the flag holds it on). |
| `msg.log_debug_on` | Event-log detail when debug mode turns on (the setting, the environment variable or the flag). |
| `msg.log_fallback_read_timeout` | Log detail when the Node fallback finished but its stdout or stderr was still open at the deadline. |
| `msg.log_hung_kill` | Log detail when a client ends a hung daemon (verified pid) so a new one can start. {pid} = the ended daemon, {why} = the stale-heartbeat detail. |
| `msg.log_hung_spared` | Log detail when a client declines to end a daemon it found hung, because the heartbeat moved, or the process generation (pid, start time, executable, state dir) could not be confirmed. {pid} = the pid the heartbeat names, {why} = the stale-heartbeat detail. |
| `msg.log_lock_fail` | Start-failure detail when the lock file cannot be opened. Placeholders: {path}, {err}. |
| `msg.log_lock_no_daemon` | Log detail when a starting daemon gives up on the singleton lock while no daemon answers on the socket. Placeholders: {path}, {pid} (the pid the lock file names, may be empty), {live_engine}. |
| `msg.log_malloc_decay_applied` | Event-log detail (kind malloc_decay) when the daemon, started without the allocator tuning in its environment, applied the decay settings of daemon.malloc_conf at runtime. Placeholder: {settings} (key=value list). |
| `msg.log_malloc_decay_skipped` | Event-log detail (kind malloc_decay) when the allocator decay settings could not be applied at start; the daemon runs with the allocator's own defaults. Placeholder: {reason}. |
| `msg.log_not_socket` | Start-failure detail when something other than a socket sits at the socket path. Placeholder: {path}. |
| `msg.log_operator_reset` | Log detail for `reset`. |
| `msg.log_panic` | Log and failure detail when a request handler panicked. |
| `msg.log_proc_spawn` | Event-log detail (rate-limited, code proc_spawn_failed) when a helper process could not be started. Placeholders: {what} (the program), {code} (os<n>), {err}. |
| `msg.log_proc_timeout` | Event-log detail (rate-limited, code proc_timeout) when a helper process ran past its timeout and its process group was killed. Placeholders: {what}, {ms}. |
| `msg.log_proc_unread` | Event-log detail (rate-limited, code proc_unread) when a helper exited but its output did not reach end of file within proc.read_grace_ms (a process it left behind held a pipe); its group was killed. Placeholder: {what}. |
| `msg.log_pruned` | Event-log detail when maintenance forgets old applied write ids. Placeholder: {n}. |
| `msg.log_restored` | Event-log detail of a restore. Placeholders: {from}, {kept}. |
| `msg.log_rollback_request` | Log detail when the crash-loop rule asks for a roll-back. Placeholder: {sha}. |
| `msg.log_rss` | Log detail when the daemon is over its memory cap. Placeholders: {rss}, {cap}. |
| `msg.log_stall` | Log detail when the accept loop stalled. |
| `msg.log_start` | Log detail for a daemon start. Placeholders: {version}, {pid}, {rlimit}. |
| `msg.log_stuck` | Log detail when a worker is stuck. Placeholder: {i}. |
| `msg.log_system_restart` | Log detail when a daemon is found gone without a clean exit AND the operating system booted after its last sign of life (a reboot, an OS update, a power loss): the machine stopped it, it did not crash. Placeholders: {pid}, {last_alive_ms}, {boot_ms}. |
| `msg.metrics_quantile_note` | Printed with every latency histogram: how to read its percentiles. |
| `msg.net_not_measured` | Listed in net.not_measured for a part of the NET figure that has no data in the window. Placeholder: {name}. |
| `msg.no_price_for_model` | Said by `impact` for a model that is not in the price table, instead of a guessed figure. Placeholder: {model}. |
| `msg.obs_counter_write_failed` | Log line when a counter could not be appended to the journal (the count is lost; nothing else changes). |
| `msg.obs_diag_unknown` | Printed when `diag` is given a topic that is not in diagnostics.diag_topics. |
| `msg.obs_diag_usage` | Usage of `ah-engine diag`; {topics} is the list in diagnostics.diag_topics. |
| `msg.obs_profile_bad_duration` | Reply to a `--for` value that is not a number with an optional unit suffix. |
| `msg.obs_profile_off` | Log line when a runtime profiling window ends or is switched off; {why} is off, expired or full-file. |
| `msg.obs_profile_on` | Log line when a runtime profiling window starts. |
| `msg.obs_profile_usage` | Usage of `ah-engine ctl profile`. |
| `msg.obs_trace_dump_failed` | Log line when the trace ring could not be written. |
| `msg.obs_trace_dumped` | Log line when the trace ring is written because a hard limit tripped. |
| `msg.panic_payload_unknown` | Panic payload text when Rust did not carry a string. |
| `msg.panic_row` | Event-log detail for a panic: message and source location first so the row's length cap never cuts them; the backtrace lives only in the crash file. Placeholders: {message}, {location}, {thread}, {context}. |
| `msg.reason_breaker` | Recorded reason when the client breaker opens. Placeholders: {n}, {secs}, {why}. |
| `msg.reason_crashloop` | Recorded reason when the daemon keeps dying. Placeholders: {n}, {secs}. |
| `msg.regex_literal_invalid` | Panic text when a literal regular expression in the source does not compile (a bug the tests catch). |
| `msg.reply_budget` | ERR body when evaluation exceeded the CPU budget. |
| `msg.reply_busy_detail` | Fail-open detail of a request that was shed (queue full or rate limited) and answered BUSY. |
| `msg.reply_defer` | ERR body when a built-in check defers to the Node hook. |
| `msg.reply_internal` | ERR body after a contained panic. |
| `msg.reply_malformed` | ERR body for a hook payload that is not JSON. |
| `msg.reply_missing_cwd` | ERR body for a project request without a cwd. |
| `msg.reply_read_deadline` | ERR body when the client did not deliver its request in time. |
| `msg.reply_read_error` | ERR body for a socket read error. |
| `msg.reply_test_panic` | Panic text of the test-only `panic` verb. |
| `msg.reply_too_large` | ERR body for an oversize request. |

| `msg.layer_why_incomplete` | Reason: a rule with a new id has no action (only a rule that changes a lower layer's rule may leave fields out). Placeholder: {id}. |
| `msg.layer_why_len` | Reason: a rule field is too long. Placeholders: {id}, {field}, {max}. |
| `msg.layer_why_loosen_action` | Reason: the rule would get a less strict action. Placeholders: {id}, {from}, {to}. |
| `msg.layer_why_loosen_field` | Reason: the field would change a rule of a lower layer (narrowing it). Placeholders: {id}, {field}. |
| `msg.layer_why_loosen_off` | Reason: the rule would be switched off. |
| `msg.layer_why_no_id` | Reason: a project rule has no id, so it cannot be told apart from another. |
| `msg.layer_why_not_file` | Reason: the path is not a plain file (a symlink, a pipe, a directory). |
| `msg.layer_why_regex` | Reason: the pattern does not compile (or is over layers.regex_size_limit). Placeholders: {id}, {err}. |
| `msg.layer_why_setting_dir` | Reason: a layers.project_settings entry has no known direction. Placeholder: {key}. |
| `msg.layer_why_setting_loosen` | Reason: the project value is less strict than the one below it. Placeholders: {key}, {value}, {below}, {dir}. |
| `msg.layer_why_setting_unlisted` | Reason: the project file names a setting that is not in layers.project_settings. Placeholder: {key}. |
| `msg.layer_why_size` | Reason: the file is over layers.max_file_bytes. |
| `msg.layer_why_toml` | Reason: the text is not valid TOML. Placeholder: {err}. |
| `msg.layer_why_top` | Reason: a rule file may only hold `rules` (an array of tables). Placeholder: {key}. |
| `msg.layer_why_type` | Reason: a rule field has the wrong type. Placeholders: {id}, {field}. |
| `msg.jev_bad_default_mode` | Why the shipped integration table is invalid: an integration lists a mode that is not on, shadow or off. Placeholder: id. |
| `msg.jev_endpoint_ignored` | Printed once per process to stderr when a test endpoint override is refused because its host is not loopback; it never names the URL or a key. |
| `msg.jev_generic_key_bound` | Why a vendor-less Jev key option was not used: it is bound to the other vendor. Placeholders: bound, option, vendor. |
| `msg.jev_key_multiline` | Why a Jev key file was refused: its content is not a single line without whitespace. |
| `msg.jev_key_not_file` | Why a Jev key file was refused: it is not a regular file. |
| `msg.jev_key_outside_roots` | Why a Jev key file was refused: it does not really live under one of the allowed directories. |
| `msg.jev_key_too_large` | Why a Jev key file was refused: it is larger than the limit. Placeholder: max. |
| `msg.jev_key_unreadable` | Why a Jev key file was refused: it could not be read. |
| `msg.jev_no_home` | Printed by `ah-engine jev` when the home directory variable is not set, because the settings and the log live under it. |
| `msg.jev_unknown_question_type` | Why a Jev request was refused: its question type is neither noul nor choice. Placeholder: kind. |
| `msg.jev_usage` | Usage line of `ah-engine jev`. |
| `msg.jev_arrival_done` | The one line `ah-engine jev arrival` prints: the outcome word of the run and its counts. |
| `msg.cli_usage_restore` | The usage line of `restore`. |
| `msg.cli_usage_schedule_run` | The usage line of `schedule run`. |
| `msg.client_what_timeout` | What the client was doing when a socket option could not be set (the {what} of msg.client_io). |
| `msg.agent_act_child` | Appended to the escalation when the live coordinator of a hung subagent or teammate was asked to stop it. Placeholder: {parent}. |
| `msg.agent_act_child_request` | The stop request queued for the coordinator of a hung subagent or teammate. Placeholders: {agent} (its id), {name}. |
| `msg.agent_act_codex` | Appended to the escalation when a hung one-shot Codex run was sent SIGTERM. Placeholder: {pid}. |
| `msg.agent_act_none` | Appended to the escalation when the action found nothing it may stop (no single pid matched, or no live coordinator). |
| `msg.agent_act_workspace` | Appended to the escalation when a hung DevSwarm workspace was asked to stop. |
| `msg.agent_armed_lapsed` | What {armed} reads when the last one has lapsed; {ago} is how long ago. |
| `msg.agent_armed_never` | What {armed} reads when no wake path was ever armed in the transcript window. |
| `msg.agent_disabled` | What a tick prints when the tracker switch is off. |
| `msg.agent_drift` | Correction reminder: recent work does not match the declared step. Placeholders: {agent}, {step}, {overlap}. |
| `msg.agent_heartbeat_stale` | Reminder: a heartbeat file went stale. Placeholders: {agent}, {age}, {step}. |
| `msg.agent_hung` | Advisory: an agent has produced no output for too long. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {idle}, {tool}. |
| `msg.agent_idle_open_task` | Wake advisory: an agent finished its turn with a task open and went quiet. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {idle}, {task}. |
| `msg.agent_looping` | Advisory: an agent repeats the same call. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {count}, {what}. |
| `msg.agent_monitor_unarmed` | Reminder to arm a wake path (generic sessions), one short line. Placeholders: {count}, {armed}. |
| `msg.agent_monitor_unarmed_devswarm` | Reminder to arm the wake-watch (DevSwarm workspaces). Placeholders: {command}. |
| `msg.agent_no_tool` | What {tool} reads when the agent's last activity was not a tool call. |
| `msg.agent_no_work` | Advisory to the coordinator: a subagent ended without doing anything. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {tools}. |
| `msg.agent_status_empty` | What `agents status` prints when no agent is tracked. |
| `msg.agent_status_source` | The status footer for the Claude Code CLI source. Placeholders: {version}, {ok}. |
| `msg.agent_status_source_off` | The word for a CLI source that is unavailable or unverified on this version (the transcripts are used). |
| `msg.agent_status_source_ok` | The word for a working CLI source. |
| `msg.agent_status_totals` | The summary line under the status table. Placeholders: {agents}, {flagged}, {signals}, {queued}, {delivered}, {suppressed}, {recovered}, {fp}, {burned}. |
| `msg.agent_token_waste` | Advisory: an agent spends tokens with no progress. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {tokens}, {window}. |
| `msg.agent_usage` | Usage line of `ah-engine agents`. |
| `msg.agent_wake_line` | The stdout line the wake-watch prints for one wake row; this is what the host delivers to the idle session. Placeholder: {text}. |
| `msg.agent_wake_reason_held` | Why the wake-watch did not arm: another live watcher already covers this session. |
| `msg.agent_wake_reason_no_session` | Why the wake-watch did not arm: no session id in the environment. |
| `msg.agent_wake_reason_off` | Why the wake-watch did not arm: a switch is off (agents.tracker or agents.wakeWatch). |
| `msg.agent_wake_refused` | Printed by a wake-watch started by hand (not --auto) that declines to arm. Placeholder: {reason}. |
| `msg.agent_watched_exit` | Wake advisory: a background shell task an agent started has ended. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {count}, {task}. |
| `msg.native_wake_prompt` | The prompt `workspace reactivate-child` queues for an idle workspace; it only sends the workspace to its mesh inbox. Placeholders: {prefix} (agent_tracker.wake_prefix), {id} (the workspace), {text} (a short preview, may be empty). |
| `msg.agent_waste` | Advisory: an agent spends tokens without matching outcomes. Placeholders: {agent}, {kind}, {score}, {source} (judge or formula), {verdict}, {window}, {reason}. |
| `msg.lock_stall` | Wake notice to the coordinator: the process holding a shared lock is idle while others wait. Placeholders: {lock}, {pid}, {cmd}, {idle_min}, {waiters}, {term} (empty, or the auto-action sentence). |
| `msg.lock_stall_term` | Appended to the wake notice when the auto-action sent SIGTERM. Placeholder: {pid}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge` | The nudge to the direct parent. Placeholders: {kind}, {name}, {dur} (how long the child has run), {tokens} (k/M), {evidence}, {walked} (empty, or msg.agent_nudge_walked), {answer} (msg.agent_nudge_answer). |
| `msg.agent_nudge_acted` | Owner notice after the stop action ran on an escalated child. Placeholders: {kind}, {name}, {action} (one of the msg.agent_act_* sentences). |
| `msg.agent_nudge_answer` | How a nudge tells the parent to answer. Placeholders: {ref} (the nudge's ref token), {cmd}, {child} (the child's id). |
| `msg.agent_nudge_dead` | The notice about a child that died (no question). Placeholders: {kind}, {name}, {when} (how long ago it last wrote), {why}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_dead_batch` | The one line that replaces more dead notices than limits.dead_per_target for one target in a tick. Placeholders: {n}, {project}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_escalate` | The escalation on the owner's channel. Placeholders: {kind}, {name}, {parent}, {evidence}, {why}, {answer}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_need_reason` | Refusal of `other` without a reason. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_recorded` | Confirmation that an answer was recorded. Placeholders: {child}, {answer}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_repeat` | A repeat of an unanswered nudge (short). Placeholders: {n} (the reminder number), {kind}, {name}, {evidence}, {answer}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_usage` | Usage of the nudge answer verb. Placeholder: {cmd}. |
| `msg.agent_nudge_walked` | Added to a nudge that went past a parent that is not live. Placeholder: {direct} (the direct parent). |

## Metrics

| Name | Kind | Unit | Labels | What it counts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `accept_errors` | counter | errors | code | Accept calls that failed for a reason other than nothing pending (EMFILE, ENFILE, ENOBUFS, ENOMEM), by OS error code (os<n>); each one backs the accept loop off for daemon.accept_error_backoff_ms. |
| `agent_scan_kept` | counter | lookups | result | Kept-walk lookups of the agent scan (silent-agent-nudge and the agent gates): hit (the walk resumed from where the last scan stopped) or miss. |
| `agent_scan_kept_miss` | counter | lookups | reason | Why a kept-walk lookup missed and the window was walked afresh: none (nothing kept: first scan, daemon restart, eviction or idle expiry), gen (defaults changed), file (other file or shrunk), window (kept walk older than the slid window allows), rel_min or straddles (an event or call left the window), digest (head or back of the file changed), straddles_after (appended lines judged a call outside the window), error (an older line raised). |
| `answers_dropped` | counter | answers | event, kind, reason | Check answers a request did not get, by the event, whether it was a guard event's (kind guard) or an optional one's (kind optional) and the reason (shed, client_gone, hard_deadline, cpu_budget, check_deferred). The check's failure policy decided in their place. Lifetime; status answers_dropped.this_daemon has the count since the daemon started. |
| `budget_soft` | counter | requests |  | Requests that used more thread CPU than the SOFT budget (daemon.eval_soft_us); only warned about, every check kept its answer. |
| `budget_trips` | counter | evaluations |  | Evaluations cut off by the per-request CPU budget. |
| `bus_dropped` | gauge | notifications |  | Pub/sub notifications a full subscriber queue could not take since the daemon started (the data stays in SQLite). |
| `bus_published` | gauge | notifications |  | Pub/sub notifications delivered to subscriber queues since the daemon started. |
| `busy_replies` | counter | requests |  | Requests answered BUSY (queue full or rate limited), which made the client fall back. |
| `check_bytes_read` | counter | bytes | check, size | Transcript bytes a built-in check read (tail windows and walks it opened), by check and transcript size class; divide by check_calls for the mean per run. |
| `check_calls` | counter | runs | check | Built-in check runs, by check. |
| `check_cpu_us` | counter | us | check | CPU time (microseconds, the worker thread's own) spent inside each built-in check, by check: the sum over its calls. Divide by `check_calls` for the mean; wall time is `check_latency_us`. |
| `check_decisions` | counter | runs | check, decision | Built-in check outcomes, by check and decision (allow, block, advisory, defer). |
| `check_latency_by_size_us` | histogram | us | check, size | Wall time of a built-in check run, by check and by the size class of the transcript the request named (load.size_labels). |
| `check_latency_us` | histogram | us | check | Wall time of a built-in check run, by check. |
| `check_mem_alloc_bytes` | histogram | bytes | check | The bytes one call of a built-in check (and its script) allocated in total, freed or not, by check: a histogram whose max is the check's worst call (`diagnostics.check_mem`). |
| `check_mem_peak_bytes` | histogram | bytes | check | The most one call of a built-in check (and its script) grew the heap above where the call started, in bytes, by check: a histogram whose max is the check's worst call. Counted from per-thread counters in the allocator (`diagnostics.check_mem`). |
| `check_mem_retained_bytes` | counter | bytes | check | The bytes a check's calls kept allocated when they returned (allocated minus freed, positive only), by check: the sum over its calls. A check that keeps growing here holds on to memory. Calls that freed more than they allocated add nothing. |
| `client_gone_skipped` | counter | checks |  | Checks not run because the request's client had already closed its connection (daemon.skip_when_client_gone). |
| `db_archive_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Size of archive.db (0 until it is first used). |
| `db_archive_wal_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Size of archive.db's write-ahead log. |
| `db_commits` | gauge | commits |  | hot.db transactions the writer committed since the daemon started; fewer than db_writes means group commit is sharing syncs. |
| `db_hot_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Size of hot.db. |
| `db_hot_wal_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Size of hot.db's write-ahead log. |
| `db_writes` | gauge | writes |  | Writes carried by those transactions since the daemon started. |
| `deadline_soft` | counter | requests |  | Requests answered after the client's fail-fast wait (client.deadline_ms) but inside the hard deadline; only warned about. |
| `dispatch_checks` | counter | entries | event, check, answer | Built-in check entries the dispatcher sent to the daemon, by event, check and answer (decided, or defer = its Node hook ran instead) (D58). |
| `dispatch_entries` | counter | entries | event, entry, outcome, cfg | What the dispatcher's plan did to each table entry of an event it asked the daemon about (D87): ran, skipped_predicate, skipped_max_rules, skipped_budget, shadowed or off, by event, entry, outcome and the hash of the non-default hook configuration the plan was made under (`default` when none). |
| `dispatch_overhead_us` | histogram | us | event | Wall time of a dispatched hook request that no built-in check accounts for (request wall minus the sum of the checks), by hook event: parsing, plan, locks, waits and queueing inside the daemon. |
| `errors` | counter | requests |  | Requests answered ERR. |
| `event_check_cpu_us` | counter | us | event | CPU time (microseconds, the worker thread's own) spent inside built-in checks while serving each hook event: the sum over every check call of that event (`status --json` `cpu.by_event`). |
| `evidence_cache` | counter | lookups | result | Transcript evidence lookups (claim-ledger and other `ah.transcript.evidence` callers): hit (nothing appended), extend (only the appended bytes were read) or rebuild (the window was read afresh). |
| `evidence_cache_rebuild` | counter | lookups | reason | Why a transcript evidence lookup read its window afresh: none (nothing kept: first call, daemon restart, eviction or idle expiry), file (another file or a shorter one), window (the window moved past the kept lines) or digest (the file was rewritten in place). |
| `evidence_walk` | counter | walks | result | Evidence walks (the claim ledger's `ah.transcript.evidenceWalk`) the memory registry refused to keep, so the check deferred. |
| `fail_open` | counter | events | reason, check | Engine-level fail-opens by reason and check: the request was answered without the check's verdict (missing_key, deadline_cut, script_timeout, jev_breaker_open, busy, internal_error, undelivered_verdict). |
| `hook_calls` | counter | requests | event | Hook requests served, by hook event. |
| `hook_latency_us` | histogram | us | event | Wall time to serve a hook request inside the daemon, by hook event. |
| `hook_phase_us` | histogram | us | event, phase | Where the time of a hook call goes, by hook event and phase: the client's connect, request-to-ACK, ACK-to-response; the daemon's queue wait, judging and delivery (reply written to ACK(res)); the launcher's startup. |
| `inject_emitted` | counter | blocks | cut | Gated hook blocks passed on whole, by cut (injection gate). |
| `inject_emitted_bytes` | counter | bytes | cut | Bytes of the gated hook blocks that were injected (whole blocks, and the short keepalive forms), by cut. |
| `inject_gate_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Estimated memory of the injection gate state. |
| `inject_gate_evictions` | gauge | items |  | Sessions or blocks the gate dropped to stay within its bounds since the daemon started. |
| `inject_gate_sessions` | gauge | sessions |  | Sessions the injection gate holds state for (bounded by inject_gate.max_sessions). |
| `inject_gate_slots` | gauge | blocks |  | Gated blocks remembered across all sessions. |
| `inject_keepalive` | counter | blocks | cut | Unchanged gated blocks passed on again because their keepalive turn came, by cut. |
| `inject_suppressed` | counter | blocks | cut | Gated hook blocks the model already held and the gate dropped, by cut. |
| `inject_suppressed_bytes` | counter | bytes | cut | Bytes the gate kept out of the context (the dropped blocks, and what a keepalive form saved over the whole block), by cut. |
| `launcher_counter` | counter | events | name | Counters the launcher reports with each call (soft and hard limit hits, retries, fallbacks, ...), summed by name. |
| `maintain_last_ms` | gauge | ms |  | When the last maintenance run happened, in ms since the epoch (0: never). |
| `maintain_runs` | gauge | runs |  | Maintenance runs recorded in hot.db (D26). |
| `memory_leak_notices` | counter | notices | top | Memory-registry leak notices, by largest holder. |
| `panics` | counter | panics |  | Request-handler panics that were contained. |
| `procwatch_events` | counter | events | kind, class | Process-watch findings, by kind (orphan_candidate, orphan_kill, resource_warning, disk_warning) and class or reason. |
| `queue_depth` | gauge | connections |  | Connections waiting for a worker when status or metrics is read. |
| `rejected_peers` | counter | connections |  | Connections dropped because the peer uid was not ours. |
| `requests` | counter | requests |  | Requests the daemon handled, any type. |
| `rss_kb` | gauge | KB |  | Resident set of the daemon, sampled when status or metrics is read. |
| `rule_hits` | counter | matches | action | Regex rule matches, by action (deny, warn, context). |
| `schedule_cpu_us` | counter | us | job | CPU time (microseconds) the threads that ran a scheduled job used, by job; a subprocess job's own CPU is not in it. Divide by schedule_runs for the mean per run. |
| `schedule_missed` | counter | runs | job | Runs that caught up a missed window or skipped it, by job (D33). |
| `schedule_runs` | counter | runs | job, status | Scheduled runs that finished, by job and status (ok, failed, timeout, planned, skipped) (D33). |
| `script_soft` | counter | calls |  | Script calls that used more thread CPU than their SOFT limit (script.time_limit_ms); only warned about, the call was not cut. |
| `slow_replies` | counter | replies |  | Replies finished after their client's deadline had passed: slow but healthy (the client fell back to Node), counted apart from errors. |
| `spool_applied` | counter | writes |  | Spooled writes the daemon applied (D24). |
| `spool_quarantined` | counter | records |  | Spool records moved to quarantine: damaged, or refused for good by the store (D24). |
| `tasks_cache` | counter | lookups | result | Task-line lookups of `ah.transcript.tasks` (task-guard, tasklist-guard, task-tracker): hit (nothing appended), extend (only the appended bytes were read) or rebuild (the window was read afresh). |
| `tasks_cache_rebuild` | counter | lookups | reason | Why a task-line lookup read its window afresh: none (nothing kept: first call, daemon restart, eviction or idle expiry), file (another file or a shorter one), window (the window moved past the kept lines) or digest (the file was rewritten in place). |
| `tel_dropped` | counter | samples | reason | Telemetry samples or events that could not be kept: slots (a counter table was full) or ring (an event was overwritten before it was flushed). |
| `tel_events` | counter | invocations | k, h, e, o | Telemetry invocations recorded, by kind (k), hook or check (h), hook event (e) and outcome (o) (D78). |
| `tel_injected_bytes` | counter | bytes | h, e | Bytes injected into model context, by hook or check (h) and hook event (e). The whole-hook rows (h=hook) add up to the total; a per-check row is attribution inside it (D78). |
| `tier_bytes` | gauge | bytes |  | Bytes charged to the in-memory layer's budget (D25). |
| `tier_evictions` | gauge | items |  | Items dropped from memory to stay within the budget since the daemon started (SQLite keeps them). |
| `tier_expired` | gauge | items |  | Items dropped from memory because their TTL ended since the daemon started (SQLite keeps them). |
| `tier_hits` | gauge | reads |  | Key-value reads answered from memory since the daemon started. |
| `tier_items` | gauge | items |  | Active key-value items held in memory (D22). |
| `tier_misses` | gauge | reads |  | Key-value reads that went to SQLite since the daemon started. |
| `uptime_s` | gauge | s |  | Seconds since the daemon started. |
| `wire_events` | counter | events | kind | Ack protocol events by kind: acked, delivered, ack_timeout, retry, abandoned. |
| `jev_asked_sync` | counter | calls | id | Stop/SubagentStop asks the gate let wait for Jev (the rule layer had flagged a likely unverified claim), by integration. |
| `jev_calls` | counter | calls | backend, mode | Jev decisions asked for, by backend (jev, cache or baseline-only) and mode. |
| `jev_changed` | counter | decisions |  | Decisions in on mode where Jev changed the outcome (always an added block or advisory). |
| `jev_cooldowns` | counter | calls |  | Jev calls skipped because a vendor's circuit breaker was open. |
| `jev_cost_micro_usd` | counter | micro-usd |  | Cost of fresh Jev calls in millionths of a US dollar, as reported by the vendor or priced from the reported tokens; a cache hit adds nothing. Never an estimate of what a judge call would have cost. |
| `jev_gate_timeouts` | counter | calls | id | Flagged Stop/SubagentStop asks whose wait for Jev ran out (the check failed open on its baseline), by integration. |
| `jev_latency_us` | histogram | us |  | Latency of fresh Jev network calls. |
| `jev_skipped_unflagged` | counter | calls | id | Stop/SubagentStop asks the gate skipped because the rule layer flagged nothing: no synchronous Jev call, the check kept its baseline. By integration. |
| `jev_slow` | counter | calls |  | Jev calls slower than the SOFT limit (jev.soft_ms); their answers were still used. |
| `jev_timeouts` | counter | calls |  | Jev calls that ran out of their time budget. |
| `jev_verdicts` | counter | decisions | id, verdict | What each Jev decision did, by integration and verdict: added or changed (an on-mode outcome moved), would-change (a shadow call that would have moved it), none (Jev agreed with the baseline) or no-answer (it failed or was skipped). |
| `jev_arrival` | counter | events | outcome | Jev arrival labelling, by outcome: what became of a queued message or of a worker run (see jev_arrival.outcomes). |
| `mesh_descriptor_read_skipped` | counter | reads | site, reason | Reads of a file named by a descriptor that were skipped because it is no regular file (a FIFO, socket or device) or is over the read cap, by site and reason. |
| `mesh_own_sends_excluded` | counter | counts |  | Counts that left out unread rows the recipient's own identity family sent (an own send is not inbound mail). |
| `mesh_pull_ts_fallback` | counter | batches |  | Pulled batches holding a message whose time is a form Date.parse accepts but the engine does not reproduce: its store row carries the import time instead (the message and its hash are intact). |
| `mesh_ref_resolved` | counter | references | outcome | How a workspace reference given to a verb (send --to, archive, nudge, gate, ...) resolved, by outcome: exact, mesh, prefix, ambiguous, none. |
| `mesh_sender_fallback` | counter | messages | where | Messages whose sender came from a fallback instead of the message's own branch, by where: ingest (a child's queue: the Primary), read (the NDJSON line's own sender, or the Primary for a NULL store row). |
| `mesh_summary_owner_fallback` | counter | rows |  | Roster/summary rows counted from the shared floor because the workspace's partition has no live reader row (the base is the least-advanced live reader otherwise). |
| `mesh_watcher_matched_by_checkout` | counter | checks |  | Watcher-live checks answered by another row's lock on the same checkout because the workspace's own id had no live lock. |
| `mesh_heartbeat_degraded` | counter | steps | site, reason | Heartbeat steps that failed and were read as Node's fail-open reads them, by step and reason. |
| `mesh_report_skipped` | counter | inputs | why | Supervision-report inputs skipped (an unread timestamp, a malformed rollup file), by reason. |
| `mesh_store_backend_skipped` | counter | stores | site, backend | Partition stores the engine did not read because they are held in the journal backend, by site and backend. |
| `mesh_summary_read_failed` | counter | reads | site | Store reads of the summary projection that failed and read as empty (Node's fail-open), by site. |
| `mesh_summary_settings_unreadable` | counter | reads | key | Summary settings read while the settings file was one the engine cannot parse but JavaScript can, by key. |
| `rt_edges` | counter | edges |  | Workspace state changes emitted. |
| `rt_reconcile_repairs` | counter | edges |  | Changes a full reconcile found that the event path had not already applied: the health measure of the realtime event layer (close to 0 is healthy). |
| `rt_shadow_mismatches` | counter | mismatches |  | Differences between the engine's workspace state and the Node witness's. |
| `dsx_actions` | counter | actions | feature, outcome | Automatic archive and nag attempts of the DevSwarm expansion features, by feature and outcome (ok, refused, failed). |
| `dsx_auto_archive_mistake_rate` | gauge | ratio |  | Mistake signals per successful auto-archive since the engine started (gauge). |
| `dsx_auto_archive_success_rate` | gauge | ratio |  | ok / (ok + failed) of auto-archive attempts since the engine started (gauge, 0..1); a refusal is a safety check working and is not counted. |
| `dsx_latency_us` | histogram | us | feature | Wall time of one automatic archive or nag attempt, by feature. |
| `dsx_mistakes` | counter | signals | feature, signal | Mistake signals recorded after an automatic action, by feature and signal (unarchived, activity-after-archive, nag-ignored). |
| `dsx_nag_mistake_rate` | gauge | ratio |  | Mistake signals per delivered nag since the engine started (gauge). |
| `dsx_nag_success_rate` | gauge | ratio |  | ok / (ok + failed) of nag attempts since the engine started (gauge, 0..1). |
| `dswire_actions` | counter | actions | kind, outcome | DevSwarm actions the engine ran or declined from a state change, by kind and outcome. |
| `dswire_advisory` | counter | advisories |  | Advisories injected into a session. |
| `dswire_full_sweeps` | counter | sweeps |  | Full action sweeps (every workspace's facts read, plus the mistake scan and the nag pass) run by the DevSwarm layer. |
| `dswire_jev_coalesced` | counter | requests |  | Jev sweep requests folded into the queue because a sweep was already running. |
| `dswire_jev_dirty` | counter | marks |  | Workspaces marked dirty for a per-child Jev sweep. |
| `dswire_jev_threads` | counter | threads |  | Threads started for a per-child Jev sweep (one per sweep that found queued workspaces and no sweep running). |
| `dswire_mode_change` | counter | changes | mode | Times the DevSwarm layer's mode (devswarm_rt.mode) changed while the daemon ran, by the new mode. |
| `dswire_reconcile_cpu_us` | counter | us | cause, phase | CPU microseconds of the calling thread spent in a DevSwarm reconcile, by cause (startup, event, periodic, overflow) and phase (derive: read and diff the sources; sweep: the action sweeps that follow). |
| `dswire_reconcile_runs` | counter | runs | cause, outcome | DevSwarm reconciles by cause and outcome (noop: no state change found; changed: edges found). |
| `dswire_stall_actions` | counter | actions | kind, outcome | Pokes and escalations of silent workspaces the engine ran or refused (feature 5), by kind (poke, escalate) and outcome (ok, failed, refused); the same actions, their inputs and the mistake signals found later are in the action log (`ah-engine telemetry actions stall`). |
| `dswire_standdown` | counter | sweeps | kind | Action sweeps the engine skipped because the action's executor is not the engine. |
| `dssup_appdb_date_unread` | counter | dates |  | Dates read from the DevSwarm app database that are a form Date.parse accepts but the engine does not reproduce: that stamp counts as absent (the row is otherwise read in full). |
| `ingest_drops` | counter | paths | reason | Paths found as ingest projects that were not drained, counted when the reason is first seen or changes, by reason. |

## Impact kinds

| Kind | What it records |
|---|---|
| `advisory` | A check returned an advisory instead of a decision (for example the handover-budget notice). |
| `block` | A check or rule blocked a call. The reason is the check or rule id. |
| `context` | A context-action rule matched and injected text for the agent. |
| `disk_warning` | The disk watch warned about low free space. The reason is warn or critical. |
| `fallback` | The engine could not or would not answer (a check deferred, or the request failed) and the client ran the Node hook instead. |
| `orphan_candidate` | The process watch found a process left behind by an ended Claude session. The reason is its class. |
| `orphan_kill` | The process watch stopped an orphan whose class is in kill mode. The reason is its class. |
| `resource_warning` | The resource watch warned about a process or the system. The reason is cpu, memory, swap or pressure. |
| `route` | A model-routing decision at agent spawn (D78/D86). Route events carry requested_model, parent_model, task_class, recommended_tier, selected_model, outcome and spawn_key; legacy route rows without selected_model are read with a deterministic fallback. A forced cheaper-model delegation also records a delegate event with spawn_key, requested_model, selected_model and task_class, never prompt or description text. |
| `warning` | A warn-action rule matched and added a warning for the agent. |

## Error codes

Environment-class codes get a plain self-fix hint; any other code is a permanent failure that asks for an issue.

| Codes | Class | Self-fix hint |
|---|---|---|
| `os28` | env | the disk is full (no space left); free some space, then it recovers by itself |
| `os13`, `os1`, `unsafe_dir` | env | ah-engine's state directory is not writable or not private; fix its ownership (chown to yourself) and permissions (chmod 700 ~/.anti-hall/ah-engine), or set AH_ENGINE_DIR to a directory you own |
| `os36`, `os22`, `path_too_long` | env | the socket path is too long; set AH_ENGINE_DIR to a shorter path (e.g. /tmp/ah) |
| `os24`, `os23` | env | the process ran out of file descriptors; raise `ulimit -n` or close other programs |
| `os12`, `sig9` | env | the OS killed or starved ah-engine (low memory); close other programs or lower AH_ENGINE_MEM_MB |
